subject: Compositor: Anisotropic Kuwahara speedup
message:
Compositor: Anisotropic Kuwahara speedup

Speed up Anisotropic Kuwahara by:
- CPU: 25-30%
- NVIDIA GPU: 2X
- Apple GPU: 10X (yes ten times faster)

Details on how:
- GPU: unroll sector loops. This helps massively, 2x on nvidia, 10x
  on apple.
- CPU: do not use double precision exp() for sector weights.
  Well, while at it, use a polynomial approximation for the exp()
  input range we use.
- Reduce number of sector weight accumulators: they are symmetric
  so we can use 4 instead of 8.
- Simplify the logic how the first row pixels are skipped (we
  can just start y=0 row at x=1 instead of having a check in the
  inner loop).
- CPU: skip zero weight sectors while accumulating.

More performance details in the PR.

subject: 3D Texture Paint: Implement Mask brush
message:
3D Texture Paint: Implement Mask brush

The masking brush allows users to paint a mask onto a mesh using an
image texture. In the full implementation, the mask will limit the
effects of other Texture Paint brushes, making it possible to protect
existing texture work from being painted over. This makes it much safer
to perform tweaks to textures. This addition is a step towards feature
parity with the legacy Texture Paint.

Note that with this PR, the painted mask texture doesn't affect the
3D Draw brush. This PR only allows users to paint on a mask texture.
Restricting the new 3D brushes will come in a future PR.

Currently, the masking brush code is almost identical to the texturing
brush, the difference being that the brush colors are restricted to
greyscale. The brush will be refactored in a future PR to be more
efficient since it's essentially working with greyscale information
that only requires one channel, not 4 like the current implementation.

This new masking brush is experimental, so the `3D Texture Paint`
option in the Blender preferences needs to be enabled to use it.

subject: VSE: Ripple Editing
message:
VSE: Ripple Editing

Design Task: #153963

This PR adds a full ripple editing framework to the video sequencer,
building on the ripple delete operator added in !160607.

The overall idea is that the "overlap mode" becomes a "default" method
of resolving overlap in all cases, however, you can override this with
the dedicated ripple operators like ripple delete, trim, and so on.
- This means that we no longer hardcode the "shuffle" overlap mode for
  many operators, and instead choose whatever the user has set
  currently.
- Notably, Expand overlap mode has been renamed to Ripple.

Behavior for these ripple operators and the ripple overlap mode can be
adjusted via options from a newly added popover.
Options are grouped into three categories:
- Edit: apply to all ripples
- Add: only applies to cases where strips are newly created or push
  others out of the way
- Delete: only applies to ripple delete
These options "seed" the initial properties of ripple operators like
ripple delete, ripple trim, or sequence slide, and for further
customization, you can temporarily override them in the redo panels.

They can also be adjusted in real time during strip movement with a
modal keymap (as seen in the status bar), where keys `R`, `V`, and `S`
set ripple/overwrite/shuffle respectively.

This commit also implements the second suggestion in #125054, to quickly
trim strips based on the playhead location. These are bound to `Shift+Q`
and `Shift+W` by default, and use all the same helper functions for
ripple logic.

Ripple Delete was also redesigned with a new Clear Ranges option. This
clears all strips in the frame region marked by ripple deleted strips,
before rippling later strips back.
  - If `All Channels` is on, this deletes strips along all channels
    along that range, else only strips on the same channels as one of
    the deleted strips.
  - This option guarantees that the full region is rippled at the cost
    of being destructive sometimes.
Turning off Clear Ranges will find all gaps in the frame region marked
by ripple-deleted strips, and only ripple strips back that far, without
editing any other strip
  - This option avoids overwriting/changing other strips, but may be
    clamped and thus not ripple the full amount in some cases.

More example videos in the PR.

subject: Refactor: Mesh: Simplify edit mesh snap filtering
message:
Refactor: Mesh: Simplify edit mesh snap filtering

Currently the snapping system converts BMesh to Mesh for snapping, then
does some filtering of the Mesh before building the necessary BVH trees.
That's generally a good design that avoids a bunch of duplicate code,
but the filtering step is a bit complex. A few global callbacks are
stored that filter the Mesh data based on the equivalent indices in the
BMesh, and those callbacks change the visibility attributes on the mesh,
which indirectly control the created BVH tree. It's clearer to just
calculate an IndexMask of desired snapping elements and create the BVH
tree from that. That should be more efficient anyway, and fits much
better with a future where edit mode doesn't imply that a BMesh is
available (see #163678).

Fix: Vulkan: Incorrect attachment count for local read shaders libraries

Fixes VUID-VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo-renderPass-09531 reported by
validation layers when using VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read with
graphics pipeline libraries.

The shaders library set VkRenderingInputAttachmentIndexInfo::colorAttachmentCount

`max input attachment index + 1` of the shader. The spec requires this to be the
render pass color attachment count.

it for both counts. This keeps the library shareable between framebuffers with
the same attachment count while matching the fragment output library.

subject: GPU: Shader Tool: Compile time check of conditional resource access
message:
GPU: Shader Tool: Compile time check of conditional resource access

## GPU: Shader Tool: Allow usage of enum values in resource conditions

More globaly, all constexpr are emited as their values.
This means the create infos do not need to be aware of
the symbol declarations.

## GPU: Shader Tool: Compile time check of conditional resource access

With this PR, every access to a resource
declared with `condition` attribute checks
if the condition is actually checked.

For the test to pass, the condition must
be checked in a static branch if condition
statement before the accessor statement.

We keep a stack of active conditions when
inside static if branches.

The conditions are split into sub expression
based on their logical operators.
Then, the needed conditional sub expression
are all searched inside the active conditions
stack. If one subexpression remains, the
condition is not met and an error is raised.

The checking of these condition is a NP-complete
problem and would require a proper SAT solver.
Since this is overkill for us, this is a simpler
substitute.

See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boolean_satisfiability_problem

## Fix: GPU: Comply to new compiler restrictions

- Use same text for conditions matching
- Add missing condition check
- Remove bogus conditions

Fix: Alembic: crash when exporting an attribute which changes types

Exporting an attribute which changes type during animation crashes the

already have an attribute of that name. Then, when writing empty
samples for the missing frames for this new attribute, we crash on
uninitialized data.

To fix this, verify that the type of the (potentially new) attribute
matches what we exported so far for the attribute of that name.

subject: Fix: Cycles: Alpha upscaling with DLSS
message:
Fix: Cycles: Alpha upscaling with DLSS

Flickering could be observed at the edges of scenes with a transparent
background. This was caused by the alpha channel being copied as-is
from the input to the output, which does not produce accurate results
with pixel jittering and upscaling active. Both the OptiX denoiser and
DLSS support alpha upscaling to solve this.
This requires making alpha available to the denoisers. The primary
change here is therefore in `DenoiserGPU::denoise_color_read`, to
enable it to copy alpha into the denoiser input too. The film convert
kernel already transforms transparency to alpha and applies scaling as
part of that, so the post-process kernels had to be adjusted to reverse
that again.

subject: Fix #163419: Avoid invalid aligned Fillet Curve handles
message:
Fix #163419: Avoid invalid aligned Fillet Curve handles

Fillet Curve creates the inner Bezier handles from the original
corner direction to approximate a circular arc.

When neighboring fillets overlap, or nearly coincide after radius
limiting, the paired outer vector handle can point in a different
direction. Recalculating an aligned handle then changes the intended
arc.

Keep the handle aligned when recalculation preserves the constructed
arc, and use a free handle otherwise.

This keeps the previous fix for #162043 in place for exactly
coincident handles.

subject: Fix #161827: Audio mixdown from scripts produces bad output
message:
Fix #161827: Audio mixdown from scripts produces bad output

Caused by f02819b292.

In background mode, the script (and therefor blender) finishes before
the worker thread finishes, killing all running jobs.
Similarly, when called multiple times from a script, a second execution
would kill previous jobs, ruining the output.

To resolve, just execute the relevant code synchronously when the
operator is just executed, and only use a background job when invoked.
This is in line with what quadriflow remesh & and uv pack are doing.
Alembic & USD use a similar (but less straightforward) approach, the
former has an RNA operator property for this while the later allocates
some data in invoke to signal the exec that it has been invoked prior...

So we keep a progressbar when invoked from the UI, otherwise it runs
blocking on the main thread.

NOTE: even from the UI it is still possible to launch mixdown mutiple times
with the same consequence: following calls kill preceeding jobs. This PR
just makes usage in scripts more predicable.

subject: Fix #162997: Cycles viewport stutters when cursor wrapping occurs
message:
Fix #162997: Cycles viewport stutters when cursor wrapping occurs

When cursor wrapping occurs, an immediate redraw is forced even though
there was no effective view change. This means the session is not reset
during the Cycles synchronize (since there was no actual camera change
yet), but it still draws again. Since the current texture is still
aligned at this point, waiting on the next full render update now only
introduces stutter. The solution is therefore to only synchronize main
and rendering thread after a reset (e.g. due to camera update while
navigating).

subject: Subdiv: Simplify/remove converter and MeshTopology abstractions
message:
Subdiv: Simplify/remove converter and MeshTopology abstractions

Continuation of changes from #130917.

The "converter" as it exists now basically takes a mesh represented by
plain data arrays and presents it to our OpenSubdiv library wrapper in
the form of a callback per mesh element. A previous refactor replaced
the face callback with a plain array of the face offsets- the same
representation used directly by meshes. This PR follows that lead and
replaces the callbacks for face vertex indices, edges, and sharpness
values with plain arrays in the converter.

This change makes the actual data manipulation much clearer, avoids
function call overhead, and opens the door to avoiding these data
array copies completely in the future. The code is so much simpler that
over over 700 lines of "abstraction" are removed, and the ways we could
avoid copying are very nearly obvious.

subject: Fix: Geometry Nodes: `Duplicate Hair Curves` Outputting Duplicate IDs
message:
Fix: Geometry Nodes: `Duplicate Hair Curves` Outputting Duplicate IDs

The current implementation of `Duplicate Hair Curves` asset
has two problems regarding how it handles IDs:

1. The IDs are rehashed even for the original curves. This causes
visible changes in randomization, even if 0 duplicates are made.

2. The hashing uses `Duplicate Index` as the seed. This causes ID
collisions with the original curves *(where that field is 0)* and the
first duplicate *(which has duplicate index 0)*.

This patch updates the asset to retain the IDs of the original curves
and only hash new ID values for the duplicate hair curves.

subject: GPU: Include Vulkan pipeline compilation in shader compilation status
message:
GPU: Include Vulkan pipeline compilation in shader compilation status

Previously `bpy.app.is_job_running("SHADER_COMPILATION")` only reflected
the async shader compiler, so on-demand Vulkan pipeline creation during
drawing was not reported and could affect EEVEE performance tests.

The pipeline pool now counts pipelines compiled on demand and exposes
whether any were compiled since the last per-frame reset. The status
query reports this alongside the async shader compiler. The per-frame
reset is driven by a `frame_change_post` callback registered after
Python starts, so it runs after the frame change handlers and a poll
reflects the pipelines compiled during the previous frame.

subject: Fix #163292: GreasePencil Lasso/Box Delete crash in Multiframe mode
message:
Fix #163292: GreasePencil Lasso/Box Delete crash in Multiframe mode

The birds-eye situation is as follows:
- code collected `points_to_remove_per_drawing` (all good with that)
- `remove_points_and_split_from_drawings` was then possibly acting on a
non-correspondent drawing with the "wrong" mask
- that lead to the crash with different point counts

Details:
`retrieve_editable_drawings` already does a good job at collecting (it
takes multiframe-editing into account, knows which frame to consider if
there is no keyframe on the current frame, etc.).
What it does not do is create new keyframes for auto-key. That was in
turn implemented in `remove_points_and_split_from_drawings` but with
"own" behavior of adding keyframes (was trying to add keyframes for all
layers and for all collected drawings). It was also getting a drawing at
the **current frame**which can be wrong when multiframe-editing is at
play.

To derail a little bit: I found behavior of autokey to be inconsistent/
confusing throughout (this can be tackled separately, but this also
bleeds into the reasoning for the fix, so bear with me):
- editmode and sculptmode seems to always key all layers (even if no
edits took place)
- drawmode operations seem to prefer to only key the active layer only
(but then again, fill doesnt...)
- selection of new keyframes happens for drawing but not for other
operations
- there are two possible behaviors of autokey: duplicate a frame or
insert a new frame
  - there are tools where current behavior does not make sense (the fill
tool creating blank frames before trying to fill them?)

Solution:
Create the needed keyframe up front (before
`retrieve_editable_drawings`), in the active layer only (this was
confirmed in chat as expected behavior) and select it (deselect others).
Remove the keyframing part of `remove_points_and_split_from_drawings`.
Also act directly on the drawings collected by
`retrieve_editable_drawings` without referring to the current scene
frame again.

subject: Build: Tweak path to the system Python
message:
Build: Tweak path to the system Python

The buildbot rules are enabling special tests that ensure some of our
scripts work on the default system-wide Python. This was especially
important for Rocky, which uses Python 3.6 by default and it is quite
old release.

There is a check in the code that disables system python tests when
the system Python path does not exist. A confusing consequence of this
is that the number of CTest suits that is run depends on the OS that
is used on the worker. For example, Rocky and Ubuntu workers will have
different number of tests run for the same CMake options.

This change makes it so that if /usr/bin/python3.6 does not exist
/usr/bin/python3 is used instead, making the number of run tests match
for Ubuntu and Rocky.

subject: Python API: Add optional name parameter to constraints.new()
message:
Python API: Add optional name parameter to constraints.new()

`PoseBone.constraints.new()` and `Object.constraints.new()` now accept
an optional `name` parameter:

  pose_bone.constraints.new('COPY_LOCATION', name="Copy Location FK")

This is inconsistent with `modifiers.new(name, type)`, because that
function's signature is not well designed. It demands a modifier name
instead of leaving it optional. In this case, the name MUST be
optional for backward compatibility.

This is not a change for mere convenience (or mere common sense).
Setting `Constraint.name` is expensive: It calls
`BKE_animdata_fix_paths_rename_all(...)`, which goes through the
animation data of every ID in the file. This is a performance
bottleneck for rig generation scripts, particularly CloudRig. Rigify
never gives constraints unique names, so isn't affected.

This change allows such scripts to dodge the expensive rename, by
initializing with the desired name instead, resulting in a significant
rig generation performance boost (see the PR for numbers).

subject: Fix #163757: Image Undo can sometimes restore incorrect tiles
message:
Fix #163757: Image Undo can sometimes restore incorrect tiles

The idea is assign a unique changeset ID per ImBuf. That is also renewed
whenever on full buffer updates on an ImBuf, for example on resize.

Undo steps copy the changeset ID on push, and can then only be restored
on ImBufs with a matching changeset ID. The changeset ID is also copied
from the undo step back to the ImBuf on full update,
so that subsequent partial updates apply.

This mechanism is used so that alternating memfile and image undo steps
both work correctly, and don't need a full image copy whenever a memfile
undo step is added between image undo steps. This is important for
memory usage when painting high resolution images while editing
materials or other scene data.

subject: Cycles: Optimize integrator state allocations on integrated CUDA GPUs
message:
Cycles: Optimize integrator state allocations on integrated CUDA GPUs

The integrator state currently has to be copied from device to host
around kernel launches for scheduling decisions. Various other
allocations made under the `MEM_READ_WRITE` type also have to be
duplicated/copied for use. This makes sense for dedicated GPUs where
access to host memory is slow. However, on integrated GPUs where the
physical memory is shared, the story is slightly different. There that
memory can be allocated only once and directly accessed by both the CPU
and GPU, avoiding the need for the copy operations between kernels.
Unfortunately the details are a bit complicated on Windows right now,
so for optimal performance the allocation goes through a bit of an
obscure VirtualAlloc2+cuMemHostRegister path.

subject: Geometry Nodes: Index of Nearest: Use grouped indices instead of masks
message:
Geometry Nodes: Index of Nearest: Use grouped indices instead of masks

The elements of each group were collected into an IndexMask per group, built
by appending every index to a per-group vector on a single thread. The group
indices are already compact, so group the elements with a parallel counting
sort into one flat array instead, and build the KD trees from those indices
directly. This also avoids the overhead of an IndexMask for every group, which
matters when there are many small groups.

Scene evaluation time with 2 million random points (minimum of 3x6 runs):
| Group ID                            | Before   | After    |
| ----------------------------------- | -------- | -------- |
| index / 4                           | 38.6 ms  | 10.6 ms  |
| index / 4, 2/3 of points evaluated  | 92.7 ms  | 14.0 ms  |

subject: Mesh: Flatten data on GPU instead of CPU
message:
Mesh: Flatten data on GPU instead of CPU

Mesh data referenced by shaders on the GPU needs to be stored per-
corner. For positions, vertex and face normals, and attributes, this
means much more data to the GPU than necessary. Instead, this PR uploads
mesh topology arrays to the GPU and uses simple shaders to propagate the
data from vertices, edges, and faces to face corners.

In typical scenarios the cost is increased GPU memory usage: four extra
bytes per face corner, but in return we transfer 4 times less data for
changing positions and normals. In a simple test render on my laptop
with a 9 million face corner mesh, frame times decreased by almost 1.9x.

Beyond the immediate performance benefits, this approach will work
well with improved caching in the future. For example, if topology stays
the same but positions changed, the topology GPU buffer won't have to be
re-uploaded, further improving performance. It's also good that GPU
buffers directly correspond to attribute arrays; that will work well
with potential GPU attribute storage.

message:
BLI: Add utility to find compact indices for group IDs

Many places convert arbitrary integer IDs to compact group indices by adding
them to a VectorSet on a single thread and then looking up every ID's index.
Add array_utils::group_ids_to_indices() that gives the same result, but uses a
lookup table filled in parallel when the IDs are within a limited range.

Use it for the Merge Points node (for meshes and point clouds), and the
Points to Curves, Cluster by Distance, and Index of Nearest nodes.

Also use it in IndexMask::from_group_ids(), where we also use a utility
for grouping instead of appending to many groups. That indirectly affects
the Split to Instances, Sample Nearest Surface, Geometry Proximity, and
Fill Curve nodes.

This is mainly targeted at the Merge Points node, where this part of the
work gets significantly faster:

| Scene                    | Before  | After  |
| ------------------------ | ------- | ------ |
| ngon_split (2.4M verts)  | 95.1 ms | 8.5 ms |
| quads_to_tris (2.2M)     | 33.1 ms | 6.9 ms |

| weld_split (2.5M)        | 12.8 ms | 4.1 ms |

| sparse (4M, 0.2% merged) | 3.5 ms  | 1.5 ms |

subject: Color Management: Revert Rec.709 video default change, add optional role
message:
Color Management: Revert Rec.709 video default change, add optional role

Interpreting Rec.709 video as BT.1886 is too big a break changing, and
there is not enough time to address it for the 5.3 release, if it can
be addressed at all.

Some issues:
* Cutting a Rec.709 video would change the colors as there is no more
  paired sRGB input and output.
* Tagging sRGB CICP for video output does not work well for all cases,
  for example YouTube will give different results.
* Many Rec.709 videos are meant to be interpreted as sRGB or (Gamma
  1.961 on Apple), for example screen recordings.

This effectively restores the previous behavior before 163710, but for
advanced users there is now an OpenColorIO configuration role named
"video_rec709" that controls the interpretation of such video files for
input and output.

It can be set to Rec.1886 (or equivalent color spaces in another config)
to match the Color Interop Forum intepretation. If unset it defaults to
sRGB.

One difference is that both images and video now interpret 1/1 as being
sRGB on read (or the video_rec709 role if specified).

Color Management: Per-project OpenColorIO configuration

Previously, a custom OpenColorIO configuration could only be configured
through the `BLENDER_OCIO` and `OCIO` environment variables, which is a
poor UX because Blender is rarely launched from a shell, and it is not
straightforward to configure a project to persist a specific value of

is written as `ocio_config` in `project.toml`.

Resolution order, highest precedence first:

1. `BLENDER_OCIO` env
2. `OCIO` env
3. Project config
4. Blender bundled config
5. Fallback config

The OpenColorIO config is reloaded whenever a blend file is opened.
There is currently no automatic reload, only a message indicating the
need for it. This can be improved, but would complicate the initial

subject: EEVEE: Allow reference spheres to scale down with camera zoom
message:
EEVEE: Allow reference spheres to scale down with camera zoom

### Summary
Fix #164365: Reference spheres take up entire camera space when zoomed
out.

### Cause
In `LookdevModule::calc_viewport_scale()`, `viewport_scale` had a rigid
minimum clamp of `0.5f`. When zooming out in camera view where
`visible_rect_` tracks the camera boundary, the reference spheres could
not scale below `0.5f`. As a result, the spheres occluded the scene
center and extended outside the camera bounds.

### Solution
- Lower the minimum viewport scale clamp from `0.5f` to `0.25f` in `LookdevModule::calc_viewport_scale()` so the reference spheres scale
down gracefully when zooming out in camera view.
- Guard the extent calculation in `calc_sphere_extent()` with
`max_ii(..., 4)` to ensure safe minimum texture dimensions.

This reworks `make showhash`, originally this command came from an era

would build the release on their own machine and upload it. Having

information is a bit lacking, it will give me the hash, but I still

subject: Fix #159219: Selectability & Visibility viewport toggles inconsistent
message:
Fix #159219: Selectability & Visibility viewport toggles inconsistent

Viewport object-type visibility & select-ability were handled
inconsistently for instances/duplis:

- `Selectability` excluded the instancer *and* its duplis.
- `Visibility` excluded only the instancer, its duplis were still drawn.

This applied to geometry-nodes instances (as reported in #159219),
object instancing & other dupli types.

The cause was the draw & select loops each
having their own object drawing checks.
Drawing only checked `BKE_object_is_visible_in_viewport`,
so the instancer was hidden while its duplis were still drawn. Selection
had more involved logic that took duplis into account (from [0]).

Resolve by sharing a single function between the draw & select
loops so they can't diverge again. Type exclusion is checked
on the instancer before the visibility/selectable checks,
returning `DrawFilter::SkipRecursive` so the exclusion applies
to its duplis too.

Duplis aren't checked against type exclusion themselves since
selecting a dupli selects its instancer (they share a `select_id`),
they still go through `BKE_object_is_visible_in_viewport` as before.

Selection now respects viewport type exclusion,
so hidden instances can't occlude or be picked.

Depth drawing (used for retopology, snapping & depth picking)
had the same divergence, while not reported, duplis of excluded
instancers were written to the depth buffer, this now uses the
shared check too.

[0]: c2c3a728b7bd9e2221e484f0452a8b1e7e8a54a6

Ref !163415

Store the source corner for every interpolation weight, so the generic
attribute_math::mix_groups function can be used instead of a mixer for
every attribute type. This reduces the binary size for the function
from 11.7 KB to 0.7 KB, and because of parallelization the mixing
can become much faster too.

Boolean attributes are now mixed with "or" instead of averaging.

subject: Refactor: Mesh: Boolean: Avoid to_static_type in corner propagation
message:
Refactor: Mesh: Boolean: Avoid to_static_type in corner propagation

Instead of mixing every attribute for each output corner inside of the
per-face loop, first compute the source corners and weights for every
interpolated corner, then use attribute_math::gather and mix_groups for
each attribute. A mask argument is added to mix_groups to make this possible.

This also makes the attribute interpolation faster, since mixing happens
in larger batches and doesn't need type dispatch per corner. With 8 corner
attributes, the time spent interpolating them went from roughly 22 ms to 8 ms
(exact solver) and from 18 ms to 6 ms (manifold solver) for two 512 segment
spheres, and from 235 ms to 95 ms for an n-gon with 4096 vertices cut by
the exact solver.

The one behavior change is that boolean attributes are now mixed with "or"
instead of averaging, but that is meant to be the behavior for propagation.

subject: Refactor: Geometry: Compare attributes one component at a time
message:
Refactor: Geometry: Compare attributes one component at a time

Instead of generating code for every attribute type for sorting and
comparing values, extract each scalar component into a float or integer
array and sort based on that. This reduces the size of the file's
compiled code from 188 KB to 50 KB.

Comparison of 4D float vectors is fixed too, previously only the first
component was compared. And sorting of 2D 16 bit integer vectors wasn't
implemented.

in parallel too. Faces are processed for splitting  afterwards on a

| quads_to_tris   | 19.5 ms | 5.9 ms |
| collapse_blocks | 16.9 ms | 5.9 ms |
| solidify_merge  | 11.1 ms | 3.6 ms |
| weld_split      | 6.9 ms  | 3.2 ms |
| cube_2500x      | 5.3 ms  | 3.6 ms |
| sparse          | 4.4 ms  | 1.5 ms |
| ngon_split      | 5.4 ms  | 8.4 ms |

In ngon_split, every face has 16 corners and is split, so most of the
work remains single threaded and is now done in a separate pass.

Mesh: Merge: Parallelize building weld faces

A face is affected by the merge when any of its vertices is, so find the
affected faces with an IndexMask, then initialize their weld faces and
corner links in parallel. The estimate of the number of new faces
created by splitting is also parallelized.

Time building the weld faces (minimum of 12 runs):
| Scene           | Before  | After   |
| --------------- | ------- | ------- |
| quads_to_tris   | 57.6 ms | 12.1 ms |
| solidify_merge  | 23.6 ms | 5.1 ms  |
| collapse_blocks | 17.9 ms | 2.6 ms  |
| sparse          | 14.9 ms | 8.8 ms  |
| cube_2500x      | 14.4 ms | 3.1 ms  |
| weld_split      | 5.2 ms  | 1.5 ms  |
| ngon_split      | 5.0 ms  | 1.2 ms  |

subject: Mesh: Merge: Parallelize finding collapsed and duplicate edges
message:
Mesh: Merge: Parallelize finding collapsed and duplicate edges

Find the affected vertices, the collapsed edges, and the remaining
affected edges in parallel, using index masks instead of a single-
threaded vector build.

To find duplicate edges, group the them by their lower vertex after
merging, then sort each group by the higher vertex. Duplicates are next
to each other after sorting, and the first of each which has the lowest
index is kept. This replaces the single threaded intersection of sorted
vertex to edge lists, and replaces "WeldEdge" struct with OrderedEdge.

Time finding collapsed and duplicate edges (minimum of 12 runs):
| Scene           | Before   | After   |
| --------------- | -------- | ------- |
| quads_to_tris   | 117.9 ms | 39.2 ms |
| collapse_blocks | 68.8 ms  | 25.3 ms |
| weld_split      | 66.7 ms  | 12.3 ms |
| solidify_merge  | 58.3 ms  | 25.4 ms |
| sparse          | 27.9 ms  | 12.1 ms |
| cube_2500x      | 22.0 ms  | 13.8 ms |
| ngon_split      | 8.8 ms   | 9.5 ms  |

subject: Mesh: Merge: Replace WeldCorner struct with an array of indices
message:
Mesh: Merge: Replace WeldCorner struct with an array of indices

Each corner of the affected faces used a 16 byte struct to store its
vertex and edge after merging, its source index, and the next corner,
plus a map from every mesh corner to its weld corner. The vertex and
edge are available from the input mesh and the vertex and edge target
maps, and faces are just linked lists of their remaining source corners.
Replace all of that with a single array of the next corner for the
corners of affected faces.

This makes the code refer to the input data more directly, and reduces
memory usage. (from 180 MB to 36 MB on a 1500x1500 grid with all corners
affected). The corner iterator is replaced by a simple loop over the
linked list.

Time building the weld context (minimum of 12 runs):
| Scene           | Before   | After    |
| --------------- | -------- | -------- |
| collapse_blocks | 240.3 ms | 132.5 ms |
| quads_to_tris   | 316.3 ms | 143.9 ms |
| solidify_merge  | 191.7 ms | 145.1 ms |
| weld_split      | 124.7 ms | 105.8 ms |
| sparse          | 88.8 ms  | 52.2 ms  |
| ngon_split      | 49.1 ms  | 28.9 ms  |

Building the result corners looks up the vertex and edge of every corner
now, which is slightly slower when all corners are affected (e.g. 83 ms
to 115 ms for quads_to_tris), but that is outweighed by the other
changes and will be parallelized in a future commit anyway.

subject: Cycles: Offset denoising depth by near clip plane
message:
Cycles: Offset denoising depth by near clip plane

Future versions of Intel Open Image Denoise (OIDN) will expect the
denoising depth value to lie between a near and far value. Supplying
values outside of this range can lead to visual issues.
So far, Cycles let a depth of 0 correspond to the near clip plane and
chose the maximum depth value `FLT_MAX`.

The following changes are introduced to make the denoising depth more
robust:
- The near clip plane is added to the depth for bounce 0. This makes
  sure that the depth value will never be lower than the near clip
  plane. For orthographic cameras this is skipped, as
  `nearclip = -farclip / 2` is used and OIDN does not accept negative
  near clip planes.
- When writing the background denoising features, `FLT_MAX` is replaced
  by the far clip plane depth. For orthogonal cameras, `cliplength` is
  used due to the reasons outlined above.

subject: Outliner: Custom Sorting for Objects and Collections
message:
Outliner: Custom Sorting for Objects and Collections

This PR is an implementation of #68502. The PR adds manual sorting for
objects in the Outliner, allowing users to manually reorder objects and
collections. Objects and Collections can be interleaved. Old files are
switched to Custom mode.

If both Alphabet and non alphabet sorting is on in the old file the
sort_index will use the non alphabet(collection.gobject) order and the
outliner with Alphabet will stay in alphabet mode.

The objects are sorted in the UI not the actual collection storage
(Collection.gobject) due to the concern that other code may need scene
data in a different order, or might want to change order for its
operations. New objects are placed at the end of the collection. If the
objects were added in alphabetical modes they get added add the end in
alphabetical order. If you add in custom mode the objects are added at
then end. I multiple are added with a script the objects get added at
the end of the collection in alphabetical order.

CollectionObject's sort_index and parented_sort_index are exposed to the
Python API. CollectionChild's sort_index is also exposed. When in
alphabet mode there may be gaps in sort_index values or index of -1,
meaning the object has not been assigned a value (This will happen when
switching to custom, or it manually be set). When in custom mode if an
object was added with python and the Depsgraph has not run with
ID_RECALC_HIERARCHY tagged, then there can be gaps or index of -1.

Initial ordering is preserved from the ordering mode the was switched
from when first switching to custom ordering.

If an old file had alphabet mode off that order of the gobject is the
initial sort_index order and the new mode is now custom.

subject: Alembic: remember default and active color attributes
message:
Alembic: remember default and active color attributes

Prior to version 3.5, when importing an Alembic file the default and
active color attributes were set to the first color layer. Since then,
as the default and active color attributes are stored as strings on the
Mesh object, importing an Alembic file leaves those uninitialized.

Note that this only worked prior to 3.5 as the indices for the active
and default layers were initialized by default to zero.

Remembering those default and active attributes is necessary after
an import for e.g. being able to visualize the colors using viewport
shading overlays.

As Alembic does not have a concept of default or active color
attribute, this writes the name of those attributes in the mesh user
properties during export.

During import, we lookup those properties and use them to set the
default and active color layers. If the properties do not exist, we
default to the first color layer.

This adds a test for the new export and import of the default and
active names, and updates old tests to check that the fallback to the
first layer works.

subject: Vulkan: Fix missing instance extensions
message:
Vulkan: Fix missing instance extensions

The Vulkan spec states:

```
Any device extension that has an instance extension dependency that is
not enabled by vkCreateInstance is considered to be unsupported, hence
it must not be returned by vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties for any
VkPhysicalDevice child of the instance.
```
Unfortunately this has not actually been followed by many drivers so far,
but it is to be fixed in future driver releases. The problem is that
Blender currently relies on the broken behavior: For its platform checks
it creates a Vulkan instance with no instance extensions enabled and
then checks all physical devices enumerated via that instance for
support of the "VK_KHR_swapchain" device extension.

That extension has a dependency on the `VK_KHR_surface` instance
extension, which means that as per the above spec statement it may only
be enumerated if the instance was created with that extension enabled.
Since that wasn't the case, the code would fail and report
"VK_KHR_swapchain" as a missing feature on drivers that follow that spec
directive, causing Vulkan initialization in Blender to fail as a whole.
This patch fixes that by simply creating the instance with the required
extension enabled.

Some values don't need full float precision, and with millions of states
reducing memory usage is important, while the math to pack/unpack these
is quite cheap. On CPU full precision is used since there are few states
and the extra conversion cost only hurts.

features like LIGHT_PASSES + DENOISING or SUBSURFACE + VOLUME.

Benchmarks do not show any significant impact on GPU render time either
way.

USD: Add support for importing UsdVolParticleField3DGaussianSplat

Add import support for the ParticleField3DGaussianSplat USD schema.

A notable implementation detail for this schema is that USD allows
both full-float and half-float data types to be used for each of the
positions/orientations/scales/opacities/radiance attributes (the

memory usage. Our implementation hides this behind some simple wrappers
while accessing the data. The half-float data is converted to full-float
when loading into our geometry attributes.

subject: Cycles: Switch to CUDA 13 and enable DLSS
message:
Cycles: Switch to CUDA 13 and enable DLSS

The commit switches Cycles to use CUDA-13 by default, which makes it
easier to add support for CUDA on Windows arm64 platform.

This commit also enables Cycles DLSS denoising, make Blender ready to
utilize this technology as soon as an updated Nvidia driver is releases
with the required runtime.

The changes are coupled together because they required changes on the
buildbot system side: the SDK's needed to be installed, and the
information about them somehow needed to be passed to Blender. To make
similar deployments easier in the future this change makes it so the SDK
versions from

  build_files/config/pipeline_config.yaml

to

  build_files/buildbot/config/blender_version.cmake

Buildbot provides information about root directory where the specific
SDKs are installed, giving flexibility to the buildbot to move things
around if needed, but also making it more control to Blender developers
to tweak the logic.

Last but not least, the way how CUDA toolkit is selected for Cycles
kernels got refactored to make it easier to follow:

- There is an easy to follow table of per-architecture or family
  toolkits.
- If there is no architectural preference, all provided toolkits are
  probed. For SM kernels newer toolkits are tested first, and for
  COMPUTE the oldest toolkits are probed first.
- If there is no suitable toolkit with explicit major version the
  default one is used.

A driver version 580 and above is now required. From quick checks it
seems that on Windows it shouldn't be a problem since 582 driver is
available for sm_50 devices (the oldest architecture we compile).

Grease Pencil: Boolean Carver Tool

This PR implements a new `Carver` tool in Draw Mode.

Both strokes & fills are cut along the lasso input. Holes are
automatically created when needed.

Notes:
* Cutting non-poly curves is currently not supported. All non-poly type
  curves near the lasso will be converted to poly, with a warning
  displayed to the user.
* Fills are automatically split into separate ids when the shape is
  split up into multiple fill islands.
* If a curve uses both stroke and fill, carving a hole into the fill
  will also add a stroke to the hole.
* If a curve uses both stroke and fill, carving into the shape from the
  outside will currently close the fill.

The implementation is based on a modified version of the Greiner-Hormann
clipping algorithm.

subject: Fix: GLSL C++ files are recompiling after editing CMakeLists files on Windows
message:
Fix: GLSL C++ files are recompiling after editing CMakeLists files on Windows

The reason for this was that the "wrapper" file that was including the
actual GLSL file was written on every invocation of the CMake: the file
timestamp changed, and the file was rightfully recompiled.

Solved by using file(GENERATE) which only writes the output file only
if the content changes.

The tricky part is that the same GLSL source file might be used by
multiple targets with different compiler definitions. This leads to
file(GENERATE) complain that the same file was requested to be generated
twice. To solve this issue the generated file name is prefixed with the
library name.

subject: Nodes: new Comment node
message:
Nodes: new Comment node

This adds a new Comment node to simplify documenting a node tree.

Currently people use two main ways to add such comments:
* Frame nodes with titles/descriptions. Titles should stay, but
  multi-line text in frame nodes doesn't work well and might be removed
  eventually.
* String input nodes. Since those have multi-line textboxes, they can be
  used for documentation.

For the common use-case of adding a description to some part of the node
tree (that is not just a frame title), this new Comment node is superior
to both alternatives. It has better ux and supports markdown rendering.

The Comment node uses the same background color as frame nodes and thus
integrates nicely visually already. It also has the same alternating-color
behavior like nested frames so that it remains visible even if it's in a
frame.

There are multiple ways to edit the comment:
* Double click on it.
* Activate the node and press F2.
* Hover the node and hit enter.
* Click the edit icon.
* In the sidebar in the node panel.

subject: BLI: New KDTree implementation with better performance
message:
BLI: New KDTree implementation with better performance

This PR adds a new KD-tree implementation that is much faster to build
and has much faster lookup performance. It's a new implementation
because the API is different, and the heritage of the code is completely
separate. The code structure is derived from the nanoflann library [0],
but heavily modified to work better with Blender code and to further
improve performance, by a large amount in some cases.

The provided API is a bit opinionated: it forgoes the separate "insert"
and "balance" steps with a single "build" step, making the caller build
their own coordinate array that can then be referenced by the caller.
Optionally, a subset of the coordinates can be referenced by an index
span or an IndexMask.

A few bounding box calculation functions are also improved to use
pipelining to reduce the cost of dependent writes. For some cases that
can be a 3-5x performance improvement as well.

Overall performance is a significant improvement. In a test of 1 million
points on a Ryzen 7950X:

|                   | BLI_kdtree | nanoflann |        |
| ----------------- | ---------- | --------- | ------ |
| Build (random)    |     204 ms |    5.5 ms |  37.2x |
| Build (grid-like) |     168 ms |    4.4 ms |  38.2x |
| Find nearest      |    4.49 us |    479 ns |   9.4x |
| Find 8 nearest    |    8.27 us |   1.40 us |  5.91x |
| Memory            |    26.7 MB |    6.5 MB |  0.24x |

For more performance numbers, see the pull request.

For this initial commit, I only changed usage in three Geometry Nodes
files. After that, incrementally switching in separate commits should be
a much better process.

[0]: https://github.com/jlblancoc/nanoflann

subject: Anim: world space copy paste frame range
message:
Anim: world space copy paste frame range

This adds functionality to store world space data in a temporary file
on disk and paste it on other objects.
(technically `AnimTransformable`s, which is objects or bones, but for
simplicity I will be talking about "objects" here)
Compared to the existing functionality this can also copy a
range of frames. Because the data is stored on disk, it is possible
to copy and paste between files.

**Matching Logic**
* When 1 object copied and 1 selected -> paste no matter the naming
* When 1 object copied and 2:n selected -> paste the same data to
all selected
* When 2:n objects copied and 1:n selected -> paste based on naming.
It is possible to paste between objects and bones as long
as the name matches.

**Depsgraph**
* Introduces a new API function `DEG_foreach_dependent_component`
* this function iterates the outgoing links starting at a given ID
* it is used to find the order in which to paste world space transforms
since we have to paste in order of dependency -> dependent
for it to work correctly.

**UI**
Adding a new panel because the new operators are not compatible
with the existing ones. I cannot remove the existing operators because
they provide functionality that I don't yet provide.
To make it clear that they don't work together, they get their own panel.

**Limitations**
* objects with constraints may not end up at the correct world space.
That is expected for limit constraints, but additive constraints would
need to be inverse solved which is a job for another day.
* when the rotation mode is animated, pasting world space animation
will override all keys in the baked range to be the value at the
start of the range.

subject: Geometry Nodes: Poisson solver node for grids
message:
Geometry Nodes: Poisson solver node for grids

The grid Poisson solver node solves `Poisson's equation, which relates
the value of each grid voxel to its neighbors. The result is an output
grid that produces the input grid when the Laplace operator is applied
(sum of gradient contributions from surrounding voxels).

In addition to the source values of the input grid the solution also
depends on boundary conditions at the edge of the solution space.
The default condition enforces a solution value of zero at the boundary
everywhere. Other modes allow enforcing custom fixed values
(Dirichlet condition), or custom gradient values of the resulting
function (Neumann condition), or a combination of both ("Mixed" boundary
condition).

The node is based around the OpenVDB Poisson solver. The solution is
computed on the active values of the input grid. Voxel faces between
active and inactive voxels form the boundary. Technically each face
could have its own boundary conditions, but for practical reasons the
conditions are evaluated at all inactive voxels bordering on the active
solution space (i.e. a 1-voxel dilation of the input grid). This means
all boundary voxels share the same condition, which is an acceptable
limitation for common Poisson problems.

subject: Fix #161249: Scene thumbnails flicker when drawing
message:
Fix #161249: Scene thumbnails flicker when drawing

When a thumbnail frame is looked up we check if it already exists in
cache (exact match), if so we use it otherwise we request that thumbnail
and load the nearest frame in the meantime.

However if a frame gets invalidated (eg. when a scene frame updates),
the thumbnail immediately gets removed from the cache, and is requested
so nothing is loaded between removal time and request completion time
leading to the flickering behavior observed in #161249.

Solution: add a "stale" flag to cache fame entries. If we find a stale
frame, we still display it, but request a new one to be generated.

subject: GSplat: Initial rendering support for Cycles
message:
GSplat: Initial rendering support for Cycles

Based on the "Stochastic ray tracing of transparent 3D Gaussians" paper
by Xin Sun et. al. The basic idea: perform stochastic intersection with
the Gaussian splat based on its transparency.

Gaussian splats are implemented as a dedicated primitive type, but it
shares the same layout for position and radius as points, so a lot of
existing functions (positions, attributes, etc) work for both points
and splats.

For the Embree and hardware intersection it is implemented as a custom
primitive type.

The choice of using bounding spheres mainly comes from a balance between
performance and memory usage. More ideal would be to use OBB, but it is
not supported for custom primitive types in Embree and GPU HW-RT on all
backends.

There is a known limitation that comes from the fact that the datasets
are trained in sRGB space and Cycles work in Linear space: areas with
low opacity and high radiance render noticeably differently from the
ground-truth implementation.

drop PLY file into the node editor and it would import as either

subject: GSplat: Implement SPZ format importer
message:
GSplat: Implement SPZ format importer

The SPZ format is more space efficient storing gaussian splats, and is
quite popular on the Internet.

This commit implements it naively without using the SPZ library.
Motivation:

- Simplifies platform maintenance.

- Allows to have writes of different versions.
  For example, glTF currently mentions SPZ v2 in the extension draft
  while the current SPZ library is v4 (it is a bit unclear whether glTF
  is talking about library or format version tho).

- Lowers peak memory usage by avoiding multiple copies of the same data
  in memory.

Currently does not implement extensions reading, and does not handle
the anti-alias flag.

Expects the content to follow the convention of Right-Up-Back.
An observation was made that not all editors and tools create SPZ files
with this convention. Even the ply_to_spz command line tool from the
SPZ repository does not transform the typical PLY convention assumed by
the library to the SPZ convention. In practice it means that a manual
re-orientation of the import might be required.

The commit is limited to import via the File menu and dropping the
file onto the viewport. Support of importing SPZ via geometry nodes is
coming soon.

subject: GSplat: Use specialized shader network for gaussian splats
message:
GSplat: Use specialized shader network for gaussian splats

This change makes it so a specialized shader network is created when
adding a new material on a Point Cloud that is a 3D Gaussian Splats.

This is because gaussian splats are radiance fields that need to be
rendered as emissive shader.

The network consists of the following nodes:

  [Attribute Node: "radiance"] -> [Emissive BSDF] -> [Surface Output]

The radiance attribute is a special attribute that will return
evaluated radiance for the shading point, taking into account view
angle dependent contribution. The view angle dependency comes from
the spherical harmonics that are sued by gaussian splats.

There are a few reasons to why it is done via the attribute node.

One of them is we want some flexible system where more attributes
could be represented via spherical harmonics. For example, maybe
albedo could be extracted from radiance, helping with relightable
gaussian splats.

Another reason is a bit technical, coming from the way how render
engines currently store attributes. They might store base radiance
separately from the spherical harmonics for bands >= 1, allowing
for either skipping spherical harmonics for speed and memory
efficiency, and using packing for the spherical harmonics. In the
future it might change, and we might use some specialized packing
that will become the radiance attribute and the existing shader
networks will keep working.

It also worth mentioning that from the render engine perspective it
does not make a lot of sense to implement something more generic like
"evaluate base + spherical harmonics for the given angle".
This is because shape and opacity depend on the vie wangle as well,
and those are handled by the rasterization/intersection code.

GSplat: Ensure PointCloud type is preserved through modification

The way to ensure it is to require the type passed to the point cloud
creation function. While this is quite disruptive change, it ensures
that the type is not forgotten to be set. It made it easier to catch
all places where the type needs to be preserved, and it will make it
more reliable in the future when new operations are added and tested
on a points without keeping in mind the existence of the gaussian
splats.

Some operations in the geometry nodes might not be fully ideal yet as
operations that operate on multiple geometries only considers the first
point cloud. It might be better to change the logic so that it checks
whether there is any gaussian splat and set type to gsplat in this

- Rendering algorithms
- Attribute handling to eventually support rigging of gaussian splats.

Attribute convention for the future IO and render engines integration:
- "scale" for the scale of the gaussian splat, stored as float3
- "rotation" gaussian splat rotation, stored as quternion
- "radiance:base" the base (DC) radiance of the splats, followed by
   opacity and stored as float4
- "radiance:sh_{index}" for the coefficients of the bands >= 1 of the
  spherical harmonics, stored as float3.

Note that the relation of scale and radius is not very trivial (meaning
storing scale as radius that would become float3 was considered but was
not accepted). The scale is used to define the covariance matrix, and
the gaussian splat is technically unbound. It is possible to calculate
a bounding radius for the splat using scale and a cut-off opacity, but
it is rather arbitrary.

[kerbl3Dgaussians] Kerbl, Bernhard et. al.
  "3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering" (2023)

Alembic: export arbitrary attributes

This adds support to export arbitrary attributes to Alembic, for
meshes, curves, and pointclouds.

All attribute types are exported except `float4` which is not supported
by Alembic. See code comments for potential solutions if this becomes a
problem in the future.

`TypedGeomParam` for each attribute. To keep track of those
`TypedGeomParams` across frames, a class `AttributeParamMaps` is added.
This class holds a map for each type from attribute name to geom param.

lazily created when exporting attributes. This class generalizes what
we have currently in `CDStreamConfig` for UVs, vertex colors, and

not exported by this new code as they have the option to be
deduplicated and indexed, which is not supported for other attribute

subject: Vulkan: Make multi viewport feature optional
message:
Vulkan: Make multi viewport feature optional

Blender unconditionally requires the Vulkan multiViewport feature and
will fail to create a context on drivers that do not report it.

The feature is now optional. A new GPU_multi_viewport_support()
capability reports whether it can be used. Vulkan requires the
multiViewport feature and at least GPU_MAX_VIEWPORTS viewports;
Metal and OpenGL always report support. Apparently all devices
only support 1 or 16 viewports.

EEVEE uses the capability for shadow rendering. When it is unavailable,
the shadow module falls back to rendering each shadow view separately.
The fallback reads back the number of used views and each size,
restricts the shadow visibility shader to one view at a time and renders
at the origin of the shadow framebuffer.

When the fallback is enabled the performance would be slow, but at least
we can draw the correct shadows on these systems.

shader nodes. It is entirely handled by the inliner, so underlying
render engines don't need to change.

The node allows creating custom error/warning/info messages for higher
level node groups.

The most tricky thing about this node is that the warning node is not
necessarily connected to the output. The same solution as for Geometry

connected to the final output "side effect nodes". I used the same
terminology here.

subject: Fix #158954: Knife breaks under certain conditions
message:
Fix #158954: Knife breaks under certain conditions

Both the Knife tool and Knife Project were affected if the first point
is "outside geometry" and depending on certain views (more on that
later)
- when starting the Knife tool, it would not draw a line at all then
- Knife Project could end up making entirely unpredictable cuts at wrong
places

Probably caused by "cleanup" 6d491da0be35

Prior to 6d491da0be35, `knife_start_cut` (so the first click with the
tool or the first point in the "cutter") would set `kcd->prev.cage`
[which does not exist at that point - so still (0,0,0)] based off of the
mouse position offset to in front of the view via `ED_view3d_win_to_3d`.
This code block was removed in 6d491da0be35.

After 6d491da0be35, `knife_start_cut` relies on `knife_snap_curr`. If it
doesnt find geometry under the mouse cursor it can end up "getting a
point at the mouse ray closest to the previous point" via
`isect_line_plane_v3` instead -- but since it used the previous point
[still (0,0,0) at this point] this can get wrong down the line.
Especially if that ends up being **behind** the view, which in turn can
get even more unexpected when reprojecting into viewspace via
`knife_project_v2`].

Since knife_snap_curr always sets curr.cage and kcd->prev = kcd->curr
follows it, restoring copy would only overwrite a valid snapped
coordinate with the fallback point, so this needs to be left as-is.

So to resolve, bring back the part of 6d491da0be35 that handled
`prev.cage` so `knife_snap_curr` can then properly function.

NOTE: the whole "going back and forth between 3d and screenspace
coordinates" can generally lead to unexpected situations when navigating
whie using the tool, but this is subject for a possible future
improvevment.

subject: Core: initial support for stable .blend files
message:
Core: initial support for stable .blend files

The goal of this patch is to get to a state where opening a .blend file and then
saving it again can result in the byte-per-byte identical .blend file. While
that in itself is not all that useful, it helps indirectly with compression and
potentially other tools build for .blend files in the future. This is basically
an extension to previous work on stable pointers: #127729.

The main thing this patch fixes is that run-time data is more consistently reset
before the file is written. That was already done in a few places, but always
fairly ad-hoc with a custom temporary copy of the data. This patch extends the
`BlendStructWriter` API to make it easy to reset data before it is written to
the file and without having to adjust the original data.

Testing this with a specific .blend file is easiest when
`GENERATE_DEBUG_BLEND_FILE` is set to `1` in `writefile.cc`. This outputs a
human readable version whenever writing a .blend file. Diffing these text files
shows which data needs to be made stable.

While this fixes a large number of places, there are still a few files that are
not stable. Especially when opening a file in the GUI, UI data changes easily
without actually doing much.

I mostly tested this with all our regression test files with a script. The
script does the following:
1. Open the .blend file, then save it to a new location.
2. Open that saved file and save it to yet another location.
3. Same thing again.

These steps give a more accurate picture because sometimes, due to versioning
etc. stuff happens in the first save that does not happen the second time
around, especially for old files. Here is the summary of running that over all
test files:
```
A: First saved file.
B: Second saved file.
C: Third saved file.

A == B == C: 1.107 files
A != B == C:   652 files
A != B != C:   251 files
Other error:    31 files
```

As we can see, the majority of files become stable with this patch (at least
when opened/saved with a script, without GUI). Without this patch, none of the
files is stable.

subject: Fix #163594: Bad performance after seeking while playing
message:
Fix #163594: Bad performance after seeking while playing

The movie reader cache was not sufficiently guarded against concurrent
renders. When prefetch is enabled, when trying to render uncached area,
both prefetch and main thread will try to render around the same frame.
The movie reader cache was reused and prefetch thread was forced to
seek backwards which is costly. This blocked main next frame render.By
the time 1 cycle was complete, AV sync caused current frame to advance
much further, so this cycle did repeat.

Add thread owner tracking to movie reader cache, so prefetch or any
other thread never reuses readers of main thread.

minimum number of frames, but not a minimum number of recording time
seconds. For example, at 500 FPS, the previous limit of a minimum of 250

message:
Mesh: Merge: Use identity map for un-merged vertices in API

At the API level, it's simpler if the vert merging map consistently
uses the vertex index itself to represent vertices that aren't merged,
that way calling code doesn't have to worry about the distinction
between vertices that are completely un-involved in the merge and
vertices that are targets.

Inside the merging code, a separate map with the -1 values for
un-involved elements is still built, but its purpose as a performance
improvement is clearer. On the outside, the API only requires a Span,
not a mutable array, which simplifies the geometry node.

Technically this means that sometimes information is lost at the API
barrier, but overall the simplicity benefit is worth it, and the cost of
one more array of integers isn't necessarily meaningful in practice.

subject: Cleanup: CMake: Remove legacy blender/makesdna target dependency
message:
Cleanup: CMake: Remove legacy blender/makesdna target dependency

This blender -> makesdna target dependency dates back to the initial
CMake integration commit from 2006 (24f4440d05aa), at the time, blender
was still directly using dna.c in its add_executable target command and
this dependency was required to ensure the file was properly by the
makesdna custom_command() regenerated.

However, with time and refactors, this direct dependency doesn't make
sense anymore. Nowadays the blender target (and many other module) link
against the bf::dna target (introduced in 7cebb61486bc), which owns
dna_*.cc files, whose generation then depend on makesdna. Bypassing the
need for direct blender -> makesdna relationship completely.

Cleaning-up this specfic dependency now allows for simplification in
the `android` branch where the use of an extra host_tools CMake module,
which allows to build host generation tools like makesdna for the *host*
and not the target, requires the use of additional dependency logic
with the generation of files then depending on both the `host_tools`
target and the outputed generator executable which isn't possible with
simple target `add_dependency()` CMake statements.

subject: UI: support markdown labels
message:
UI: support markdown labels

This implements a new `layout.label_markdown(text="...")` function which
supports drawing a subset of Markdown in the Blender UI. The original motivation
for this was to support markdown in a new Comment node (#163168). However, the
functionality is more useful more generally. For example it could be used to
draw extension descriptions or maybe tooltips in the future etc.

It uses the [md4c](https://github.com/mity/md4c) library for the actual markdown
parsing. It has the MIT license. It's a very simple to integrate C library, just
on .c and one .h file.

The following markdown features are supported currently:
* Headers
* Paragraphs
* Bold/italics/monospace text
* Clickable links
* Code blocks
* Inline code

Intentionally omitted:
* Tables: Could be added later.
* Images: Could be added later, but needs design regarding internet access.
* Footnotes: Could be added later if needed.
* Latex math Could be added but requires more work to render such text in the
  first place.
* Underlined and striked through text: Could be added if our font system
  supports it.
* Syntax highlighting in code blocks: Could be added later.
* Raw HTML: Unlikely that this will be supported.

All the various margins etc. are hard-coded but there is a UI to be able to find
the right values by using `4002` in the `Debug Menu`. The settings could be
theme settings but it seems overkill to add that many right now.

subject: Cycles: Add NVIDIA DLSS support for viewport denoising
message:
Cycles: Add NVIDIA DLSS support for viewport denoising

Adds the option to use DLSS Ray Reconstruction for viewport denoising
in Cycles. For this to work, scheduling is adjusted to continuously
reset samples (so that independent frames are rendered), pixel jitter
is forced on and the required denoising passes (color, depth, diffuse
albedo, specular albedo, normals, roughness, motion vectors, specular
motion vectors) are enabled.
DLSS expects those inputs in the form of CUDA textures, while Cycles
keeps passes in an interleaved buffer layout. The data therefore has to
be converted, for which specialized versions of the existing denoising
filter kernels are introduced, which read/write directly to temporary
CUDA textures that are managed in denoiser_dlss.cpp.

The integration of DLSS itself is done in a similar fashion to OptiX:
The DLSS SDK is pulled in for the type definitions, but the DLSS
implementation is loaded by the NVIDIA driver installed on the system.

subject: Fix #163609: Targetless IK constraint transform is broken
message:
Fix #163609: Targetless IK constraint transform is broken

Caused by af9ba6af76

Above commit neglected the fact that a bone with a targetless IK
constraint can still be grabbed (as if AutoIK was enabled). Such a
constraint always gets flagged `CONSTRAINT_DISABLE` though (by
`test_constraint`), now failing the new `BKE_constraint_has_influence`.

This in turn led to  the loop in `initialize_posetree` no longer
stopping after adding a sole PoseTarget, but also appended the temporary
auto-IK copy created while grabbing the bone. The IK solver then
received two goals for the same end effector: one tracking the mouse,
one frozen at the drag's starting position.

LLM review also spotted a second case in `iksolver_execute_tree` (also
involving IK constraints carrying the `CONSTRAINT_DISABLE` flag while
still needing to be considered valid).

To resolve, tweak `BKE_constraint_has_influence` to even return true for
IK constraints carrying `CONSTRAINT_DISABLE` (if they are also flagged
`CONSTRAINT_IK_AUTO` or `CONSTRAINT_IK_TEMP`)

subject: UI: add pre/post drawing callbacks to SpaceType
message:
UI: add pre/post drawing callbacks to SpaceType

Add two callbacks `draw_pre(context, area)` and `draw_post(context,
area)` to the `SpaceType` type. These are called before and after all
dirty regions in a space/area are drawn.

This is not yet used, but will be in use by the Dope Sheet in the
future. The draw callbacks for the 'channel list' and 'main' regions can
then cache their animation channels, cleaning them up in the new
post-draw call.

Without this space/area-level post-draw call, it would be much harder
for the individual region draw callbacks to share state, and still have
that state properly invalidated for the next draw call.

Furthermore, any memory can now be freed when it is no longer used,
rather than keeping it around until it's known to be 'dirty'.

subject: Fix #163256: error where filling curves with holes only output a hole
message:
Fix #163256: error where filling curves with holes only output a hole

Filling relied on original face ids to decide which
faces must stay valid, these are only set for CCW faces,
so every edge inside a CW face was dissolved.
The "Fill Curve" node then output only the holes.

Resolve by using the hole status for output types with holes,
as the even-odd & non-zero rules accept either orientation.

Note that this changes how winding multiple times is interpreted,
each lap flips the even-odd "fill" state.
So 1x winding around a polygon is filled, 2x isn't 3x is ... and so on
(matching SVG/PostScript behavior for the even-odd method).

Remove `USE_FACE_ORDERED_EDGE_DEDUPE` since it doesn't define expected
behavior for filling and was only added as a stress test.
An OBJ face that walks its boundary twice no longer imports as a face,
update the test data accordingly.

Technically a regression in [0], although it only worked by accident:
the face-id flood used to escape the face boundary and tag the whole CDT
(the slowdown [0] resolved), so no interior edges were dissolved.
Limiting the flood-fill exposed that `add_face_ids` skips CW faces,
leaving the input face winding to decide which faces are kept,
even though even-odd filling should ignore the winding.

subject: Fix: Motion Path evaluated range logic
message:
Fix: Motion Path evaluated range logic

Caused by 8ecb6d30e47

The logic used for checking if a target was already evaluated wasn't
correct. It started each target normally and added the evaluated range.
The issue is that the evaluation may not hit the start and end frames
of the range.
That means comparing the evaluated range against the range of the
motion path could create a case where the optimization is always skipped.

In the normal case that means 5 extra depsgraph evaluations per target.
The fix is to look at the start frame instead of the full motion
path range. That frame is clamped into the motion path range, so in
case the ranges don't overlap it will still work.

due to the known limitation where altering data in handlers can cause

not protected by the interface lock. So to fix it, we also do not update
the cursor if the interface is locked.

subject: Refactor: Paint: Store and use `AssetCategory` instead of `PaintMode`
message:
Refactor: Paint: Store and use `AssetCategory` instead of `PaintMode`

The `PaintMode` enum is used as a kind of polymorphism for the
underlying stroke and shared paint systems, allowing specifying behavior
for different modes based on their support.

This concept previously was stored on the `PaintRuntime` object, which
has some now obvious downsides, mainly that it cannot represent Image
and Texture paint correctly. The two modes share the same `Paint`
struct, and the current plan is for them to continue to do so as much as
possible.

Therefore, it is incorrect to store the `PaintMode` on runtime
initialization, as it adds burden to be correct when switching between
the Image Editor and the 3D Viewport while texture painting.

The other usecase for this data was to map to a specific essentials
asset file at runtime. Since Image and Texture paint share the same set
of brushes, it makes more sense to allow this to be stored and scoped
for this specific usage.

In other operators, the `PaintMode` should either be retrieved from the
context, or hardcoded if specific to a given mode.

subject: Fix: Grease Pencil: Double start point
message:
Fix: Grease Pencil: Double start point

This fixes a problem where the second point would have the same position
and radius as the first point.

This was caused by 11bfac7f1109fc4c7ca760129ec29c6aae9333df
The `linear_interpolation` is only every applied to the new points
(never the first point) so `include_first_point` only every caused
duplicate data.

To insure the first point is not moved by smoothing the
`active_smooth_start_index_` should start at 1 instead of 0

The `active smoothing` would change the position of the second point
causing the problem to be hard to find.

When `active smoothing` is zero or less then 8 points are drawn the
double point can be seen, and will cause rendering problems.

subject: Fix #162455: Geometry nodes bool attribute needs correct default input type
message:
Fix #162455: Geometry nodes bool attribute needs correct default input type

Since 1561c1ea4ab a bool input socket with a default attribute name will
not be automatically set to the `Attribute` default input type.
All other input socket types do this because they use the
`make_common_value_and_attribute_props` function which selects between
`Attribute` and `Value` default input type based on the existence of the
default attribute name. The bool socket type was not using this wrapper
function because it includes the "Layer" enum option.

For bool sockets select the correct default input type:
If the socket is marked as a "Layer" then use the `Layer` type.
Otherwise use `Attribute` or `Value` just like for other attribute
socket type, depending on the default attribute name.

subject: Core: Add type-safe `ListBaseT<T>` first/last element functions
message:
Core: Add type-safe `ListBaseT<T>` first/last element functions

Add type-safe methods to `ListBase<T>` to get the first and last item
in the list.

- `T *first()`: Return the first item as a `T*`
- `T *last()`: Return the last item as a `T*`
- `U *first_as<U>()`: Return the first item as a `U*`
- `U *last_as<U>()`: Return the last item as a `U*`

This changes code like this:

```cpp
const bTheme *btheme = static_cast<const bTheme *>(U.themes.first);
return static_cast<View3D *>(area->spacedata.first);
```

into:

```cpp
const bTheme *btheme = U.themes.first();
return area->spacedata.first_as<View3D>();
```

This PR may not be complete. There might be uses of `first_` and
`last_` left that could use the accessor functions. Also there may be
casts around `first()`/`last()` that can be replaced by
`first_as<>()`/`last_as<>()`. Those cases can be fixed up later.

Co-authored by @filedescriptor

I used an LLM (locally-run llama.cpp + opencode + Qwen 3.6 model) to
do some of the refactoring and help with the merging of the PRs.

subject: Fix #162908: Cycles: Copy correct number of pass components
message:
Fix #162908: Cycles: Copy correct number of pass components

`render_buffers_host_copy_denoised` always copied 4 components per
denoised pass, overflowing into the following pass for 3-component
passes such as the shadow catcher pass.

Since 74ffed0a34, the denoising albedo pass happened to sit right after
the shadow catcher pass in the render buffer, so the stray write
corrupted the albedo, making it red on the first sample and shifting to
blue as samples accumulated.

The issue is fixed by copying only the actual number of components of
each pass.

subject: Refactor: Outliner: Remove the now unused & unsafe element add functions
message:
Refactor: Outliner: Remove the now unused & unsafe element add functions

All element types now construct through the type safe `add_element()`,
so the `void *create_data` overload and the
`AbstractTreeElement::create_from_type()` switch it went through are
unused. With them, the last places where an arbitrary pointer was cast
to whatever the element constructor expected are gone, and where a
non-ID pointer was reinterpreted as an `ID *` to serve as the tree-store
identity.
