subject: Fix: race conditions in HTTP downloader
message:
Fix: race conditions in HTTP downloader

Fix race condition between main & background process when cancelling
and re-queueing downloads. This could make the downloader skip
downloads, as a re-queue of the same download would be cancelled along
with the original.

The main process keeps track of pending cancellations, so that
re-queued downloads are handled properly even when the previous
cancellation still has to be handled by the background process.

The background process now also emits 'was cancelled' reports for
queued-but-not-yet-started downloads, which means that any download
request sent to the background either gets completed or gets an error
reported. Before this PR, cancellation of queued-but-not-started
downloads would be silent. This guaranteed messaging of cancellations
is what makes the main process' bookkeeping work.

One minor API change: when queued downloads are cancelled,
`BackgroundDownloader.all_downloads_done` now flips at cancel time
rather than when the report round-trips via the background process. So
even when there is still a pending download (that is scheduled for
cancellation), the `BackgroundDownloader` will say that they're all
'done'. In a sense it's still true, and shutting down the downloader
at that time will simply cancel those about-to-be-canceled-anyway
downloads.

`BackgroundDownloader._num_pending_downloads` is no longer explicitly
tracked, but rather derived from the number of 'on done' callbacks.
This reduces the bookkeeping to one source of truth.

subject: Core: Optimize out truely indirect packed data on write.
message:
Core: Optimize out truely indirect packed data on write.

Until now, on write we'd always write all packed data unconditionally.

While this worked, this had several draw-back:
  - Bloating blendfiles with useless data. Especially in complex
    multi-stage pipelines, the latest stages could acuumulate hundreds
    of useless packed assets e.g.
  - Making it harder to recover from issues like the one fixed by
    a4a8dd0214.

This commit does two main changes:

Changes to definition of direct/indirect linked packed ID
---------------------------------------------------------

Now, a linked packed ID is considered directly linked if it's used by a
local ID, _or by any other packed ID also directly linked_.

The later part is the change here, as linked packed IDs dependencies are
conceptually part of the packed data (as they participate in the deep
hash value), so if one is directly used, all of its dependencies must
also be considered as directly used.

As a reminder, linked packed IDs can only use other linked packed IDs,
they are not allowed to depend on regular linked data.

Changes to library writing and packed IDs writing
-------------------------------------------------

Now that there is a more useful and coherent definition of directly vs.
indirectly linked packed IDs, code writing linked data can now only
write directly linked packed IDs.

The indirectly linked ones are exclusively used by regular linked data
from other libraries, so writing them in the current blendfile is
useless and only wastes space.

The way libraries has also been refactored to fix a situation where the
'parent' regular library could be ordered after some of its 'children'
archive libraries in Main, leading to invalid writing order.

Regular lib should always be written immediately before all of its
archives, so code now ensures that it is the case.

subject: GPU: Metal support for Hardware Ray Queries
message:
GPU: Metal support for Hardware Ray Queries

Implement the GPU ray-query API on the Metal backend, mirroring the
Vulkan implementation from 348bb4a2d0. Acceleration structures can now
be built and traversed from any shader stage on Apple Silicon.

- Add MTLBottomLevelAS and MTLTopLevelAS: triangle bottom-level builds
  and instance top-level builds via an acceleration structure command
  encoder.
- Refit the top-level structure in place for instance transform updates
  instead of rebuilding, matching the Vulkan update path.
- Bind the top-level structure for compute, vertex and fragment stages,
  keeping the structure and its referenced geometry resident.
- Provide an MSL shim mapping the GLSL GL_EXT_ray_query functions onto
  Metal's inline intersection_query, including ray-flag handling (cull
  modes, opacity forcing, terminate-on-first-hit).
- Store a per-instance user ID in the top-level instance descriptors
  (the Metal equivalent of the ray-query instance custom index),
  currently 0 to match the Vulkan backend.
- Report ray-query support on macOS 13+ Apple Silicon.

Also sort the acceleration structure input segment in
ShaderInterface::sort_inputs(), correcting shader input lookups for
ray-query shaders on all backends.

subject: Assets: download online previews in LIFO fashion
message:
Assets: download online previews in LIFO fashion

When browsing online assets, download the last-requested preview
first. This ensures that, when scrolling through the assets, the
previews that are scrolled into view get priority over previews that
are scrolled out of view.

This introduces an optional keyword-only parameter to
`http.BackgroundDownloader.queue_download(queue_side=QueueSide)`,
where `QueueSide` is an enum with values `FRONT` and `BACK`.

The asset downloader always uses `BACK` for FIFO behaviour, and the
preview downloader always uses `FRONT` for LIFO behaviour.

This causes preview images in the asset browser to be downloaded
bottom-to-top (speaking visually here). This can be adjusted in
Blender's C++ code by requesting the thumbnails in the opposite order.

As an alternative implementation, a priority queue was discussed.
Previews that are scrolled out of view could then get a lower
priority. This means that Blender would have to track which previews
are requested for download, as well as track how many windows are
showing certain previews (because "scrolled out of view in one asset
browser" doesn't always mean "no longer visible"). Simply downloading
the previews in LIFO order was considerably simpler, and likely
sufficient.

Fix #161404: Deps: Build OpenXR as shared library on macOS/Linux to fix symbol shadowing issue

type metadata symbol to be duplicated and shadow the base libc++
symbols, causing exception catching type comparaison to fail in

connect on macOS and Linux. Since the library situation doesn't change
on Windows (where the OpenXR Loader lib remains static) a rebuild
should only be needed on macOS / Linux, and can be skipped on Win32 /

subject: Shader Nodes: replace closure recursion check with stack limit
message:
Shader Nodes: replace closure recursion check with stack limit

Previously, recursive closures were forbidden in shader nodes because they could
lead to infinite recursion. Now recursive closures are allowed and infinite
loops are prevented by enforcing a maximum stack limit. The same approach is
used by Geometry Nodes (#156843).

The existing `geometry_nodes_stack_limit` user preference is renamed to
`nodes_stack_limit` and is used in Geometry and Shader nodes now. The limit is
100 by default.

This fixes #161692.

Note that technically, the problem with recursive closures here is slightly
different here compared to Geometry Nodes. In Geometry Nodes, recursive closures
could actually lead to running out of stack space because it uses recursion
during evaluation when entering a closure. Shader nodes inlining is not
recursive but iterative, thus one doesn't run into the same stack space issue
but it's still effectively an infinite loop.

subject: Fix #161532: Undoing from Texture Paint into Particle Edit corrupts data
message:
Fix #161532: Undoing from Texture Paint into Particle Edit corrupts data

Particle Edit undo restored its mode by calling
`ED_object_particle_edit_mode_enter_ex()` directly.

When the undo step was decoded while Texture Paint was active, the
previous mode was not exited first. Since Particle Edit mode entry adds
its mode bit with `|=`, the object ended up with the invalid combined
mode `48` (`TEXTURE_PAINT | PARTICLE_EDIT`).

Exit the current mode through its normal lifecycle before restoring
Particle Edit, following the same pattern used by sculpt undo.

Files that were already saved with mode `48` crashed during editor
initialization because `object_mode_op_string()` returned `nullptr`.
Unsupported saved modes are now rejected safely, leaving the object in
Object Mode while preserving its particle and hair data so the file can
be resaved.

(because of higher register pressure).

subject: Anim: Improved AnimData rename API
message:
Anim: Improved AnimData rename API

Through a convoluted logic the previous AnimData renaming code
basically did:
* For any given ID
* check all FCurves it uses directly for the rename string
(includes owned drivers)
* check all other AnimData in Main if the given ID is being used as
a driver target

When doing that in a loop for many IDs, things can slow down
considerably. The solution is to build a map of ID to the drivers using
it as a target beforehand.
That way, we only have to do loop main once to build the map and
can then reuse it to subsequent calls to the rename function
(which only looks at the given ID)

### Implementation

**Removed `BKE_animdata_fix_paths_rename`**:
Since this function doesn't check for driver targets by looping main,
it missed to rename them leaving invalid drivers behind. When renaming
anything that can be animated it is never correct to ignore driver
targets which is why I removed it. Replaced with calls to
`BKE_animdata_fix_paths`.

**Removed `BKE_animdata_fix_paths_rename_all_ex` and `BKE_animdata_fix_paths_rename_all`**:
This has been replaced with a combination of
`BKE_animdata_build_driver_target_map` and `BKE_animdata_fix_paths`.
By splitting this up we can get the performance
gains when doing many renames at once.

**Added `RNA_path_name_to_infix` and `RNA_path_number_to_infix`**:
The new functions no longer assume anything about the rename string
they are given. Instead the caller has to format the strings accordingly
which is done with this function.
Doing so removes a boolean argument from the API.

In order to get the un-escaped name (which is needed for drivers
targeting pose bones by name) I added `infix_to_name`. This function
is not public because it makes a few assumptions
about the structure of the given string.

**`driver_target_path_fix` no longer verifies the path**
RNA paths for drivers can contain a trailing number like `[0]` to
indicate the array index. For regular rna paths this is usually a
separate integer which is why such paths won't resolve. Verifying the
path would mean that driver targets are not correctly updated, as
confirmed by the unit test that was disabled.
This is now fixed and the unit test was enabled.

### Fixed Issues

Fixes #155262
Fixes #159712
Fixes unreported: Drivers targeting VSE strips break if strip is renamed

Depending on the file, this is up to 27x times faster.

Part of #160849

subject: Fix & Improve threaded zstd blendfile compression code.
message:
Fix & Improve threaded zstd blendfile compression code.

This is addressing a potential concurrency issue introduced by
f541b19a98a and detected by a llm-based review [1].

I was not able to actually trigger this potential issue in own
tests, even with only one or two threads available, so it's unclear
if the issue is real or theoretical only.

In details: `ZstdWriteWrap` pushed one task per chunk to a shared
`TaskPool` with no limit on how many could be in flight at once.
Each task blocks until its frame number is next in line to be written,
which relied on the scheduler always giving a worker thread to whichever
pending task happens to be next. TBB's `task_group` gives no such
ordering guarantee, so it was possible for every running worker to be
blocked on a frame that had not been dispatched yet, with none left to
run it, hanging the save indefinitely.

The approach of this PR is to remove the 'write to blendfile' part from
the compressing worker. It also ended up simplifying things a lot,
removing an intermediary struct and several synchronization primitives.

Now, tasks in the pool only perform the compression itself. Gathering
compressed zstd frames and writing them in the correct order in the
blendfile is performed by a new utils, which runs in the main thread as
part of the `write` function.

NOTE: also tried to keep a single background task running dedicated to
gathering and writing all compressed frames as they become available,
while ensuring correct order. It made code somewhat more complicated
(and was painful to get fully reliably working), while ending up
slightly slower than the current PR.

In addition, slightly fixed/improved error handling (returning `false`
from `WriteWrap::close()` was ignored, and the error report generated
was not very helpful, especially in case the `errno` itself was
irrelevant, which often happens in zstd compression case).

Pull Request: https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/pulls/161569

subject: Anim: Convert animation between rotation modes
message:
Anim: Convert animation between rotation modes

This adds code to convert animation from one rotation mode to another.
There are multiple ways to do the conversion:
* Using Ctrl+R in pose mode
* In the 3D viewport, open the "Object" or "Pose" menu, under
"Animation" there is a new entry "Convert Rotation Mode"
* Using the python API `convert_rotation_mode()` either on bones or
objects

**Important Behavior**
* The result of the operation is always a fully keyed rotation, even
if previously only a single channel was keyed. This is the only way
to ensure that the rotations line up.
* Interpolation may not match. In fact it is expected not to.
This is desired for animators for when they are running into gimbal
lock and they just want to try if a different rotation mode works better.
* In case interpolation *has to* match, there is an option to insert
keys on every frame before the conversion.
* key types are somewhat preserved. We assume that for any given
frame, all rotation keys are the same type.
* keys on all related actions are converted, that includes the NLA

Even though the animation data conversion could be triggered
automatically by changes to the rotation_mode RNA property, I chose not
to do that for a reason.
This may be set directly via python in an addon and we shouldn't
include the costly (and maybe unexpected) side effect of converting
animation.

This adds a new operator `anim.rotation_mode_convert` instead of
modifying the existing `pose.rotation_mode_set`.
Since the operator now works with objects as well, it's probably better
to move it out of the `pose` category.
`pose.rotation_mode_set` and `pose.convert_rotation` from rigify are
deprecated with a warning that pops up every time you execute them.

**Implementation**
The core of the changes are in `anim_convert.cc`.

* `convert_to_rotation_mode` is a high level function that converts
the rotation for a single transformable.
* `build_rotation_fcurve_map` and `convert_rotation_keys` are two
functions that work in concert. The first builds the data structure
to quickly find FCurves by their RNA path and the second consumes
that data to do the conversion.
* `bake_rotation_fcurves` utility function to bake FCurves before
converting their rotation.

This uses the `AnimTransformable` class to make this functionality
available to objects and bones at the same time.
When dealing with multiple transformables, we would need to iterate
the action for each to find the FCurves for it.
To avoid that I added `ChannelbagFCurveMap` which is created by
`build_rotation_fcurve_map`.
With that we can easily iterate iterate the FCurves of each Channelbag
sorted by RNA path.

`KeyframeIterator`
Is a new helper class to iterate all frames with keys of N FCurves.

**Deprecates** the existing `POSE_OT_convert_rotation` operator and
removes it from the pose menu.

Resolves #149607
Resolves #159131

Design: #137281

UI improvements will be handled in a separate PR: !159981

subject: Fix #161421: VSE: Off-center origins offset rendered result for reduced output resolutions
message:
Fix #161421: VSE: Off-center origins offset rendered result for reduced output resolutions

Problem was inside `calc_strip_transform_matrix`.

`image_center_offs` was the "distance from the input (image) center to
the output (canvas) center", to be applied as a translation after
scaling. Its purpose was to center the image in the canvas when zero
translation is present.

However, scale would bundle two separate steps: scaling done by the user
_and_ a potentially necessary internal scaling with
`image_scale_factor`, both about the image origin.

These should have been separate. Any internal scaling should always be
about the image center. Otherwise, scaling with `image_scale_factor`
w.r.t. an offset origin moves the image's center in its coordinate
space. As soon as this happens, `image_center_offs` is no longer
correct, and over/undershoots.

I rewrote `calc_strip_transform_matrix` to properly break up the steps
and added lots of documentation.  As part of the fix, I also renamed
some functions which were clear misnomers.

Notably, before, `image_center_offs` was intentionally kept as an
integer to avoid interpolation with zero user translation.
However, I argue that this was the wrong choice -- it meant that we were
introducing positional error whenever the image could not be perfectly
centered, leading to misalignment with the image's bounding box.
Since the updated logic breaks tests, this will be relegated to a future
patch.

subject: VSE: Update scene strip content length when scene changes length
message:
VSE: Update scene strip content length when scene changes length

Part of https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/issues/160377

Fixes: #145521

For scenes (and especially with !140271) it is not unusual for the length
to change. This is not so much a problem for e.g. video and audio files
where we don't expect the length to change during the same Blender
session.

When storing the length of the scene in the strip, updating that length
becomes very tricky. Scenes can be linked, properties can be overriden,
etc. so it's not as simple as adding an RNA update function to the
scene start and end. The solution is to compute the strip length
dynamically for scene strips instead of storing its length in DNA.

So this PR tries another approach: the strip always gets the length from
the scene it references. This ensures that we get the updates "for free"
because everytime the strip needs its length, it gets the right and
up-to-date one.

Changes:
- Implement `content_length()` and related getters and setters that
computes scene strip frame number dynamically. Note: Existing usage of
`Strip::len` in versioning was not changed because `Strip::scene` might
not be valid before linking, see `blendfile_versioning_*` tests.
- Remove 'Update Scene Frame Range' from UI
- Deprecate the operator `SEQUENCER_OT_scene_frame_range_update`.
Using it will log the following in the console:

`WARNING SEQUENCER_OT_scene_frame_range_update is deprecated and will be
removed in 6.0. Operator`

subject: Cycles: HIP-RT: Reduce indirections in the BVH traversal
message:
Cycles: HIP-RT: Reduce indirections in the BVH traversal

This change switches BVH traversal/intersection code from using custom
index arrays that are specific to HIP-RT builder to the general data
arrays that are available on all backends. This is possible since there
are no primitive splitting based on the BVH time steps.

Some functions (like set_intersect_point) still have the same number of
fetches, but some of the fetches are now int and not int2.

Other hot functions (like motion_triangle_custom_intersect) now have
only 2 fetches instead of 4.

subject: Cycles: HIP-RT: Remove BVH steps
message:
Cycles: HIP-RT: Remove BVH steps

The goal of the change is to reduce memory usage and potentially lower
the memory bandwidth in the BVH traversal.

The bandwidth is a bit tricky to predict, as the number of fetches is
probably the same, but of a lower size (int instead of int2). At a very
least it'll be possible to remove duplicated information.

While the core idea of the implementation matches BVH2, there are a few
extra indirection arrays with offset and primitive types.

Having it a more built-in feature to the BVH itself would be much more
preferred, as without it it is quite hard to have good quality BVH with
a low memory footprint.

As for the BVH2, implementing heuristics from the STBVH paper could be
nice. Or, make the inner nodes aware of the time range. However, the
relevance of BVH2 is becoming lower and lower. Perhaps, it is time to
simplify it as well, and fully rely on the good quality HW-RT.

subject: Cycles: HIP-RT: Remove primitive bounds valid check
message:
Cycles: HIP-RT: Remove primitive bounds valid check

These checks would lead into primitive indices mismatch between the
actual BVH state and the objects primitives offset calculation.

It is not currently a problem as the HIP-RT BVH uses its own index
arrays. However, these arrays do require extra memory, and could
lead to extra fetch indirections from the BVH traversal.

The need of these checks is not really clear, and it doesn't seem that
other backends perform them. These checks exists from the beginning of
the HIP-RT integration.

The reasoning for the curves control points check is also unclear,
and it would be good to have an example where it is actually needed
and know what problem it solves. Is it some sort of memory optimization
or was it intended to solve numerical intersection problem.

subject: Cycles: HIP-RT: Skip visibility check for primitives
message:
Cycles: HIP-RT: Skip visibility check for primitives

HIP-RT handles visibility at the TLAS instance level, and the motion
triangle intersection was using software intersect that accesses the
visibility flag, which is redundant. Curve and point primitives were
fully relying on the instance visibility mask.

The change allows to free the prim_visibility array once the BVH build
is finished, to save up GPU memory. This is not done as part of this
commit as there seems to be more arrays that are only needed during the
build process. It would be easier to have a dedicated patch for this.

subject: Fix #160815: Core: Saving creates excessive threads
message:
Fix #160815: Core: Saving creates excessive threads

`ZstdWriteWrap::write` calls `BLI_threadpool_insert` once per chunk.
`BLI_threadpool_insert` calls `pthread_create`. `BLI_threadpool_remove`
joins it after. A typical file save calls `write` hundreds of times,
creating and destroying a thread for each chunk.

The intent is to multithread saving but the problem
is `BLI_threadpool` doesn't reuse threads as described above.

Replace with `BLI_task_pool`. This pushes one task per chunk and run on
the existing thread pool. No extra thread created.

With 12 cores on tree_creature_v2.blend:
| |  `strace -c -e trace=clone3` |
|-|---|
| Before | ~1260 |
| After | 16 (all startup threads) |

Tested saving scenes in blender-benchmark. All pass.

subject: Fix several potential errors when reading corrupted DNA data.
message:
Fix several potential errors when reading corrupted DNA data.

This commit improves handling of reading corrupted DNA data by erroring
(and aborting) when:
* Some array size value is invalid (negative, or way too big).
* The raw SDNA buffer is read beyond its declared size (could happen e.g.
  from an invalid `members_num`, `types_num` or `structs_num` value).
* A `SDNA_Struct::type_index` is not in the valid range.
* A `SDNA_StructMember::type_index` or `SDNA_StructMember::member_index`
  is not in the valid range.

These changes should prevent any out-of-bound access in the DNA raw
buffer, and in general detect way more issues (data corruption) than
before.

It also refactors the 17 years old 'gravity [3]' issue (#20330) fix to be
a bit more secure and deterministic, and avoid an extra loop over the
whole array of structs.

Fix #161338: Crash rendering empty subdivided mesh in Cycles

Cycles could crash while tessellating an empty mesh with subdivision enabled.

subject: Fix #161299: GPU: Crash using certain custom Python shaders
message:
Fix #161299: GPU: Crash using certain custom Python shaders

The crash was caused by the shader convertion step
wrongly using the BSL grammar parser in `shared` variables
conversion stage.

This parser mandates the use of braces after a `if` or `else`
statements. If the given shader source fails this check it would
create an error and result in null output string. This would
create a crash when trying to be compiled.

Instead, rely on the `DummyParser` which doesn't do grammar parsing
and still allow the needed transformation.

Also, instead of crash, try to make the
compilation fail and print an error to
the console if we ever emit one.

subject: Fix #160310: VSE: Strip animations don't play in sequencer-type scene strips
message:
Fix #160310: VSE: Strip animations don't play in sequencer-type scene strips

This problem was originally resolved in 2019 with a372e5e426, by calling
`BKE_animsys_evaluate_all_animation` when recursing into these strips.
This worked at the time because it would iterate `main->scenes.first`
and evaluate each scene's animdata including strip animation.

However, it still did not fix it for prefetching, which uses a separate
`bmain_eval`.

In 2025 with bd61e69be5a, the scene animdata evaluation was removed
inside of `BKE_animsys_evaluate_all_animation` which broke things again
for the non-prefetch case.

"Sync Scene Time" happens to fix it because it forces playback in the
nested sequencer scene, which triggers animation evaluation.

Fix for both prefetch and non-prefetch by just evaluating the scene we
are about to recurse into. We no longer need to evaluate _all_
animation, e.g. masks do their own `BKE_animsys_evaluate_animdata` in
`seq_render_mask` and other datablocks are dealt with similarly. The
function was only ever used in this one edge-case, so we can remove it.

There is one case that existing code does not cover: animation of
compositor node trees inside the nested sequencer-type scene strip.
This would require some more work, and can be deferred for a future 5.2
backport patch once there is a better plan for how to tackle evaluation
in this case.

subject: Fix #161263: Handle empty bundle lists in Geometry Nodes
message:
Fix #161263: Handle empty bundle lists in Geometry Nodes

Empty bundle lists stored with `SingleData::ForDefaultValue` could still
behave as if they had one value during list iteration. This caused
viewer logging to call `ensure_owns_direct_data()` on the default null
`BundlePtr`, which then asserted in `ensure_mutable_inplace()`.

Fix this by making `List<T>::foreach` and `foreach_for_write` return
early for zero-sized lists. `SingleData` can store one value shared by
all logical list elements, but when the logical list size is zero, that
storage is only a placeholder and should not be visited.

Null bundle pointers are also treated as trivially owning their data,
since they do not reference any nested data.

The regression test also exposed an existing memory leak in
`SingleImplicitSharingData`. The stored default value was destructed,
but its separately allocated storage was not freed. Free that storage
during cleanup as well.

A regression test was added for `SocketValueVariant::ensure_owns_direct_data()`
on an empty bundle list.

subject: Fix: VSE: Clear cache of seq-input scene strips when modifying their contents
message:
Fix: VSE: Clear cache of seq-input scene strips when modifying their contents

Previously, scene strips would only be invalidated if datablocks inside
the scene they were pointing to were changed. They would not clear cache
if the scene itself changed (as with strip changes).

Fix by including the case of `ID_RECALC_SEQUENCER_STRIPS` when deciding
whether to invalidate.

Also replace the `ELEM` ignore check with a bitwise check. Before, we
would only ignore invalidation if `id->recalc` matched exactly, and
could slip through if extra flags were present, causing unnecessary
cache clears. Now, only ignore if removing all of those flags would
result in an empty `id->recalc`.

subject: Fix: VSE: Cannot prefetch sequencer-input scene strips
message:
Fix: VSE: Cannot prefetch sequencer-input scene strips

Previously, sequencer-input scene strips would never pass the step of
recursing into its contents. This was a bug and addressed in !160637.
But now that they pass through, they are checked to see if they are a
"scene strip" and since they technically are, they are ignored.

While fixing this I found many other bugs we don't cover, so I decided
to just rewrite the entire check. For one, `relations_render_loop_check`
is being improperly used here: it should only be checking for recursion
of effects but we're using it for our scene check. This is also the only
reason why we were using the cumbersome `query_scene_strips`.

Instead, do mutual recursion over a seqbase, strips inside, and any
seqbases they may reference. This is hopefully easier to understand and
more logically consistent, fixing many bugs.

This fixes two related issues:

1. System files could be replaced when downloading assets. A malicious

   specific assets are downloaded. This was dangerous, because the
   listing downloader performs various safety checks while the asset

   that would potentially overwrite a 'system file' (listing file, file
   hash database, those kind of files).
2. Converting asset paths from the listing to a relative path, so they

   thorough. It now also properly handles Windows paths that are

subject: Fix #161015: Serialize geometry and bundle lists in bake data
message:
Fix #161015: Serialize geometry and bundle lists in bake data

Baking the experimental Cloth Simulation modifier could hit an assertion in
`serialize_list()`.

The cloth bake state can contain nested lists of values such as geometry sets,
bundles, and strings. These are valid runtime bake values, but the bake
serializer only handled primitive custom-data lists and `SocketValueVariant`
lists. This caused lists such as `GList<GeometrySet>`, `GList<BundlePtr>`, and
`GList<std::string>` to fall through to the custom-data type path, where no
matching data type exists.

The fix adds explicit serialization and deserialization support for those list
types. They are written as regular bake values instead of custom-data blobs,
matching how the individual value types are already serialized.

A regression test was added for round-tripping a nested bundle containing
geometry, bundle, and string lists.

subject: Fix #160091: Remember active attribute by name during BMesh conversion
message:
Fix #160091: Remember active attribute by name during BMesh conversion

Converting meshes between Mesh and BMesh  changes the attribute layers, because some things that are attributes in Mesh are part of the BMesh data (for example  the `sharp_face` attribute) and don't exist as an attribute in BMesh. This changes the number and order of the attribute layers.

Because `Mesh.attributes_active_index` is an (integer) index in the layers we need to remember the active attribute by name and set it again after the conversion.

This is a bit of a stopgap fix , eventually we want to store the active_attribute as a name , but that would need an incompatible change to the .blend format so we postpone that the next major release.

subject: Compositor: Fallback to group output if no viewer exists
message:
Compositor: Fallback to group output if no viewer exists

This patch makes it such that the compositor falls back to the group
output node result if the viewer output was needed but no viewer node
actually exists. So the final mechanism is: Find a viewer node in the
active compute context, if none exists, find a viewer node in the base
compute context, if none exists, fallback to the group output node.

The default node tree was changed to not include a viewer node, since it
is now useless by default.

This is needed as a prerequisite to the Layered Compositor project,
since we can't expect the user to insert viewer nodes in modifiers.

Implementation-wise, all front-ends were unified to use the same
mechanism and implementation, instead of relying on special behavior for
the viewport and sequencer compositor where the group output was treated
as a viewer in the scheduler.

Resolves the first point of #108656.

Fix #160212: 5.2 files with nodes with pixel subtype interface crash in 5.1

Opening a blend file with node tree socket interface of subtype Pixel
crashes in 5.1 and earlier.
Also, sockets of built-in nodes with `Pixel` subtype show as Undefined
in 5.1

The crash happens on the UI drawing level in geometry nodes and during
evaluation for the compositor. Although the blend file reading code can
handle undefined subtypes, other parts of the code assume valid socket
data.

The commit contains two fixes
1. Fix crash by replacing the `Pixel` subtype with `None` during writing
time and restoring the `Pixel` subtype during reading again.
2. Fix undefined node sockets by replacing the `Pixel` subtype with
`None` at write time. Unlike interface sockets, the subtype gets
restored automatically at read time through
`socket_decl.update_or_build()` called by `node_verify_sockets()`

subject: UI: Add new status icons
message:
UI: Add new status icons

Currently, all errors and warnings labels use the same "error" icon.

This leads to warning-looking labels that are actually errors,
and users/devs missing a way to show something it's an actual error.

Additionally, the Info Editor icon is being used for info labels, which
can be confusing as well, and if one day the editor icon changes,
it will make all existing labels look different.

Add new status icons, with a `STATUS_` prefix. That way, existing usage
of the old icons won't be affected.

The icons are:

* STATUS_ERROR
* STATUS_ERROR_FILLED
* STATUS_INFO
* STATUS_INFO_FILLED
* STATUS_WARNING
* STATUS_WARNING_FILLED

The "filled" variant is for when extra contrast is required, or when a
button/label is active.

Make these icons available in Blender 5.2 LTS, so later add-ons that
make use of these new icons can be compatible with 5.2.

No user-facing change is expected.

See !161002 for details and screenshots.

subject: Fix #158621: Asset library sometimes crashes on file reload
message:
Fix #158621: Asset library sometimes crashes on file reload

Even though rebuilding the asset catalog service was mutex-protected
(most importantly in `AllAssetLibrary::rebuild_catalogs_from_nested()`),
reading it to build the catalog tree wasn't. The asset browser catalog
tree building may obtain a reference to the catalog service and trigger
rebuilding of the catalog tree - if necessary. Meanwhile the catalog
service rebuilding may free the service.

The solution here is to use a shared pointer, so that the UI can keep
the catalog service alive for as long as it's working on it, even while
the catalog service rebuilding replaces it inside the asset system. The
UI will receive the new catalog service and it's catalog tree on the
next redraw still.

subject: Build: Remove CMake blender_project_hack_pre/post macros
message:
Build: Remove CMake blender_project_hack_pre/post macros

This commit removes blender_project_hack_pre/post macros from our root
CMakeLists.txt, which were used to hackily swap O3 optimization flags
to O2 in the C/CXX release flags.

In addition to this, this commit moves the macros.cmake `include`
statement below the main `project(Blender)` statement. This then allows
the macros.cmake logic to be executed within the environment set by the
`project()` call. For example, in the case of cross-compiled builds, this
then allows using the proper target defines by respecting the optionally
provided CMake toolchain file loaded by `project()`.

This commit also highlighted an issue that the previous O2 flag was
masking in Cycles. Where the Scene::create_light_node() templated
function lacked explicit template instantiations for use outside of
its TU (in cycles/blender/geometry.cpp and light.cpp) causing linking
error on Linux x64.

Fixed by adding the missing explicit template instantiation statements
at the bottom of cycles/blender/scene.cpp, similarly to what is done in
cycles/utils/colorspace.cpp for ColorSpaceManager::to_scene_linear().

subject: Fix #160915: Avoid field structure on non-field sockets
message:
Fix #160915: Avoid field structure on non-field sockets

Socket structure inference could assign field structure to sockets whose type
does not support fields.

In the reported file, a Geometry Switch output depended on a field condition.
Because the output structure dependency also included that condition, merging
the dependencies could infer `StructureType::Field` and assign it to a Geometry
output socket. From there it propagated through the group and caused the Curve
to Tube geometry output to be displayed/inferred incorrectly.

The fix normalizes inferred structure types for the socket type before storing
them. Unsupported socket types remain single values, while field-supported value
sockets can still infer fields normally.

Regression tests were added for non-field socket types and to make sure field
inference still works for supported value sockets.

subject: Vulkan: Reuse memory when using assign_if_different
message:
Vulkan: Reuse memory when using assign_if_different

When submitting commands to Vulkan the viewports and scissors are
compared with the last command. When different the viewport and scissor
commands are send to the GPU driver. For this the `assign_if_different`
template was used.

This template wasn't developed for complex types and callers were forced
to perform a copy and this copy could then be moved. This isn't a
bottleneck when working with flags or counters.

When used with complex struct the copy was always created, passed to the
function and destroyed after calling the function. In larger scenes this
could be found when profiling. This has now be worked around by using
copy-assign operator.

subject: Vulkan: Inline construction of draw nodes data
message:
Vulkan: Inline construction of draw nodes data

In large scenes many drawing nodes are added to vulkans' render graph.
Each drawing node contains many data, that was copied (and freed) along
the way.

This PR reduces the copy/free overhead by first allocate the space for
the node inside the render graph and let the caller fill the data. When
that is done the caller can finalize the node that will do the rest of
the process.

Other nodes could be added to this mechanism as well, however they don't
have benefits due to their leaner used structures. Also some nodes will
not benefit at all and still require to do the copy-ing, only in a different
location.

See PR for performance figures.

subject: Fix #156442: VSE sequence detection fails with 11 consecutive numbers
message:
Fix #156442: VSE sequence detection fails with 11 consecutive numbers

Caused/exposed by 5a0c0826b709

Both sequence detection (`ImageFrame` in `ImageFrameRange` has
wrong filenumber) as well as path handling (string for the filename gets
filled with '#') have issues, this PR concentrates on the path handling

Path handling is a combination of `BLI_path_frame_get`,
`BLI_path_frame_strip` (and `BLI_path_frame`) and we could run into the
situation (with more than 11 consecutive numbers in the filename) that:
- `BLI_path_frame_get` would return a garbage frame number (uses
`atoi()` which can only fit into integers)
- `BLI_path_frame_strip` would still replace the invalid "frame number
part" with '#'
- `BLI_path_frame` would the write zeros

So to resolve, make
- `BLI_path_frame_get` return false if it does not find a framenumber
which fits into an integer
- `BLI_path_frame_strip` do nothing if it does not find a framenumber
which fits into an integer
(doing this will keep the filename which is what we want in this case)

subject: Re-enable multi-bind and OpenGL texture pool on supported Intel GPUs
message:
Re-enable multi-bind and OpenGL texture pool on supported Intel GPUs

In `detect_workarounds` of the OpenGL backend, two workarounds were
used on Intel GPUs:
- `GLContext::multi_bind_image_support = false`
- `GCaps.texture_pool_workaround = true`

For the former, I re-confirmed that, when rendering the reproducer from
#120273 with the OpenGL backend and multi_bind_image_support
re-enabled:
- The visual corruptions are visible a Intel Gen8 Processor iGPU with
  driver version 101.2141.
- The issue is NOT visible on a Meteor Lake iGPU with driver version
  101.5972.

Thus, multi-bind was re-enabled for drivers with version >= 101.5972.

For the latter, issues with `glTexturePool` were fixed in drivers with a
version >= 101.8801 on Intel Xe2+ GPUs.
Thus, the general enablement of the workaround from
https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/pulls/152033 is undone by
adding a driver version check and reusing the Intel GPU architecture
check previously introduced for the same use case in the Vulkan backend.
For this, a new function `BLI_windows_get_directx_intel_driver_info`
is added for querying the device driver version and device ID.
This function works similar to `BLI_windows_get_directx_driver_version`
used for Qualcomm GPUs, but uses the device LUID for unique device
matching and parses the DXGI User Mode Driver (UMD) version in the
format used for Intel GPU driver versioning.

all subprojects independently download dependency source code. In

that do not inherit this setting, causing them to still attempt

subject: Fix: Invalid ID name uniqueness code handling of ID name removal.
message:
Fix: Invalid ID name uniqueness code handling of ID name removal.

Specifically, when removing an ID name from the 'global' map, code would
incorrectly consider its numeric suffix as unused, which was not true in
case the same ID name was still used by other IDs in other namespaces
(typically, from different libraries).

reference, since numeric suffixes that should have been considered as
used were now marked as unused.

This could lead to generating several IDs in the same namespace with
the same name.

Affected e.g. the liboverride code, which generates globally unique
names for liboverrides IDs when the exact reference ID names cannot be
used as-is.

subject: Fix #160570: macOS: Broken window drawing on fullscreen window restoration
message:
Fix #160570: macOS: Broken window drawing on fullscreen window restoration

When Blender was opened with a fullscreen window, either by starting
Blender with the `--window-fullscreen` CLI option or by using a
startup.blender that was saved as fullscreen, window drawing would be
slightly broken and drawn out of bound until framebuffer drawn size was
refreshed. When using the macOS Stage Manager, the problem would be

subject: Fix #158751: JPEG export fails with long CryptoMatte manifests
message:
Fix #158751: JPEG export fails with long CryptoMatte manifests

When writing JPEG files with long CryptoMatte manifests, where long is
defined as bigger than 65533 bytes, the file is not written and only a
single error message reading "Bogus marker length" is outputted.

This happens because libjpeg hardcodes a maximum marker length of 65533
and raises an error if we try to write a marker exceeding that length.
Raising the error then calls our `jpeg_error` callback which performs a
longjmp to reset the state of the process to whatever it was set to
before trying to write the file so nothing is written to disk, and no
other error message is printed.

As we do not really support reading CryptoMatte manifests from JPEG
files, and since the manifests (and other comments) are prefixed with
"Blender:" (which implies that they may not be useful for other
programs), to fix this, simply write the data truncated to the maximum
allowed marker length. This also prints a warning that some data is
written truncated.

Fix #160259: Edge slide acts differently when camera is inside a mesh

Sliding an edge when a camera is inside the mesh
only had a vertical component to the slide even though

sliding between how one would naturally expect the edge to
slide.

to prevent the ray from shooting behind the camera.

Fix #160754: Images pasted from Windows snipping tool are offset

The in memory DIBv5 format that many Windows applications use when
posting images to the clipboard is woefully mis-implemented across the
ecosystem. Of particular interest here are the 12 bytes used for the RGB
masks (but not the Alpha mask).  The v5 structure includes these masks
as fields in the header proper. But legacy versions (before v4 I think)
included such things after the end of their headers.  Seems like various
applications kind of write both(?) now and we now have to account for
those applications out in the wild.

Perform a size check to see if we are exactly 12 bytes off and skip them
if so.

subject: Cycles: Use identity motion transforms to avoid numerical inaccuracies
message:
Cycles: Use identity motion transforms to avoid numerical inaccuracies

When no motion is present for an object, it is expected that motion
vectors should be zero.
When `ob->use_motion()` and `flag & SD_OBJECT_HAS_VERTEX_MOTION` are
both false, `tfm_pre`/`tfm_post` and `itfm` are inverse matrices.
Due to numerical inaccuracies, this will not exactly result in an
identity matrix. This can lead to motion vectors with entries of an
order of 1e-4 even in completely static scenes.
This issue is avoided by setting `tfm_pre` and `tfm_post` directly to
`transform_identity()` in such a case.

subject: Fix #159001: Remote Asset Library duplicate assets after refresh
message:
Fix #159001: Remote Asset Library duplicate assets after refresh

When refreshing a remote asset library, already downloaded assets would
appear twice on Windows, with one being the downloaded version and the
other being the remote version.

This was because when checking if an asset had already been downloaded,
`filelist_readjob_remote_asset_library_index_read` constructed a
library-relative identifier with the path from
`OnlineAssetInfo::asset_file()`. But as relative identifiers use native
slashes and `asset_file()` uses forward slashes, the relative identifier
wouldn't match the one of the already downloaded asset on Windows, which
caused the remote asset to be listed even when already downloaded.

Fixed by converting the returned path to native slashes before using it
to look for a downloaded asset.

subject: Fix #159699: Cycles texture cache seam with light tree and environment
message:
Fix #159699: Cycles texture cache seam with light tree and environment

The problem was that next event estimation and forward sampling did not
have the same ray differential, which caused differnet mip level
selection. For multiple importance both of these need to converge to the
exact same result. The visible seam is especially an issue when there
are some discontinuous decision in sampling like the tree.

For forward sampling, previously it used the roughness of the sampled
BSDF. Instead we now use a weighted average of roughness that depends on
the direction and can be computed for both cases, as well as path guiding.

It uses the MIS weights for the weighted average, to ensure a mix of
sharp specular BSDFs and diffuse BDFs still gives a fixed differential
per direction that is suitable for both. MIS weights for sharp BSDFs
will be high in the reflection directions, while in other directions
the diffuse BSDF roughness will dominate.

Computing this weighted average roughness has some overhead. It may be
beneficial for the texture cache, as each direction will now only need
a single mip level instead of multiple.

subject: Fix: Cycles: Mismatch between world importance map and mipmap resolution
message:
Fix: Cycles: Mismatch between world importance map and mipmap resolution

When the texture cache evaluates the background shader at a low mipmap level
for next event estimation, it can hit a bright pixel from e.g. very bright
blurred. But in the importance map generated at a higher resolution, the
corresponding pixels may not be bright at all and get a low importance
sampling probability. This leads to significant noise.

To avoid this, clamp the ray differentials so they are at least the ray
differentials used for generating the importance map. This both reduces
noise and mipmap bias. It comes at some extra memory cost, but the
importance map resolution is limited by default and overall it's worth it.

subject: Fix: Color Management: sRGB detection wrong for different working spaces
message:
Fix: Color Management: sRGB detection wrong for different working spaces

It was checking if there is an sRGB transform relative to scene linear,
rather than if the colorspace is absolute sRGB.

This was missed because the implications are subtle.

* Wrong handling of "sRGB Encoded AP1" colorspace with ACEScg working
  space. This colorspace was added to the default config in Blender 5.2.
* Missing sRGB colorspace tags in USD / MaterialX export with ACEScg
  working space. This affected one Storm test, which now matches the
  Cycles render more closely and is consistent between USD and Hydra.
* Missed optimizations in painting code for sRGB images and working
  spaces other than Linear Rec.709.
* For GPU textures stored as sRGB it was actually the correct check,
  and for this case we specifically check that it's both sRGB and the
  working space is Linear Rec.709.

The code was simplified to use interop IDs rather than evaluating the
transform at various sample points, which can be expensive. This is the
right mechanism for I/O. For optimizations it should be fine too as we
have interop ID detection heuristics for older configs while newer
configs should contain interop IDs.

subject: Fix #160306: Field Variance node outputs wrong standard deviation and variance
message:
Fix #160306: Field Variance node outputs wrong standard deviation and variance

The standard deviation and variance returned by the Field Variance node
are different than the ones returned by the Attribute Statistic node
when input values are the same. This happens only when the Field
Variance node's "Group ID" field socket has a single value for all
elements (i.e. `VArray::is_single()` returns true).

In this configuration, the sum of squared differences used to compute
the standard deviation in the Field Variance node is computed using
`std::reduce`. The callback passed to it has signature
`(accumulator, value)`.

However, `std::reduce` does not consider the first argument of the
passed callback as the accumulator. Rather, it computes
`callback(value1, value2)` and puts the result back in the group for
further processing. An implementation could be:

```
a = callback(values[0], values[2]);
b = callback(values[1], values[3]);
c = callback(a, b);
init = callback(init, c);
```

where `init` is the initial value of the reduction passed as argument.
Note that this is the actual implementation in GlibC.

To properly compute the sum of differences required for the standard
deviation computation we should instead use `std::accumulate` which
does not pass intermediate results back to the callback.

As this bug has been present since the node was added in Blender 4.5,
existing files depending on the current behavior will break.

subject: Fix: Geometry Nodes: crash when evaluating NaN field
message:
Fix: Geometry Nodes: crash when evaluating NaN field

It's fairly easy to generate NaN values with math nodes when trying. Currently,
the field evaluation crashes in this case because it uses a hash table to
deduplicate fields and NaN values never compare equal to themselves.

The implemented fix is to slightly modify `operator==` for `GFieldRef` such that
it returns true when two fields reference exactly the same underlying value.

Overall, I'm not entirely happy with having this inconcistency but it's the
simplest way to fix this right now. Alternatives are:
* Change `DefaultEquality` and `DefaultHash` such that all NaN values compare
  equal to each other (instead of never comparing equal). While this would
  generally be better for use of NaN in hash tables, it has some downsides. It
  would be quite a significant change that also makes things slower in the
  common case. Usually NaN values should be prevented at the source.
* Always replace NaN values with a fallback value like 0 when immediately when
  they are produced (with with a divide node). This also makes the common case
  slower, especially because it also makes vectorization harder.
* Have a separate field comparison function for use in hash tables. That could
  generally work too. Right now it would mean a bunch of code duplication that
  doesn't seem necessary. This could be done in the future though if there are
  cases where the newly implemented behavior is causing problems.

This also adds a regression test that evaluates a field which has a NaN value.

subject: Compositor: Improve GPU playback performance
message:
Compositor: Improve GPU playback performance

This patch improves the GPU playback performance, particularly for
playing back EXR sequences. This is done by essentially disallowing
canceling frames already scheduled for execution, allowing the GPU to
more optimally pipeline and schedule compositor work. This almost
doubles the performance of playing 4k DWAB sequences:

| State | FPS | EXR Reading Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 6.5 | 59ms |
| Avoid Copies (!160267) | 8 | 59ms |
| All Above + Non-Cancelable (This PR) | 14.5 | 59ms |
| All Above + Half Float Loading | 19 | 45ms |
| All Above + Memory Mapped Files | 19 | 45ms |

This obviously comes at the cost of not being able to do intra-frame
canceling, but we still allow inter-frame canceling. But if the user is
playing back using the compositor, then it arguably runs in a reasonable
time, and support canceling is not necessary considering the cost.

subject: Core: Increase maximum number of open file handles
message:
Core: Increase maximum number of open file handles

On Windows and macOS, the default maximum number of stdio file handles
is 512 and 256 respectively. On Linux it's usually some very high
number. This increases that limit on startup to 8192, to better handle
some production files and have more uniform limits across platforms.
This is commonly done in VFX software.

Some code in Blender keeps file handles open for a long time,
particularly the Cycles texture cache and Alembic cache file datablocks.
This helps improve performance when reading tiles or frames on demand,
without having to reopen the file each time.

Cycles limits itself to 128 file handles, but there is no limit on cache
file datablocks. The production file in #160383 has 480 open file
handles for Alembic, so it was already near the limit on Windows, and
then a few more pushed it over.

By increasing the limit, at a minimum all production files that worked
before should continue to work when enabling the texture cache.
Improving the cache file datablock to use fewer handles is left for
another time.

Fix #160383: Cycles texture missing images in production file

RNA: Exposes the internal undo structures to the python read API

Add RNA types UndoStack and UndoStep, accessible via
bpy.context.window_manager.undo_stack. This allows
scripts and add-ons to inspect the undo history without
modifying it.

Each UndoStep exposes a name, type name, and skip flag.
The UndoStack provides the collection of steps and the
index of the currently active step.

This is useful for building custom undo history panels,
debugging undo behavior in add-ons, or displaying undo
state in user-facing tools.

Technical notes:

A new file rna_wm_undo.cc defines the UndoStep and
UndoStack structs. The stack is retrieved from the
wmWindowManager's existing undo_stack pointer. All
properties are read-only. The undo history operator
tooltip in ed_undo.cc is also updated to more accurately
describe its behavior.

subject: BLO: add callback to customize how structs are written
message:
BLO: add callback to customize how structs are written

This adds a new callback to all the `BlendWriter::write_*` methods. The callback
can be used to tag e.g. runtime pointers and potentially generated pointers in
the struct. This allows modifying a shallow copy of the struct before it is
written to a file or undo step.

This makes it possible to more precisely specify which pointers need to be
remapped to stable pointers for undo, to avoid performance issues when all
pointers are attempted to be remapped. Additionally, this will also help with
making the .blend file format more stable by making it easier to override
runtime data before writing.

The API is intentionally declarative, i.e. it specifies the meaning of some
struct members, but leaves the actual data modification contained in the
implementation. Maybe this kind of declarative api does not work for all kinds
of modifications we might want to do, but whenever possible, this seems better.

This kind of API was already mentioned in #151842.

subject: Fix #160055: un-subdivide creating duplicate faces
message:
Fix #160055: un-subdivide creating duplicate faces

Resolve errors where unsubdivide would create duplicate faces.

- Fix the existing face check which passed in unordered
  vertices to BM_face_exists.

- Fix BM_face_exists_multi_edge to take an unordered set of edges
  so it worked as documented

- Fix creation of duplicate faces from splitting off face-ears,
  where duplicates faces may already exist - or where splitting
  off multiple ears could create duplicates between them.

- Fix errors where vertices besides the vertex being
  dissolved would be removed.

  - A "vertex-chain" between two faces would join the faces
    and remove all vertices and edges between them.
    Now the vertex and the two adjacent edges are merged into one,
    matching the behavior of wire edge-chains.
  - When a boundary vertex dissolved into an edge that already
    had a connected face, it was possible dissolve would dissolve
    this edge too - removing vertices besides the vertex being dissolved.

  In both cases it was possible the main dissolve loop would iterate
  over freed vertices. In practice this probably didn't cause issues
  in relate builds because the BLI_mempool memory wasn't used to create
  new vertices - and is still allocated by Blender.
  Nevertheless this asserted with ASAN and is bad practice to
  rely on the content of freed vertices during iteration.

  Now only the vertices being dissolved will be removed when
  un-subdividing.

Add public functions:

- BM_face_split_check_double_face
- BM_face_pair_overlap_check_subset_{same,swap}_winding
- BM_face_exists_subset_from_face

Also fix BM_face_exists_multi_edge which didn't work on an unordered
set of edges (as documented), it didn't cause problems but was needed
for duplicate face detection.

Update test data since a cube now un-subdivides into a tetrahedron
instead of collapsing into single triangle.

Ref !160375

Fix #160029: Crash adding UV layer after converting attributes

Regression in [0] meant converting the active UV map to a vertex
group then adding a new UV map caused an out-of-bounds read
in AttributeStorage::lookup.

Vertex groups share the attribute namespace,
so an attribute can't be added with a name that matches a vertex group.
BKE_attribute_calc_unique_name didn't account for this,
so the name generated for the new UV map collided with the vertex group,
the attribute was never added,
and ED_mesh_uv_add returned a stale index.

Prevent collisions with vertex group names in
BKE_attribute_calc_unique_name.

Also convert attributes using BKE_attribute_remove instead of the
raw accessor, so the active UV map and color attribute stay valid
(matching the remove operator).

subject: Core: Harden IDProps against too-high embedding depth.
message:
Core: Harden IDProps against too-high embedding depth.

IDProperties can be embedded into one-another with no theoritical depth
limit, however the code currently uses recursive patterns to process
them, which means beyond a certain depth it will run out of stack memory
and crash.

While we cannot really prevent creating such insanely high data depth,
this commit adds several safe-guards (readfile, writefile, foreach_id,
and freeing processes), skipping further processing beyond a certain
recursion depth (currently set at 1024, which should be both well
within safety margins of any modern OS, and more than enough for any
practical use-case).

Issue initially reported by Ray Molenkemp (@lazydodo), thanks.

This commit also contains a small refactor for the IDProperty freeing
code (and IDP array resize internal logic), essentially removing public
API to free IDProperties' content - all of its usages was immediately
after calling MEM_delete on the same root properties, so can as well
call directly IDP_FreeProperty.

Finally, it fixes a potential bug related to arrays of groups freeing,
where the 'do_id_user' option was not properly propagated through the
array resize logic. Probably not an issue in practice though (not sure
if arrays of groups are used anywhere currently?).

subject: Geometry Nodes: New grid sampling kernel functions
message:
Geometry Nodes: New grid sampling kernel functions

This adds a unified set of "grid samplers" based on kernel functions
that improve and extend the grid sampling options. They are a
prerequisite for future physics simulations and point rasterization.

"Kernels" are one-dimensional functions. This patch also adds a unified
method for constructing a 3D sampling function from such 1D kernels.

Apart from the existing constant ("nearest"), linear, and quadratic
sampling options this adds a new cubic B-spline kernel.

Quadratic and cubic sampling kernels have continuous derivatives, which
is important for future physics simulations that use the gradient of a
velocity grid to compute local deformation and generate forces.

Also fixes incorrect sampling of the `openvdb::QuadraticSampler` whose
weight function needs to be shifted and offset, otherwise it leads
to asymmetric influence of the neighboring grid nodes and negative
weights on one side. The new quadratic sampler handles this internally
to make the use of samplers consistent in the sampling node.

subject: Fix: Animation playback buttons get confused when mouse is not moved
message:
Fix: Animation playback buttons get confused when mouse is not moved

Fix an issue where repeated clicks on the 'Reverse Playback' button
could actually trigger normal playback instead.

This also introduces a new operator `screen.animation_pause`, which
always ensures animation playback is paused (regardless of whether it is
currently playing). Before, the Pause button used the
`screen.animation_play` operator, which toggles playing/paused state.

The bug was caused by a few connected parts:

- The active button under the mouse is stored & restored between
  redraws, so that the correct button is kept highlighted (among other
  things). This storing & restoring is done based on the operator's
  idname.
- Since during playback the "Pause" button takes the place of the
  "Reverse Playback" and "Normal Playback" buttons, and before this fix
  these were all three the same operator, Blender would get confused and
  mark the wrong button as the active one, triggering the normal
  playback instead of the reverse.

The conditions:
- Set the Playback Loop Mode to Stop at End.
- Don't move the mouse while going through these steps.
- Click 'Reverse Playback'.
- The playback buttons are replaced with a big 'Pause' button.
- When playback stops, the 'Pause' button is replaced again with the
  'Reverse'/'Normal' buttons.
- Clicking 'Reverse Playback' button would now trigger the normal
  playback.

This is resolved by making the 'Pause' button its own operator, and by
emitting a fake mouse movement event whenever playback is
started/stopped. Both are necessary for this fix.

subject: Geometry Nodes: Grid topology boolean node
message:
Geometry Nodes: Grid topology boolean node

Boolean combination of grid topology. The result is a grid with active
voxels or tiles where at least one of the input grids has an active
voxel, depending on mode. This combines grids in index space, all grids
should have the same transform.

Supports different boolean combination modes:
- Intersection: creates active voxels where _all_ input grids have
  active voxels.
- Union: creates active voxels where _any_ input grid has an active
  voxel.
- Difference: creates active voxel where the first input grid is active
  but none of the secondary input grids are active.

The value of the output grid voxels is based on the first input grid
and discards values of any secondary grids. In _Union_ mode any voxels
that are not active in the first grid are initialized with its
background value.

subject: Compositor: Add playback cache
message:
Compositor: Add playback cache

This patch adds support for frame animation playback caching in the
compositor. There is now a Frame Cache option in the side bar, when
enabled, the compositor will cache its final viewer result across
frames. The cache is drawn in the timeline editor with a new display
option for that cache. The cache is invalidated on any change that
affects the node tree. The cache respects the memory cache limit and
will evict cached frames in the limit was surpassed. This caching
mechanism only concerns the interactive compositor, not the viewport
compositor or the VSE compositors.

A few changes were made to support this patch:

- A new DEG_id_is_user_modified query function was added to detect if an
  ID changed due to user input or not. This is used to do proper cached
  invalidation. Thanks to Brecht for the implementation.
- The compositor job now internally suspends animation playback until
  the compositor is done to make sure the entire frame range is computed
  and cached. The previous behavior of frame dropping can still be
  achieved using the playback frame dropping option.

subject: Refactor: Avoid superfluous copying in image GPU code
message:
Refactor: Avoid superfluous copying in image GPU code

This patch refactors the imb_gpu_get_data function responsible for
getting the data that will be uploaded to GPU textures for images. The
main motivation is to avoid superfluous copying in multiple places where
this happens:

- The use of float_data_for_write and byte_data_for_write could create a
  copy of the data even though no writes actually take place. Those
  functions are used because proper const correctness is not followed.
  To streamline this situation, raw memory allocations were avoided and
  the ImBuf API was used throughout, minting proper const correctness
  and allowing the use of the read-only float_data and byte_data
  members.
- Calls to functions like IMB_colormanagement_imbuf_to_byte_texture
  essentially did an unnecessary copy if premultiplication was not
  needed. So guarding conditions that check if premultiplication is
  actually needed were added.
- Comments were added and clarified throughout the function.
- The function interface was adjusted to remove redundant return
  arguments since we now return an entire ImBuf.

This improves image loading performance in the compositor and
potentially other areas.

mesh modifier stack is quite convoluted. For example, we keep removing

subject: Fix #160092: Fluid sim free_all operator causes crash
message:
Fix #160092: Fluid sim free_all operator causes crash

The `fluid.free_all` operator is implemented as a job.
Calling `execute` will start the job and immediately return the
operator with a `FINISHED` result, which lets other operators run
while the fluid sim cleanup is still ongoing.

Solution is to implement the `free_all` operator like the
`bake_all` operator:
- `execute` runs the cleanup and waits until that is done before
  returning.
- `invoke` starts the cleanup as a job and becomes a modal operator, and
  keeps running until the job is finished. This ensures other operators
  can only start once the cleanup is finished.

subject: Texture Paint: Calculate and store pixel row bounds for coarse filtering
message:
Texture Paint: Calculate and store pixel row bounds for coarse filtering

This PR makes a number of changes to the main brush stroke of the 3D
Texture Paint brush. Currently, when the `PackedPixelRow` data is built,
we store the UV `start_barycentric_coord`, from which we can calcuate
the 3D position of each pixel by first evaluating the delta, and then
performing an interpolation after re-creating the barycentric weights
for the given pixel. This is done for each pixel, on every step of the
stroke.

This PR moves this calculation outside of the main brush loop, generated
and stored alongside the `PackedPixelRow`, as `PackedPixelRowPosition`,
which contains three fields, the start 3D position of the row, the
ending 3D position, and the delta between elements in the row.

This then is used to speed up brush evaluation in two steps:
* Calculating the per-pixel position is a simple multiplication and
  addition, instead of needing to access and calculate triangle data
  to perform a barycentric weighting of the values
* We can perform a coarser brush evaluation test that does not require
  calculating and performing distance calculations on each pixel of a
  row, instead we can perform a line segment intersection test in
  parallel.

This has the downside of needing to update the cached pixel data more
often, at the benefit of improving the general stroke performance.

In general, this change improves performance across the board,
increasing in effectiveness as the pixel density per UV primitive also
increases. This is due to the existing check being an AABB intersection
test with the brush sphere and the associated primitive of a set of
rows.

Testing was done with a Suzanne mesh with a 4k texture attached. With
no subdivisions applied to the mesh, the average pixel density per node
is 10502, resulting in an average runtime of the `do_paint_pixels`
function being 0.791ms and 0.595ms, before and after this change, or a
25% reduction in runtime.

For a Suzanne mesh with a 4k texture attached and a level 3 subdivision
surface modifier applied, the resulting mesh has 31k faces (13 BVH
nodes) and an average pixel density of 172. The average runtimes are
3.160ms and 2.550ms, before and after this change, or a 19% reduction in
runtime.

See the associated PR for more detailed performance statistics.

Part of #155365

subject: Core: add --console-crash-handler flag
message:
Core: add --console-crash-handler flag

Initially noted by devops as a problem: UI tests when crashing
spawn our crash dialog, that will just sit there for 1200 seconds
until the CI environment decides the test has failed and kills the
process, clicking away the dialog also works, but neither option is
ideal here.

The crash handler knows when we are in background mode, (`-B`) and
suppresses this dialog so this is why it has not been an issue for the
normal tests. However when we do crash we get an unhelpful message
saying `Writing: blender.crash.txt` which is not collected by buildbot
so unless a developer can get a devops person to go retrieve this file
its contents will be left to ones imagination.

This PR adds a `--console-crash-handler` argument that does two things:

1 - Suppress the crash dialog even when we are not in background mode
2 - Rather than writing the crash data to blender.crash.txt write this
information to stderr so it shows up in the CI logs.

It also updates all invocations of blender I could find in our test
scripts to pass this new flag. The benchmark scripts have not been
updated as they regularly run against older blender versions that may
not support the new flag.

subject: Refactor: Images: Move GPU textures from Image to ImBuf
message:
Refactor: Images: Move GPU textures from Image to ImBuf

This is a more natural fit and will make it possible to support multilayer
and multipass images. GPU compositor output was already stored as a GPU
texture on ImBuf, and this extends that to image textures for rendering and
the 3D viewport.

* For garbage collection, the last used time is now on the ImBuf instead
  of Image, separate for CPU and GPU access.
* Getting gpu::Texture* from an image now returns an owning reference,
  to ensure the texture stays alive and is not freed. A mutex was added to
  ImBuf to make this process fully atomic.
* The draw manager now holds a list of deferred textures that will be loaded
  in parallel, instead of MaterialModule doing it. Crucially, it is this list
  that gpu::Texture** bindings for such deferred textures point into, rather
  than pointing into Image or ImBuf that may be modified by another thread
  (see #158372).
* UDIM atlas and tile mapping are stored as GPU-only ImBufs in the image
  cache. This requires some exceptions in the code as these are not
  regular image buffers, but may be the best fit with this design until
  we can do e.g. bindless textures without an atlas.
* For image sequences and movies, as before a single GPU texture for the
  current frame is kept but the mechanism is different. Previously there
  was only a single pointer that needed to be cleared when the frame
  changed, now we free other frames from the image cache.
* Error logging on failure is improved, now mentioning the specific
  failed texture file path rather than a generic message.

subject: Cycles: Reduce SVM stack usage with improved node scheduling
message:
Cycles: Reduce SVM stack usage with improved node scheduling

Use a better heuristic for scheduling the nodes: when scheduling the
next node, pick the one that increases the stack usage the least,
preferring nodes that free more slots than they allocate. This way short
lived intermediate values are released more quickly, before going into
other parts of the graph.

The impact of this was tested on blend files from older bug reports
related to complex node graphs, fixing previous issues marked as known
limitation in the process (overflow means it needed more than 255).

| Issue  | Old.     | New |
| -----: | -------: | --: |
|  37706 |       16 |  13 |
|  43245 |       37 |  17 |
|  44073 |       28 |  22 |
|  45628 |       24 |  14 |
|  46044 |       69 |  56 |
|  46782 |      102 | 102 |
|  53518 | overflow | 164 |
|  54560 | overflow |  75 |
|  77091 | overflow |  99 |
| 101654 |      237 |  87 |
| 103066 |        7 |   7 |
| 113161 |      193 |  75 |
| 115459 |       33 |  33 |
| 117706 |       81 |  32 |
| 159637 | overflow | 166 |

SVM compile time takes around 1.25x longer. It could be up to 10x in
the naive implementation I did first. There is still further improvement
possible with something like Sethi-Ullman ordering, but that is left as
future work.

Fix #159637: Cycles SVM stack too small when enabling texture cache

subject: Fix #160104: bl_versions in Remote Asset Library listing is inconsistent
message:
Fix #160104: bl_versions in Remote Asset Library listing is inconsistent

Change `required: [from]` to `required: [min]`, as `min` is the actual
field name.

Some history: I wanted to use `from`+`until`, but then realized that
`from` is a Python keyword, and so the code generated from the spec
would have to be mangled (it would become `from_` I think). Since
leading/trailing underscores are often used to denote private fields, I
didn't want to go there, and changed it to `min` instead. I just forgot
to update the `required` list.

As for using `max` (instead of `until`, to match it with `min`), I
intentionally chose not to use that, as to me it reads as "the maximum
version of Blender that is still compatible". Since the field has the
first version of Blender that is NOT compatible, I used `until` instead.

have a Render Layers node. This happens because during file loading lib
linking, ntree_blend_read_after_liblink will call node_declare, which

subject: Platform: support library path for system-wide Unix installs
message:
Platform: support library path for system-wide Unix installs

For system-wide installations on Unix, FHS defines "share"
(typically "/usr/share") as "Architecture-independent".

Blender violated this by installing libraries into `/usr/share` as
part of the GLTF add-on.

Resolve by supporting a parallel "libraries" directly that mirrors
the layout of "/usr/share".

Now they install under the lib tree (mirroring share), e.g.:

- /usr/share/blender/5.2/
- /usr/lib/blender/5.2/

Changes:

- Add `bpy.utils.resource_path('SYSTEM_LIBS')`,
  the version root under the install lib directory,
  so add-ons can find their relocated libraries.
- Use `CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR` when defined (lib/lib64/multiarch),
  so linux packages can define the directory (defaulting to "lib").

Only affects non-portable Linux installs.
Portable, Python module, Windows and macOS builds still bundle
libraries next to the add-on.

subject: Fix: Vulkan: Various render tests
message:
Fix: Vulkan: Various render tests

This PR fixes several render tests that were failing due to spec violations (VVL).

- VUID-vkCmdBeginRendering-pRenderingInfo-09588: When a BEGIN_RENDERING
  and a later DRAW node in the same group are extracted, the DRAW's
  depth-stencil -> GENERAL barrier is submitted as a group pre-barrier. The
  BEGIN_RENDERING then sees GENERAL instead of DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL.
  Fix: scan the current group's pre-barriers for the last layout transition
  and patch VkRenderingAttachmentInfo.imageLayout to match.

- VUID-vkCmdDraw-None-08600: overlay_paint_point has no push constants
  while overlay_paint_wire has PUSH_CONSTANT(bool, use_select). When the
  descriptor set tracker reuses a cached set between these shaders (early
  return path), the set handle is identical so assign_if_different skips
  vkCmdBindDescriptorSets, leaving the stale layout from the previous draw
  bound. Fix: propagate the cached handle on the early return path and
  track VkPipelineLayout changes in VKBoundPipeline to force a rebind.

- Incorrect shader create info in compositor.

subject: Fix: RNA `RNA_property_collection_type_get` generates broken ancestors data.
message:
Fix: RNA `RNA_property_collection_type_get` generates broken ancestors data.

This API is used to return a PointerRNA for the specific 'container
type' of a RNA collection (typically containing dedicated API to e.g.
add or remove items).

Simply copying the owner struct into that 'collection struct' breaks
the ancestors data, since the actual owner struct will be replaced by
the collection one in all sub-data chains.

So instead, create the rna collection struct as a child of its owner
struct, which allows to preserve the whole inheritance chain.

Note that this 'virtual' intermediary collection data will not often be
