subject: Fix #156235: VSE alpha over does not preserve compositor glow
message:
Fix #156235: VSE alpha over does not preserve compositor glow

When a floating point image (e.g. EXR file, or a scene strip result)
contains "purely emissive" colors (alpha zero, but colors not
zero -- for example as produced by compositor Glow effect), VSE Alpha
Over blending mode was not handling them correctly, effectively
"losing" the glow. Additionally, VSE colorspace conversions were also
making it buggy.

- Fix the incorrect optimization in Alpha Over effect that did not
  realize that pure emissive colors are possible.
- The edge artifacts are in places where alpha is neither zero nor one.
  By default VSE is using sRGB color space, but scene strips or EXR
  images usually are in Linear color space. So VSE does colorspace
  conversion, and it was doing it with predivide=true; this is what
  causes the artifacts around edges. Since neither predivide=true nor
  predivide=false are strictly more correct than the other, switch VSE
  colorspace conversions to use predivide=false. This matches what
  Compositor color space conversion node is doing, and fixes the
  edge artifacts.
- Note that this changes a bit how floating point images with
  semitransparencies look inside VSE, a bit. Arguably the new behavior
  is more correct.

subject: Fix: Vulkan: WRITE-AFTER-WRITE hazard on aliased pool textures
message:
Fix: Vulkan: WRITE-AFTER-WRITE hazard on aliased pool textures

When the texture pool reuses memory for a new VkImage, the resource state
tracker initialized its access mask to VK_ACCESS_NONE. This caused the first
barrier on the aliased image to have srcAccessMask=0, meaning it would not
wait for pending writes from the previous VkImage sharing the same memory,
triggering a WRITE-AFTER-WRITE validation error.

Fix by initializing aliased image state with VK_ACCESS_MEMORY_WRITE_BIT,
so the first barrier always synchronizes against all prior memory writes
on the aliased memory.

It could happen that compositor can acquire memory, clear it, but never
use it as that part of the tree isn't evaluated. The next acquire to that
texture would violate with a WRITE-AFTER-WRITE.

Fix #159520: Layered depth images could use color attachment layout

When a depth image has multiple layers or mip levels, the image tracker
in the render graph command builder uses color attachment layout
and color aspect bit in pipeline barriers, even for depth images.

This meant depth images were told to transition to
"color_attachment_optimal" instead of "depth_attachment_optimal",
which is invalid per the Vulkan spec and can cause undefined behavior
or validation errors on some drivers.

The fix passes the image aspect (color vs depth/depth+stencil) through
the sub-resource tracking so the barrier code knows whether it
is dealing with a color or depth image.

subject: Fix #159520: Layered depth images could use color attachment layout
message:
Fix #159520: Layered depth images could use color attachment layout

When a depth image has multiple layers or mip levels, the image tracker
in the render graph command builder uses color attachment layout
and color aspect bit in pipeline barriers, even for depth images.

This meant depth images were told to transition to
"color_attachment_optimal" instead of "depth_attachment_optimal",
which is invalid per the Vulkan spec and can cause undefined behavior
or validation errors on some drivers.

The fix passes the image aspect (color vs depth/depth+stencil) through
the sub-resource tracking so the barrier code knows whether it
is dealing with a color or depth image.

subject: Core: Project Awareness and UI
message:
Core: Project Awareness and UI

Adds minimal projects to Blender. Part of #133001

The high-level additions in this PR are:

- A single global run-time Blender project, which can either exist or
  not depending on whether a project is currently loaded. A python API
  is provided for creating, clearing, and modifying this run-time project.

- An on-disk TOML serialization of projects. For a given project, this
  lives in `<project_root>/.blender_project/config.toml`.
  The `.blender_project` directory functions similarly to a `.git`
  directory: any files under the directory that it's in are considered
  part of that project.  When opening a file under a project, that
  project is automatically loaded.

- New `project_root` and `project_name` path template variables, which
  are available whenever there is a project.

- A new Project editor type, where the user can create/edit/manage projects.

The UI and UX follow the "MVP - Single Project" design in:
https://devtalk.blender.org/t/2025-11-25-project-setup-meeting/43475

The core Blender project data structures are defined in C++. Currently
they are quite minimal, and only accommodate a project name and root
path. This will be expanded in the future as more project features from
#133001 are added.

Loading/saving and the on-disk format of projects is defined entirely
in Python. This was partly to make development easier, but also for
dog-fooding to ensure that the APIs are reasonable: in the future we
hope to allow Python extensions to define other ways of loading/saving
projects, to accommodate a wider range of production environments.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Parborg <sebastian@blender.org>

Cycles: Split OptiX kernels into smaller modules to improve load time

This helps especially for OSL, where load time is very long. By
splitting off shader raytrace, MNEE and volumes, the first time
rendering is much faster.

The downside is that noinline functions will be duplicated. However OSL
startup performance is very bad currently and this seems the better
trade-off for now. There are ways to make this work if we do not mark
noinline functions as static, but this will require some bigger code
reorganization.

Without OSL, shader raytrace and MNEE were combined in a single module,
and that has been split into two as well.

Besides a better user experience, This will fix OptiX OSL test timeouts
on the buildbot, where some tests need to compute a few different
specializations and the 600s timeout is exceeded, with the longest test
run time being around 300s.

subject: Fix: XR: Clipped Viewfinder view content when using viewport render region
message:
Fix: XR: Clipped Viewfinder view content when using viewport render region

When using the Render Region feature in the desktop 3D viewport, the VR
Location Scouting Viewfinder would be inadvertently clipped when using
EEVEE. This is due to the render region being a Scene render settings,
and thus applying to any rendered viewport view.

The EEVEE instance init code deals with viewport render region/border in
two branches, in case of an image render, the render region clipping is
applied to the entire view texture. Else, a ratio is computed taking
into account the camera border, which creates the issue in our case.

Fixed by adding a new `is_viewport_xr()` DRWContext method to check if
the rendred View3D declared itself as an XR surface, and use the simpler
full-width clipping logic in this case.

Note that this does *not* make is so that viewport render region
clipping will not affect the Viewfinder at all, but rather that if the
Viewport render region is set to the full camera width (0, 0, 1, 1). The
entire Viewfinder will be properly displayed as expected.

See PR for before/after comparison screenshots.

subject: Fix: Vulkan: Compositor data race condition
message:
Fix: Vulkan: Compositor data race condition

This PR fixes several data race conditions that can happen when using
Vulkan + Compositor. The issue is that a
`for-loop -> barrier -> conditional if` is not supported by the
SPIR-V specification. The compositor_parallel_reduction uses this
control flow.

Vulkan's SPIR-V validator (VUID-RuntimeSpirv-SharedMemoryDataRace)
requires that all invocations in a workgroup must access shared
variables identically. Either all always access them or all never
access them. Mixed participation based on control flow is
undefined behavior per the SPIR-V spec, even when barriers are present.

The load and store to the same shared values must also be protected
by barriers.

subject: Fix: BLI: ensure that +0.0 and -0.0 hash to the same value
message:
Fix: BLI: ensure that +0.0 and -0.0 hash to the same value

Floating point representation has the special case that `+0.0` and `-0.0` exist.
They compare equal but do not have the same bit representation. This implies
that a `bit_cast` does not work to get a hash from the number. It breaks the one
rule for these hashes: if two values compare equal, they have to have the same
hash.

Floating point values have other special values but they don't need the same
treatment:
* `+inf` and `-inf` have unique representations.
* `nan` has many different representation, all of which never compare equal to
  each other, even if the bit pattern is the same.

The fix is to add this special case in the core hashing functions and to make
sure that hashing functions of vectors, matrices, etc. derive from that.

Unique hashing is updated to properly handle this too.

This also fixes #158701.

subject: Assets: Do not download assets when dragging them
message:
Assets: Do not download assets when dragging them

Part of #130532.

Dragging an asset from the asset browser or asset shelf would instantly
download it. While this is convenient and feels fun when it works well,
it's awkward when assets take a while to download. Users may expect that
canceling the drag will also cancel the download, so they hold the mouse
button until the download is finished. Even when they know it doesn't
cancel, they still hold it until done, to avoid having to move the mouse
to the asset again and having to drag it again. It's all just awkard in
this situation. In testing we also occasionaly dragged and thus
downloaded an asset accidentally.

Instead, force users to first download assets (e.g. using the context
menu) before using. The asset shelf already works like this for poses
and brushes, so this is more consistent too.

We also want to make downloading easier, likely with a download icon
button that appears over the asset preview on mouse hover.

subject: LibOverride: Add initial support for geonodes packed bakes.
message:
LibOverride: Add initial support for geonodes packed bakes.

This is especially tricky, since packed bakes themselves are not exposed
through RNA, so generic liboverride diffing and apply code cannot handle
them.

On top of this, there is no way to tell if a packed bake in the
liboverride data comes (has been copied) from the linked reference data,
or if it was effectively generated from the liboverride itself.

This commit introduces a new `CUSTOM` liboverride operation, which is
ignored by default/generic liboverride processing, and requires dedicated
RNA property callbacks.

It is used to generate operations on the 'bakes' collection property. This
encodes the fact that the matching packed bakes from the written
liboverride data should replace the ones from the linked reference data.

It should handle most commons cases well:
- Packed bakes from the override replace the ones from the linked
  reference, in case both are defined.
- Bakes are matched by 'bake id', to ensure that a change in order or
  number of bakes in the linked reference data, does not completely
  break the override bakes.

Fixes #154029.

subject: Geometry Nodes: Bevel Node
message:
Geometry Nodes: Bevel Node

This is for a Bevel Geometry node.  The code is a kind of port of the BMesh bevel code in bmesh_bevel.cc, but it needs substantial changes to use Mesh data structures instead of BMesh ones. And therefore, it needs to deal with the fact the the Mesh is not efficiently mutable. The approach is to make an "ExtendibleMesh" that holds data about the original Mesh but also deltas to that mesh to be applied at new Mesh construction time.  Many other changes in the code were needed to use ints for Vert, Edge, Face, and Corner instead of pointers to BMesh elements.

In designing the Geometry Node, we made some decisions about some changes to the interface as compared to the BMesh interface to bevel.  These were discussed in issue #98674. Some of the bigger decisions:

- Offsets are given per edge (4 of them, one for each side of each end) or per vertex (only the first slot is used) depending on whether we are edge beveling or vertex beveling. There is no "offset kind" spec -- you can achieve kinds other than "offset" by calculating outside the node.
- Miters are both simplfied and expanded. There is a boolean per corner called "miter". If it is true, and the given corner is just past a beveled edge, then the gap between that beveled edge and the next will be mitered. It will be in "patch" miter if the angle is reflect and an "arc" miter otherwise.
- So far there is no "clamp" and "loop slide" option.  I remain undecided about what to do here. The eventual hope is that "clamp" will go away because I will use a "straight skeleton" algorithm to "eat away" geometry when it starts to overlap.  But this won't happen in time for the intitial release.  For now, I may implement clamp as "always on", but this isn't yet implemented. Loop slide can be done by calculation of offsets outside the node, but this could be tedious.  I may or may not decide to implement loop slide inside the node; if I do, maybe it will be "always on" -- not sure.
- There is an "effect Faces" option in the UI but it isn't hooked up to anything yet. I'll probably disable that for the first release.  Eventually I want to have it, as kind of inset operator.
- There is a "profile" input, meant to take a curve, that will be used for custom profiles, but that is not hooked up to anything yet.
- There are output fields, not yet hooked up, which will give selections of various parts of the new beveled mesh, to be used for things like special materials or normal handling. (As a consequence, there will be no hardening code native to this node.)

The state of the code as of this initial WIP is that many things work (with the exceptions noted above re clamping and loop slide and custom profiles).  There are about 70 regression tests, ported from the bevel_operator.py tests (with more UV maps). They all "pass" right now but that's just because I made the expected_object match the current code output. I still have to go through them carefully one-by-one to see that they match the current BMesh behavior.

I added reviewers but this isn't really in a state to review yet, unless you are interested.
One thing I intend to do: update all the "old-style" math functions (that use raw float arrays) to "new-style" math functions.

This code was heavily assisted using Claude Sonnet 4.6 in Antigravity. But I have carefully read the output and will continue to do so, and will stand by the code as if it were totally my own (and, since I wrote the original BMesh code, it is in that sense mostly mine anyway).

subject: Cycles: Metal: Integrate MTLResidencySets for explicit memory management
message:
Cycles: Metal: Integrate MTLResidencySets for explicit memory management

Introduce `MTLResidencySet` to explicitly manage GPU memory residency on macOS 15.0+ devices.

This provides the Metal/GPU driver with a clear list of resources to optimise memory handling, potentially improving performance by reducing overhead from hundreds of `useResource` calls.

Memory allocation and deallocation operations are now routed through new wrapper functions that conditionally add or remove resources from the residency set. Explicit `useResource` calls are bypassed when residency sets are active, as resource residency is now managed through the `MTLResidencySet` API. A debug flag is added to enable or disable this feature at runtime (via env var `CYCLES_METAL_RESIDENCY_SETS=0`).

subject: Fix #158292: VSE: Tabbing into meta strip adjustment layer crashes with scene strip
message:
Fix #158292: VSE: Tabbing into meta strip adjustment layer crashes with scene strip

Adjustment layers happen to "leak" image content from higher levels in
the meta-strip stack, and when there is a scene strip, prefetching
happily tries to render it.

But rather than add another check in
`seq_prefetch_scene_strip_is_rendered` to prevent the prefetch, I argue
that adjustment strips shouldn't be doing this at all.

This leads to a slight visual change: now, adjustment strips without any
other content inside a meta-strip will always render empty, even if
there is content outside the meta-strip, which arguably makes more
sense.

subject: Fix: Geometry Nodes: unnecessary evaluation with specific usage of Menu Switch node
message:
Fix: Geometry Nodes: unnecessary evaluation with specific usage of Menu Switch node

This fixes an issue where some nodes are evaluated even though their output is
not needed.

The issue is caused by a cyclic dependency when determining of which sockets the
referenced anonymous attributes should be gathered. Breaking the cyclic
dependency in `fix_link_cycles` has the fallback of assuming that the value is
used.

The fix is to split the Menu Switch node evaluation into two lazy-functions. One
that only computes the output value, and one that outputs all the booleans for
the individual cases. This works because the output booleans only depend on the
first input and not all the value inputs.

A regression test has been added that fails (by crash or timeout) when this
change is broken somehow.

subject: Alembic: deduplicate data reading between IPolyMesh and ISubD
message:
Alembic: deduplicate data reading between IPolyMesh and ISubD

Alembic represents subdivision meshes (`ISubD`) separately from
"regular" meshes (`IPolyMesh`). Since subdivision meshes seem seldomly
used, most of the improvements and bug fixes regarding mesh data
reading were implemented for the IPolyMesh reader but not the ISubD
reader. This resulted in diverging implementations leading to bugs
seemingly resurfacing when subdivision meshes are used.

This extends `AbcMeshData` to hold the rest of the common data between
polygon and subdivision meshes and deduplicates some code in order to
keep the implementations aligned and bring bug fixes and improvements
to subdivision meshes.

The polymesh and subd readers now each create an instance `AbcMeshData`
as a basis to read all common mesh data between the two mesh types. To
that effect, `read_subd_sample` is now merged info `read_mesh_sample`
which takes an `AbcMeshData` as input instead of a specific schema.
As a result of this merge, generated coordinates are now read for
subdivision meshes.

`read_mesh_sample` now also checks whether the topology has changed,
thus bringing the safety checks for polygon meshes to subdivision
meshes. Therefore, this function is also now responsible for creating
a new mesh if need be.

Detection of topological changes are extracted from `AbcMeshReader`
into a free function using `AbcMeshData` as input.

This PR also implements `AbcObjectReader.topology_changed` for
subdivision meshes.

Finally, the UVs-related fields from `AbcMeshData` were moved to
`CDStreamConfig` to keep the former structure const in function
calls.

This PR makes no attemps at reading FaceSets as materials for
subdivision meshes as we do for polygon meshes. This might require
moving some logic in a common `AbcGenericMeshReader` base class.

subject: Fix #159289: USD import places skinned mesh by skeleton transform
message:
Fix #159289: USD import places skinned mesh by skeleton transform

When a skinned mesh and its Skeleton live under a common SkelRoot but in
sibling Xforms with different transforms, the imported mesh had wrong
transforms applied because it kept the transform of its USD-hierarchy
parent instead of being positioned by the bound Skeleton.

Per the UsdSkel spec[1], a skinned mesh's own and ancestor xformOps
below the SkelRoot do not position the skinned result. The geometry is
placed by the bound Skeleton's world transform, with
`primvars:skel:geomBindTransform` aligning it as follows:
(skinned mesh world = skeleton world * geomBindTransform).

Re-parent each skinned mesh to its bound armature object (with an
identity parent-inverse). The mesh local transform is the
geomBindTransform that `USDMeshReader::get_local_usd_xform` already
assigns, so Blender's armature deform then reproduces the spec result
(mesh world = armature world * geomBindTransform). When no usable
geomBindTransform is authored, `get_local_usd_xform` now returns the
identity for skeleton-bound meshes so the mesh's own xformOps are
ignored. The re-parenting is skipped when it would create a parent cycle
(the bound Skeleton prim being a USD descendant of the skinned mesh).

Because a skinned mesh is always re-parented to the armature, it is
never the root of the transform hierarchy.
`USDMeshReader::is_root_xform_prim()` now returns false for
skeleton-bound meshes, preventing the root-level scene scale and axis
conversion from being applied to the mesh's skeleton-space local
transform on top of the same conversion already carried by the armature.

Fixes #159289, #130747
[1] https://openusd.org/release/api/_usd_skel__schemas.html#UsdSkel_BindingAPI_GeomBindTransform

Recently, more built-in node groups assets are being added. These sometimes use
many nested node groups which are not meant to be more internal. However, those
could still clutter the node add menu a lot, overloading it with many groups
that the user did not ask for specifically.

up in the add menu, if they are directly used in the file already. If they are
only indirectly used, they are not shown. It's still possible to add them though

with a dot. However, that has some considerable downsides:

message:
Assets: Disable "Open Blend File" for online assets and essentials

Online assets are downloaded to a cache on disk. Edits would could get
lost when the asset is updated/re-downloaded. The essentials are
essentially part of Blender, we just happen to bundle them as .blend
files users can open. Edits to them would put them into an unexpected
state, and the changes get lost when changing to a new Blender versions.

For reasons like this, these .blend files shouldn't be edited by users,
or at least, Blender shouldn't encourage this. The "Open Blend File"
operator was added to make editing assets easier, so this doesn't make
sense for these assets.

This adds an `bpy.types.AssetLibrary` type so properties can be queried,
accessible via `bpy.types.AssetRepresentation.owner_asset_library`.

subject: Fix: EEVEE: Undefined behavior in polygonal bokeh depth of field
message:
Fix: EEVEE: Undefined behavior in polygonal bokeh depth of field

This caused a discrepancy between Metal and other platforms.

From the MSL specification:
```
atan2(y, x)
Implemented as
if x > 0, atan(y / x),
if x < 0 and y > 0, atan(y / x) + M_PI_F
if x < 0 and y < 0, atan(y / x) – M_PI_F
and if x = 0 or y = 0, the result is undefined
```
Also the GLSL specification:
```
The result is undefined if x=0.
```

Fixed by adding a small epsilon to `atan`.

subject: Fix: EEVEE: Motion Blur: Over-blurred background
message:
Fix: EEVEE: Motion Blur: Over-blurred background

This would happen in scene with large motion vectors.
The tile dilation would make it so that most of the
static background would be covered by the motion
blur gather. Since this gather is jittered, it would
sometime not sample the static backgorund pixels
exactly at the correct location and would introduce
a slight blurring.

Correct this by increasing the center sample weight
when we detect that there is no center sample motion
and when the center sample has low weight.

UI: Refresh grayed out state of active buttons on redraw

When the "disabled" state of an active button (as in, button that's
hovered or otherwise being interacted with) would change, that change
wouldn't be reflected until the button becomes inactive.

This is needed for blender/blender!159238: When online assets are
displayed in "Add" menus, they should be downloaded first, and the menu
needs to refresh once the download is done. Without this change, the
downloaded asset would remain grayed out until the mouse moved over a
different asset. Usually the disabled state of a button doesn't change
while it's active, so this wasn't a notable issue so far. But with the
background downloading, it can change while the mouse hovers the button.

To solve this, the disabled state should always be retrieved from the
latest incarnation of a button, and not use the previous state in case
of an active button.

subject: Fix #156105: Keyframe values don't update in the property
message:
Fix #156105: Keyframe values don't update in the property

The issue comes from the fact that the same data-block is pulled into
multiple dependency graphs that are both active and evaluated (hence,
they both "flush" evaluated values back to the original IDs).

Apparently, this is a regression since 0d77f1e6aa which introduced
more relations, and caused more evaluation to happen.

It is not really clear what the proper solution would be, but it seems
to be possible to avoid regression caused by the aforementioned commit
by simply not forcing compositor build. The original reason why the
compositor node needed to be build is no longer relevant. Since then
the scene compositor is no longer an embedded data-block, so there is
no risk on remapping anything in the original bmain since the remapping
code no longer "goes inside" of the scene's compositor.

subject: Grease Pencil: New Fill Tool Algorithm
message:
Grease Pencil: New Fill Tool Algorithm

Adds a new fill algorithm for the bucket fill tool to create
exact geometry. The new solver is called `Delaunay` in the `Advanced`
options panel. It is set as the new default.
The old pixel-based flood fill method is unchanged and accessible from
the `Advanced` menu.

The solver is an implementation of "Delaunay Painting" [1] with some
additions.
* Adds a new automatic segmentation using the maximum weight that an
  edge can have.
* Adds two new settings to the fill tool.
  * `Internal Gaps`: Enables checking for gaps in internal shapes. This
    enables the following option:
  * `Gap Factor` which is a scale invariant value from 0.0 to 1.0
    (defaulting to 0.4). It's the "sensitivity" of the gap detection.
    Higher values results in more gaps detected and as such can create
    smaller fills

Also, in practice this solver is often faster than the pixel fill.

[1] https://perso.telecom-paristech.fr/parakkat/PDF/CGF22.pdf

subject: Fix: Vulkan: Avoid reading from non-host coherent memory without sync
message:
Fix: Vulkan: Avoid reading from non-host coherent memory without sync

In `VKTexture::read_sub`, the staging buffer is created with the
`VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT` flag. While it is only
accessed sequentially, it is stated that this gave better performance
with AMD GPUs.
VMA tries to preferrably find a memory type with the property flag
`VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_CACHED_BIT` in this case.

Unlike most other drivers by Intel, AMD and NVIDIA, the Intel ANV Mesa
driver does not expose memory that is both host coherent and host
cached for some Gen12 GPUs (like Arrow Lake and Meteor Lake iGPUs), but
only memory that is either only host coherent or only host cached.
This leads to the issue that host cached memory is selected by VMA due
to using `VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT`, but neither
`vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges` nor `vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` are
called, even though they are required for non-coherent memory. This
leads to race conditions and memory corruptions with these iGPUs.

This issue is fixed by introducing two new functions
`VKBuffer::flush_mapped_memory` and
`VKBuffer::invalidate_mapped_memory`, which are used by VKTexture.
These new functions have no effect when the memory is host coherent.

It was also alternatively evaluated if switching to
`VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT` fixes the
issue. While that also fixed the issue, it resulted in slightly worse
performance (3.9s vs. 3.7s for `GPUVulkanTest` over multiple runs).

subject: Fix #159102: Pose bone selection cycling order wrong
message:
Fix #159102: Pose bone selection cycling order wrong

It is now dictated by creation order instead of depth.

This was working prior to the switch to Overlay Next (409012956f).
409012956f broke it completely (no cycling whatsoever), then
04a57dd937e8 brought cycling back (but not based on view depth, but on
creation order).

Looking at `GPU_select_end`, we can go two codepaths:
- `gpu_select_pick_end` (legacy) -- this used to sort the hits by view
depth already
- `gpu_select_next_end` (Overlay Next) -- this does not sort the hits
anymore

In a comment in #140614 the preferred way to do this now is let the
"consumer" do the sorting (instead of doing it very low level in
`GPU_select_end` already). And we can see that this is indeed happening
in places (e.g. `mouse_select_eval_buffer` does it --but only for
objectmode).

So this PR adds back depth based sorting for pose bone selection
cycling.

Assets: show whether downloaded online asset files match the remote

When assets have been downloaded from a remote asset library, these are
now checked against the library's listing. If their hash or file size
doesn't match, this is shown in the UI.

This uses the Disk File Hash Service (DFHS) from various threads for the
same asset library (and thus the same storage path for the DFHS SQLite
database). This proved troublesome, as SQLite connections are not meant
to be shared across threads. To avoid this sharing, DFHS instances are
now created on a per-thread basis, and each thread is responsible for
releasing its DFHS instance. The mass-release at loading another blend
file or quitting Blender is still in place.

subject: Core: Add basic Tracy integration
message:
Core: Add basic Tracy integration

This PR adds basic integration with Tracy for developer profiling.

A new BLI header (`BLI_profile.hh`) is used to wrap calls to the
underlying Tracy macros. Not all features exposed in `Tracy.hpp`
are currently exposed in our header file.

What is included:
* Frame marking
* Zone marking
* Zone customization

What is not included:
* Memory metrics
* Arbitrary plots
* Messages
* Lock support
* Thread naming

To simplify usage and match Blender conventions, the exposed BLI API
makes the following changes:
* The default building block is `BLI_profile_scope`, corresponding to
  `ZoneScoped`. This creates a zone in Tracy that measures the timing
  of the enclosing scope.
* For cases where multiple zones need to exist in the same scope,
  `BLI_profile_scope_var` is used, corresponding to `ZoneNamed` to avoid
  confusion with user-facing names.
* A `ProfileCategory` enum is required for all `BLI_profile_scope[_var]`
  calls to ensure consistent coloring within the Tracy UI.
* All text input uses the format string variants, instead of also adding
  a version that takes a string and length.
* If a static name differing from the enclosing scope is needed,
  both of the above macros have a `with_name` variant.
* For per-call naming, `BLI_profile_scope_set_dynamic_name` corresponds
  to `ZoneName`.

From an actual instrumentation perspective, the following areas have
been updated:
* The main interaction loop (`WM_main`) and called functions, along
  with the main frame marker.
* Window drawing (a portion of `wm_draw_update`) along with the marking
  the discontinuous frames.
* Operator invoking and modal execution, dynamically named as the
  operator's `idname`.

subject: Geometry Nodes: move Transfer Attributes node out of experimental
message:
Geometry Nodes: move Transfer Attributes node out of experimental

This makes the Transfer Attributes node available by default. It was originally
developed for the hair dynamics project to copy over the simulated attributes
(like position) onto the static geometry. While transferring individual
attributes with e.g. the Sample Index node is already possible, this node is
more flexible because:
* It allows transferring a dynamic number of attributes, based on a list of name
  patterns.
* The attributes can have different data types.
* One can easily use custom IDs to map elements from one geometry to another.
* The node is optimized for various special cases. Importantly, under certain
  conditions, the node can be O(1) per attribute because of implicit sharing or
  because of single-value attributes.
* It can propagate anonymous attributes.

The basic behavior is that for each given attribute name, it first determines
the domain on the source geometry, then looks at the corresponding IDs on the
source and target geometries. If an element on the target has an id that matches
an id on the source, the value is copied over. If the target has IDs that are
not available on the source, the data remains unchanged or gets the default
value if the attribute didn't exist before.

By default, all ID inputs are the index field. In this configuration it can
easily transfer any attributes between geometries with the same topology

The output contains the names or all transferred attributes except for internal
attributes.

The topology of the target geometry remains unchanged. Only top-level attributes
are transferred, nested instances are ignored.

The `Exclude Names` option can be used to invert the patterns. When true, all
attributes not matching any of the given names are transferred.

In the future, there may be more way to generically handle attributes with
different types but this requires a couple features for Geometry Nodes that we
don't have yet (like "rainbow sockets" which can dynamically change their type).

subject: Geometry Nodes: move geometry bundles out of experimental
message:
Geometry Nodes: move geometry bundles out of experimental

This enables support for storing bundles in geometries by default. This provides
the ability to store arbitrary data on a geometry set, allowing it to be passed
whereever the geometry is passed, including across object boundaries.

This opens up significant new opportunities for building declarative systems
where the overall behavior is controlled by multiple objects. For example, it
allows creating force field objects which can be fed into simulation systems.

The geometry bundles can generally store all kinds of data that is supported by
geometry nodes, including fields, closures, other bundles and other geometry.
One notable exception is that anonymous attributes are removed as geometry
leaves geometry nodes, aka at the end of the evaluation of each modifier. This
constraint is necessary currently, because the lifetimes of these attributes
can't be tracked reliably outside of Geometry Nodes.

This adds two new nodes:
* Set Geometry Bundle: Updates the bundle stored in the geometry. If there was a
  bundle already, the old one is discarded.
* Get Geometry Bundle: Retrieve the bundle in a geometry, optionally removing it
  from the geometry.

might need a flag to record primary scatter for volumes. Additionally,

but then we'd be limited to only 8 visibility bits (which would be

subject: GPU: Force use of GLSL precise derivatives
message:
GPU: Force use of GLSL precise derivatives

This is done in order to reduce platform differences
when rendering with EEVEE.

Derivatives are used for mipmap selection, anisotropic filtering,
bump mapping and the wireframe node.

The added cost is not measurable.
## GLSL
GLSL supports precise derivatives only with ARB_derivative_control.

### Vulkan

This is built-in in Vulkan backend by using GLSL 4.5.

### OpenGL

For OpenGL we have to check for the extension support since we do not
require a 4.5 context.

Note that using `GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER_DERIVATIVE_HINT` might be possible.
But given it is legacy API, I prefer not to use it.

## MSL
MSL apparently always use precise derivatives and doesn't expose
coarse ones.

subject: Render: Hydra: Migrate render delegate to use Hydra 2.0 API
message:
Render: Hydra: Migrate render delegate to use Hydra 2.0 API

The 1.0 API is deprecated (though not yet removed) in OpenUSD 26.xx
releases. So it's time to migrate.

The API is now based on constructing a scene index with prims and schemas,
rather than getting callbacks through HdSceneDelegate to query data. This
simplifies the implementation somewhat and makes it more similar to Cycles
and EEVEE. The tricky handling of updates, objects, instances and geometry
sets was made to work more similar to Cycles.

Tasks are handled by inserting task prims into the retained scene index
rather than HdSceneDelegate.

The Storm render tests render identical to before, existing limitations
were preserved. There are some things that could be fixed by comparing
to the Cycles implementation but that's left for later.

USD has an abstraction where the host application and delegate can use
different versions. However there are some differences in material networks
that are not fully abstracted. From what I can tell, the latest Maya and
Houdini version are using Hydra 2.0 so this hopefully this improves
compatibility overall.

subject: Cycles: Hydra: Change render delegate to use Hydra 2.0 API
message:
Cycles: Hydra: Change render delegate to use Hydra 2.0 API

The 1.0 API is deprecated (though not yet removed) in OpenUSD 26.xx
releases. So it's time to migrate.

Use of the HdSceneDelegate is mostly removed, except for retrieving the
prims. Specific properties of prims are retrieved through schemas rather
than querying the scene delegate.

The full replacement of HdSceneDelegate is still ongoing in USD itself.
In the very latest 26.05 only HdPrman has an experimental option for
using the scene index directly, but for example HdStorm does not use it
yet. So removing it's use with the current 25.08 in Blender is not
expected to be stable enough.

Additionally HdRenderer is supposed to replace HdRenderDelegate and its
handling of tasks. However even in 26.05 that is only a stub
implementation so there is no actual alternative to migrate to.

Note that OpenUSD provides a compatibility layer so 1.0 and 2.0 hosts and
render delegates can work together. Which means ideally everything keeps
working the same, but there are likely some differences anyway. Support for
OpenUSD version 23.xx and older was dropped.

subject: Fix #155719: VSE crashes with retimed sound strips
message:
Fix #155719: VSE crashes with retimed sound strips

A bug in Audaspace that looks to be since Blender 3.6 (upstream commit https://github.com/neXyon/audaspace/commit/db2ff5807765):

1. Sound strips that are retimed use AnimateableProperty::writeConstantRange
  to write their section of pitch property values.
2. However, unlike AnimateableProperty::write, the writeConstantRange
  was not updating or handling "unknown" ranges of the animated values!
  So they ended up being completely uninitialized/garbage.
3. Now later on, when pitch value is read through
  AnimateableProperty::read, it does a cubic filter. Which means one of
  the filter taps can read from the "unknown" portion of the buffer,
  with whatever garbage value happened to be there.
4. As a result, effective pitch can end up being "anything", including
  values really close to zero, or values really close to infinities.
5. The JOS resample reader is not particularly safe against overflowing
  integers when it divides by ratios derived from this garbage pitch.
  So it ends up having "how much to read" being e.g. "4 billion" due
  to integer overflows.
6. Hilarity ensues!

From what I can tell, the problem is that the writeConstantRange did
not have the bit that fills in unknown parts of the buffer to have
something sensible.

Audaspace upstream PR https://github.com/neXyon/audaspace/pull/73
has been merged already.

subject: VSE: Detect when compositor effect/modifier is fully opaque
message:
VSE: Detect when compositor effect/modifier is fully opaque

Strips that have their content fully opaque benefit in two ways:
1) they can stop evaluation of strips under them that are fully
covered by their area, and 2) they do not need to get blended with a
dummy black input when they are the bottom strip.

Detect when the result of compositor evaluation is fully opaque
(i.e. no pixels contain alpha below 1.0), and mark the result
accordingly. Before this PR, strips with compositor modifier were
assumed to contain alpha just in case.

Performance: on EXR image sequence with compositor modifier that has
bloom + tune image + sensor noise, on Ryzen 5950X / RTX 3080Ti, time
to calculate VSE frame (render_strip_stack):
- 4K resolution: CPU 1550 -> 1420ms, GPU 235 -> 135ms
- HD resolution: CPU 212 -> 203ms, GPU 27 -> 18ms

In order to achieve the above: Refactor: Most VSE render functions now
return SeqResult instead of ImBuf

- The is_opaque_before_transform part of result is used above to
  properly detect compositor modifier transparency presence (can't do
  that via ImBuf color mode, since that can include alpha due to
  strip transform, even if the actual strip  rectangle is fully opaque)
- Later on, I expect ability for rendered result to live on the GPU
  will also be part of SeqResult.

subject: Fix #158665: Crash when running python script to rename and create edit bones
message:
Fix #158665: Crash when running python script to rename and create edit bones

Caused by b6a84566b9f8baad2d9316081a21c57b7df51d08

With the above commit, drivers are removed if their pose bone no longer
exists upon leaving edit mode.

The crash of the report was caused by the following chain of events.
* script goes into edit mode
* gets an edit bone
* renames it
* creates a new edit bone
* that triggers a depsgraph event
* which in turn calls `BKE_pose_rebuild` on the cow ID
* that in turn calls `BKE_pose_channels_clear_with_null_bone`
* which then cannot find the `Bone` for the `bPoseChannel` because the
name hasn't propagated correctly (see `ED_armature_bone_rename`. Tldr.
The `Bone` is **not renamed** in edit mode, but the `bPoseChannel` and
`EditBone` are)

subject: Geometry Nodes: iterate on force evaluation and Custom Force asset
message:
Geometry Nodes: iterate on force evaluation and Custom Force asset

Previously, a "custom geometry stage" had to be used for forces. One had to
manually add to the `external_force` attribute when implementing a custom force.
While this worked, it is a bit too generic for a force that is intended to be
used more generally, even in contexts that don't have the concept of a "geometry
stage".

Now there is a `Blender.Force` bundle type. It mainly contains a closure
computing the force. It has a geometry and a transform matrix as input. The
matrix would transform the geometry into world space (often it is in world space
already, in which case the transform matrix is just the identity). The closure
outputs a selection and force field.

There is a new `Custom Force` asset which makes it easier to create custom
forces. One can either directly implement the force as a closure, or just
provide a field. In the latter case, one also has to specify what space the
geometry is expected to be in for the field and what space the resulting force
is in.

There is also a new `Evaluate Forces` node group which detects which provided
forces correspond to each geometry and evaluates all the forces into a named
attribute.

subject: Refactor: Geometry Nodes: improve naming for reference lifetimes in declaration
message:
Refactor: Geometry Nodes: improve naming for reference lifetimes in declaration

There used to be lots of different node declaration functions to specify how a
node interacts with fields. The naming of those became increasingly confusing as
geometry nodes has evolved more. Things became even worse when bundles were
introduced because they could store geometries and fields together. The original
naming was designed for the case where there was a clear distinction between
field and geometry sockets.

On top of that, there are now bundles in geometries, making the naming even more
confusing. Also, structure types made some information redundant.

This patch redesigns how node declaration specify which anonymous attributes and
which fields referencing those attributes are propagated and used.

For reference, there used to be these methods which are now replaced:
`supports_field`, `field_on_all`, `field_source`, `implicit_field`,
`implicit_field_on_all`, `implicit_field_on`, `field_on`, `dependent_field`,
`field_source_reference_all`, `reference_pass`, `reference_pass_all`,
`propagate_all`, `propagate_all_instance_attributes`.

Instead of those, one uses one or multiple of the following:
* `structure_type(...)`: Not new but used instead of `supports_field` in many
  places.
* `default_input_type(...)`: Not new but used where `implicit_field_*` was used
  before.
* `propagate_all`: Existed before, but has new semantics. Instead of just
  meaning that attributes are propagated to an output, it also implies that
  anonymous attribute fields are propagated. This is now generally true anyway,
  since geometries contain fields in bundles.
* `evaluated_geometry_field`: For the common case when an input field is
  evaluated inside of this not in a passed in geometry. This could be extended
  to also take the evaluation domain etc for improved ux features.
* `anonymous_attribute_output`: For the common case that a node outputs a new
  attribute on geometry that it just processed.
* `inferred_structure_type`: Used on "function node" outputs where the structure
  type is automatically derived from inputs. E.g. when the inputs are a single
  value and a list, the inferred type will be a list.
* `propagate_references`: Indices that an output socket still contains
  references to anonymous attributes that were passed into the node as fields.

Most of these methods have two variants: one that takes an array of other socket
indices it applies to and one that implies all.

subject: Geometry Nodes: XPBD constraint residual error output
message:
Geometry Nodes: XPBD constraint residual error output

Adds residual error output to the hair solver node that represents
average relative error of the constraint solution. This indicates when a
hair setup needs more iterations to yield an accurate simulation result
and can help avoid unexpected behavior. Conversely it can also help
reduce excessive iterations and improve performance in some cases.

Residual squared error is measured per constraint and summed up by the
solver. The average error for each constraint is scaled by a threshold
value, such that the relative error is 1 when reaching the threshold.
Anything less than 1 can be considered a "good" solution.

The threshold value can be set for each constraint type and its type and
appropriate value depends on the constraint:
- Pin Position, Edge Length, Stretch/Shear, and collision constraints
  use length-based residuals. The default threshold value is 1 mm.
- Pin Rotation and Bend/Twist constraints use angle-based residuals.
  The default threshold value is 0.01 radians (~0.57 degrees)

The error output is stored in a new `XPBDSolverData` typed bundle that
is optionally added to the world output by the solver node, based on a
user-defined path.

subject: BLI: add utility methods to ListBaseT
message:
BLI: add utility methods to ListBaseT

This adds the following methods to `ListBaseT`:
* `is_empty` replacing `BLI_listbase_is_empty`
* `is_single` replacing `BLI_listbase_is_single`
* `clear_no_delete` replacing `BLI_listbase_clear`
* `free_no_destruct` replacing `BLI_freelistN`
* `count` replacing `BLI_listbase_count`

There are three goals this change is working towards:
* Use C++ methods instead of standalone functions for working on
  containers, also reducing boilerplate.
* Use more specific names instead of just `clear` and `free` which
  are ambiguous in the way they were used.
* Move freeing of some many lists into the header, so that type
  information becomes available (even though it's not used yet).

Most of this change is automated using a bunch of regex replacements.
It doesn't catch all cases, but almost all and should be safe.

```
BLI_listbase_is_empty\(([\w\.\->]+)\)     ->   $1->is_empty()
BLI_listbase_is_empty\(&([\w\.\->]+)\)    ->   $1.is_empty()
BLI_listbase_is_single\(([\w\.\->]+)\)    ->   $1->is_single()
BLI_listbase_is_single\(&([\w\.\->]+)\)   ->   $1.is_single()
BLI_listbase_clear\(([\w\.\->]+)\)        ->   $1->clear_no_delete()
BLI_listbase_clear\(&([\w\.\->]+)\)       ->   $1.clear_no_delete()
BLI_freelistN\(([\w\.\->]+)\)             ->   $1->free_no_destruct()
BLI_freelistN\(&([\w\.\->]+)\)            ->   $1.free_no_destruct()
BLI_listbase_count\(([\w\.\->]+)\)        ->   $1->count()

BLI_listbase_reverse\(([\w\.\->]+)\)      ->   $1->reverse()
```

Image: Add autosave support

This commit adds support to the autosave functionality to handle images
and allows autosave to work in Texture paint.

This requires two main changes:
* Packing all edited & editable images.
* Allow autosave to function when the most recent step is an image undo
  step.

The majority of this PR addresses the first change.

For all images that are to be autosaved, we pack to a new field on the
`Image`, `autosave_packedfiles` and mark the datablock with a new flag,
`IMA_AUTOSAVE_TEMPPACK`.

This field is used to prepopulate the `Image` datablock runtime cache
on file load, which then marks the ImBuf as dirty, so the user will be
informed to either save or discard changes.

If an image is saved, packed, or reloaded, the autosave information
(both the flag and the autosave packed file list) is cleared.
Additionally, the autosave information is cleared when the cache is
populated when loading the file.

As a similar area of concern, we also do this when creating the recovery
file, `quit.blend`

subject: Fix: Assets: Race condition when loading asset libraries
message:
Fix: Assets: Race condition when loading asset libraries

I was reliably getting a failed assert on startup, through
`remote_libraries_.add_new()` in
`AssetLibraryService::get_preferences_remote_asset_library()`:
```
BLI_assert failed: source/blender/blenlib/BLI_map.hh:1174, add_new__impl(), at
'!this->contains_as(key)'
```

This makes sense, if two threads are working in this function at the
same time. One thread notices the asset library is not present in the
map, creates it and loads catalogs from disk. Meanwhile, another thread
also notices the library is not present in the map and does the same.
Eventually they will both try to insert into the map, causing the failed
assert.

An asset browser visible in the startup file may load in parallel to the
global asset list storage used by other asset UI elements.

I use recursive mutexes, because when loading the all library there will
be nested locking. All library loading will call
`foreach_loaded_asset_library()` (locking the mutex) and pass a callback
that will load asset libraries (also locking the mutex).

subject: Rigging: Add Head/Tail slider for object-bone parenting
message:
Rigging: Add Head/Tail slider for object-bone parenting

When parenting objects to bones using the `Bone` Parent Type, the existing code positions the object relative to the *tail* of the bone, something that has been [pointed out](https://blender.stackexchange.com/questions/295201/why-does-parenting-to-a-bone-put-the-object-at-the-bone-tail) as being very unintuitive and unexpected.

The options to mitigate this were:

* Add an Empty with a `Copy Transforms` constraint pointing to the bone, then parent the child to the Empty. (convoluted, increases scene complexity).
* Manually add a local transform to the child to position it at the head. (if bone length is changed, the child transform must also be manually changed to match).

Assets: Better handle deleted libraries in asset shelves

An asset library may be deleted in the Preferences while asset shelves
are displaying it. The behavior there wasn't well defined, and some
glitches could happen or Blender could crash even.

happen when switching to a workspace with an asset shelf showing the
deleted library (would have to be the last library in the Preferences

but we're lacking a good way to "subscribe" to library deletion. The
explicit sanitizing is entirely handled internally in the asset shelf
code and it's cheap to do, so it should be okay.

subject: Anim: Implement Transformable API
message:
Anim: Implement Transformable API

This implements a generic API to transform bones and objects through a
unified interface. It is extendable to support 2D data as well.
This API is implemented to the pose slide code which now no longer
deals with `bPoseChannel` directly.
Due to that it is possible to extend the pose slide code into
objects as demonstrated by this proof of concept: !157267 and !154309
From the users perspective this is a non-functional change.

**Transformable**
Is a struct that keeps pointers to the values of the struct it wraps.
This class is focused on transform values, as such it does not deal
with BBone properties or custom properties.
Doing so keeps it lean and focused.
The values it returns are always a copy, never the original data.
The intention here is to provide a clean separation of concerns where
the user of a Transformable cannot unknowingly modify data of the struct.
It has to be explicit through a function call.
The class has functions to get, set and blend values.

It is similar to RNA in that it abstracts away the exact naming and
layout of the structs. However RNA has the issue that the names may not
be consistent between various structs. By being focused on transform
values and not relying on string names this class works around that issue.

**Rotation**
This is a new struct that combines rotation values and the mode those
values are in. With this information we can convert values to different
rotation modes with confidence.

Part of #156579

subject: Fix: "Downloading Asset(s)" not disappearing after assets are downloaded

Fix: "Downloading Asset(s)" not disappearing after assets are downloaded

The statusbar would keep showing the "Downloading Asset(s)" button, even
after all asset downloads finished.

After a recent change (I guess 80b3fc1080 ?), the status of downloaders
would only indicate that they are done downloading _after_ the
individual pings for finished asset file downloads were sent. That means
our idea of querying the status on this "finished asset file download"
ping to recognize when the downloaders are done wouldn't work anymore.

Instead, use the new `download queue empty` callback (added in
15abc945a2) of the downloader to send a dedicated ping to Blender. This
makes the previously needed function to query the downloader status from
C++ unnecessary, so it's removed here.

Semantically, the callback should also be called when all asset
downloads were cancelled. This wasn't the case and is fixed too here to
ensure the status bar button disappears in that case too.

subject: BLI: add new BLI_assert_unreachable_static macro
message:
BLI: add new BLI_assert_unreachable_static macro

This is a version of `BLI_assert_unreachable` can be used at compile time. This
is especially useful in `std::visit` calls to make sure that each type is
handled. Without this, there is no error or warning when a type is not handled
which can lead to bugs when new types are added to a `std::variant`.

There are two versions of this new macro:
* `BLI_assert_unreachable_static` can always be used when some line shouldn't be
  reached based on `constexpr if` statements.
* `BLI_assert_unreachable_static_t` same as above, but one can pass in a type as
  parameter. It's functionally the same but results in an error message that
  contains the unhandled type.

field does not need to be evaluated on the full domain. The behavior for
unselected elements is the same as in the Store Named Attribute node when a new
attribute is created, i.e. the values are initialized to their default value

subject: Nodes: Right-aligned text input and allow renaming more sockets in place
message:
Nodes: Right-aligned text input and allow renaming more sockets in place

**Problem**
Several nodes can be extended with custom sockets. Except for the
Index Switch, all these nodes allow user-defined sockets to be renamed in their
Node Properties. Some of these allow renaming user-defined sockets in the node
itself (unless a default value widget is being drawn in its place).

Among these, only the Group Input, Group Output, Closure, Evaluate Closure and
the new Field to List nodes lack this convenience. In part, this is due to the
lack of support for right-aligned text input fields, since renamable output
sockets should be rendered right-aligned.

**Solution**
Text fields can now be right-aligned, even during editing. To
support this, the `UILayout.prop` Python method now accepts an `align` argument
with values `'LEFT'/'RIGHT'` (defaulting to `'LEFT'`).

Internally, a new flag, `eUI_Item_Flag::ITEM_R_TEXT_RIGHT`, supports creating
buttons for RNA text properties with the `BUT_TEXT_RIGHT` *drawflag*. This flag
reuses the first bit, which had been previously used for `ITEM_O_RETURN_PROPS`
(now unused).

Text clipping of edited text has been improved to make use of all available
space.

User-defined sockets in Group Input, Group Output, Closure, Evaluate Closure,
and Field to List nodes can now be renamed in place, by pressing `Ctrl+LMB`,
like other nodes with user-defined sockets.

subject: Assets: add min/max version of Blender to online asset listing
message:
Assets: add min/max version of Blender to online asset listing

Add two Blender versions to each asset in the online asset listing:
`min` and `until`. The asset is shown in Blender if `min <=
BLENDER_VERSION < until`.

This includes changes to the schema, the listing generator, and
Blender itself to do the filtering.

This is intended for two things:

- Ensuring older Blenders don't see assets that are made with a newer
  version of Blender.
- Making it possible to replace assets, where older Blender versions
  still see the older version of the asset, and newer versions of
  Blender only see the newer asset.

Example listing JSON:

```json
{
  "name": "Mrežnica",
  "id_type": "WORLD",
  "files": ["worlds.blend"],
  "bl_versions": {
    "min": "5.2"
  },
  "thumbnail": {
    "url": "worlds_thumbnails/World/mreznica.webp",
    "hash": "SHA256:9785a7e242dbd8ff973736c51fb09a6a1efe401dfff62d38f38d9fb48b7f6e46"
  },
  "meta": {
    "catalog_id": "efd4ea51-c968-44a6-9781-09c20796e8a6",
    "tags": ["River", "Croatia", "HDRi"],
    "author": "Sybren A. Stüvel",
    "description": "HDRi of river Mrežnica in Croatia"
  }
},
```

The listing generator writes the version of Blender that was used to
save the blend file.

Once an asset is downloaded, it will always be shown, regardless of
the version of Blender used. That may be changed in a future PR, but
such filtering is out of scope for this one.

Note: after landing this, all remote asset listings need to be
regenerated. Without a `bl_versions.max` field, the asset will not be
shown in Blender.

subject: Fix #158644: Crash on operator redo
message:
Fix #158644: Crash on operator redo

Caused by a28091feec7081e98c02d6f81bef154db511e640

The issue was that on undo the bone indices are discarded,
so any modification to the redo panel would hit issues where
the bone could not be found from the pose bone.

The fix is to remove the pure `bPoseChannel` overloads
of `bone_is_visible` and `bone_is_selected`.
This moves the responsibility of getting the `Bone *`
to the caller who can then choose to either do
`bPoseChannel.bone_get(armature)` or `bPoseChannel.bone_get(object)`.
The latter is safer as it rebuilds the bone indices.

For all calls to the removed functions the latter call was used.
This should have no performance impact since
`BKE_pose_ensure_bone_indices` only does an actual rebuild if it is
required. It does so by comparing the `generation_count` integer on
the armature and pose, and the size of the bones array. Both calls
should be very cheap

There used to be two APIs to set the default of a node:

  generally can just stay at the default).

"middle" and "large", the names just encode the actual integer size now. Also,
these presets take the grid spacing into account, so they are all multiples of

multiple of 20.

Fix #157234: Wrong FCurve flags for property type

The issue happens when node sockets change order and is caused by the
following chain of events.
* in `versioning_450.cc` line 4132 we run `update_autoflags_fcurve_direct`
* however at that point, the fcurve rna path resolves to a property
that is an enum so the `FCURVE_DISCRETE_VALUES` is set
* then we modify the rna path in `versioning_500.cc` 2867 to
point to the new property index on the node but we don't clear the flag

The fix is to do an RNA path resolve in `fcurves_path_rename_fix`
and update the fcurve flags.
Doing so can be a performance bottleneck.

However
* The RNA resolve will only run if the path was actually changed
* The versioning code will only run once per file,
so saving the file in the new version will solve the performance issue.
* I tested a few old files and I cannot notice a difference
in opening times, though I didn't do ms measurements

subject: Geometry Nodes: use SocketValueVariant directly in baked data
message:
Geometry Nodes: use SocketValueVariant directly in baked data

Previously, when working with baked data (through the Bake node or Simulation
Zone) all data was converted into `BakeItem` values. During this conversion,
anonymous attributes were removed, material persistency was handled etc. While
this processing is still necessary, a separate data type (`BakeItem`) is not.
Instead we can just use `SocketValueVariant` all the way down. This helps
especially with recursive data like when geometries contain bundles which can
contain arbitrary data which was not supported before.

This also improves the behavior for fields in baked data. Now every
pure-attribute fields (including anonymous attributes created with a capture
node) are stored in the bake. It does not do an additional evaluation of the
field in this case. For non-attribute fields, the behavior is the same as
before: the field is evaluated on the previous geometry on the domain set in the
node. This new behavior is necessary to support storing fields in bundles
(including geometry bundles) and overall gives more flexibility when explicitly
capturing the field before it is passed into the node.

Overall, this results in a simplification while providing more functionality.

subject: Fix: SVG to Grease Pencil import gives erroneous fills/missing strokes
message:
Fix: SVG to Grease Pencil import gives erroneous fills/missing strokes

If an SVG contains a shape with a fill or a shape with no stroke, then
importing it as a Grease Pencil object would sometimes create shapes
with missing strokes, or black fills where there should be no fills at
all.

This happens because `CurvesGeometry::resize()` does not initialize
newly-created attribute values, and `hide_stroke` and `fill_id` were
only written to for shapes with no strokes and shapes with fills,
respectively, so shapes that did not meet these conditions may end up
using garbage values for these attributes. This was only a problem if
those attributes were created in the first place, hence the condition
that a shape with a fill or no stroke be present in order to trigger the
bug.

The fix here is to always write to `hide_stroke` and `fill_id` if those
attributes exist. To retain the previous behavior of not creating these
attributes until needed, explicit conditions are put in to add these
attributes upon encountering a shape with a fill or no stroke.

subject: Anim: Extend the 'Add Bone' redo panel
message:
Anim: Extend the 'Add Bone' redo panel

Often when adding a bone at the cursor you then need to scale and/or
rotate it to match world space (technically object space)
and later remember to disable the deform option before using the
automatic weighting.
Adding extra functionality to the redo panel can speed up that
workflow by consolidating many steps.

### Space
* Object: The newly created bone will use Object Space
co-ordinate system
* World: The newly created bone will use World Space co-ordinate system

### Align
* Up: Make the bone visually point upwards so the long axis is aligned
with the World/Object positive Z axis (depending on the space)
* Axes: Align the new bone to match the axes of the World/Object
* 3D Cursor: Align new bone to match the axes of the 3D cursor
* Viewport: Align new bone to match the axes of the 3D viewport

Default Option:
The default option does not change the current behavior.
However, there is a user preference setting that allows the user to
spawn objects to be viewport aligned. This also extends to bone creation.
If the user has this enabled then this PR will respect that.

### Enable Deform
This will let you disable the deform option when creating a bone.
Helpful when you are creating a bunch of control bones.

### Length
Defines the length of the new bone.
The PR also scales the B-Bone and Envelope size to match the length.
It matches the existing math which is 0.1 * the length.

Making the new b-bone/envelope scale match the new length will
be helpful when creating a bunch of small control bones in
Octahedral view, and then later changing the display mode.

message:
Fix: VSE: Off-by-one error with prefetching

Prefetching would always start one frame *past* the playhead, which was
reasonable before, where the main thread would take care of the current
frame before starting prefetch.

Now `cfra` can be nowhere near the playhead (e.g. playhead is far into
negative frames and prefetching starts at `timeline_start`); in this
case the first timeline frame would be dropped.

There should be no issues with wasted results, since prefetching does
not start until we render the first final frame, at which point if the
prefetch thread tries to re-render that frame it'll just find it in the
cache.

subject: ImBuf: Implicit sharing for CPU buffers
message:
ImBuf: Implicit sharing for CPU buffers

The current mechanisms to avoid copying ImBuf CPU buffers either do not
work in some situations, are fragile, or add too much code complexity
compared to implicit sharing / copy-on-write. This PR implements those
features for the float and byte CPU buffers. The existing "refcounter"
remains, in order to simplify the change, and because it isn't clear how
it should interact with GPU textures. Implicit sharing is added to the
file output compositor node and replaces the need for "externally owned"
semantics in the compositor's "Result" class, at least for the CPU
buffers. In that class, switching to ImplicitSharingPtr for the RAII
features made the change simpler.

Copying `ImBuf` is now quite cheap, and it should be possible to benefit
from this to simplify the code further in the future. For now, this is
used to simplify the image undo tile and paint tile implementations.

message:
Fix #156278: Grease Pencil strokes are slightly noisy in the render

The root cause of the issue seems to have been the fragment
interpolation from the vertex data. Since this is hardware dependent,
some people could not reproduce this issue.

In `gpencil_frag.glsl`
```glsl
col = col * gp_interp.color_mul + col.a * gp_interp.color_add;
```
the `gp_interp.color_mul` is interpolated for each fragment and
happend to be 1 for some fragments but only very close to 1 for others.

The fix clamps any value above `1.0f - 1e-6f` to `1.0f` which removes
the noise.

This adds back lightprobe plane support for Blended Material
and Shader to RGB evaluation.

This adds a parallax property on the Lightprobe Planes to tweak
the amount of (non-physical) distortion caused by normals.

Unlike legacy EEVEE (4.1) this implementation does not do any
raytracing even if raytracing is enabled in the render options.
Instead, it uses the same heuristic when raytracing was disabled
in 4.1. However, it now uses the new parallax amount from the
planar lightprobe property.

The heuristic fades out reflections if the normal differs from
the reflection direction or if roughness is not small.

To avoid big regression in compile time, the sampling of the
planar probe is done only once for all the BSDFs and using the
average normal.

message:
Cycles: HIP-RT: Dynamically select BVH build quality per BLAS

BLAS builds in the HIP-RT used hiprtBuildFlagBitPreferHighQualityBuild
regardless of geometry complexity or available GPU memory. On heavy
scenes this could exhaust VRAM, and for geometries that don't benefit
from SAH-optimized BVH the memory cost is unnecessary.

The change in this PR aims to address this issue by implementing a
per-BLAS heuristic that selects between high quality and balanced, based
on GPU memory pressure (consuming more than 25% of available RAM) and
AAB spatial overlap ratio for custom primitives.

subject: Fix #156702: Issues with using DJV as animation player
message:
Fix #156702: Issues with using DJV as animation player

Since `8d2c71c4c15cdc9de6f983a1d17e58394b116cd4` we always set the
process's OCIO environment var and this will be inherited when invoking
other executables like DJV through python.

Unfortunately DJV 2 does not support OpenColorIO v2 so DJV fails to open
correctly. DJV 3 was released last year that addresses this problem,
however, it's wildly different than its prior version. Namely, at least
on Windows, it no longer writes out its location in the prior registry
location AND it now seems to support side by side installs so that e.g.
DJV 3.3.3 and DJV 3.3.4 can coexist at the same time.

Additionally, the command line options supported are different.

This PR picks the latest version of 3.x to invoke on Windows, falling
back to DJV 2 if not found. MacOS checks its versioned paths. And Linux
assumes that DJV 3.4+ is being used. If DJV 2 is used, we will unset the
OCIO env var.

subject: Texture Paint: Apply parallelization to 3D brush implementation
message:
Texture Paint: Apply parallelization to 3D brush implementation

This change applies parallelization to the main 3D texture painting
brush implementation. Work is broken into two parallel steps:
* Create an `IndexMask` of initial rows to calculate based on the
  coarse triangle AABB brush intersection test
* Calculate a per-pixel, per-`PackedPixelRow` `float` factor based on
  the 3D distance and brush parameters, in parallel, then use this to
  calculate and write the new color
* Perform a parallel reduction to get the 2D bounds of the image that
  needs to be marked as dirty

There are still further performance improvements to be made, but for
a low-poly example of a cube with a 4096x4096 image texture, we see
a 53% speedup (0.65s to 0.30s). Gains for a denser mesh are much
more modest at about 11% (0.62s to 0.55s).

subject: Geometry Nodes: experimental hair physics using XPBD
message:
Geometry Nodes: experimental hair physics using XPBD

This adds new **experimental** built-in nodes and a couple of node group assets
which allow simulating hair curves and are fundamental building blocks for more
physics systems in the future.

At the highest level, there is a new "Hair Dynamics" asset which can be used as
modifier or as a node. It takes in hair curves with their corresponding surface
geometry and animates/simulates them based on the surface movement and other
effectors.

This is a fairly large node group which sets up a simulation world bundle that
ends up being passed to the new built-in "XPBD Solver" node. This node actually
updates the position, rotation, velocity and angular velocity attributes based
on the passed in constraints and forces. Note that this node generally needs
some setup like pre-evaluated fields and should generally be used as part of a
node group.

### World Bundle

The constraints as well as the simulated geometry are passed to the solver node
in form of a "world bundle". This bundle declaratively describes what the
physics system looks like.

It is a potentially potentially deeply nested bundle which contains so called
"typed bundles". The typed bundles correspond to specific constraint types based
on their type. Besides typed bundles, it also contains geometries which are
simulated.

Due to their generic nature (just a bundle), world bundles can be composed from
other bundles. For example, it is common to combine multiple
effectors/constraints into one bundle which is then added to the world bundle at
once. Objects can also "export" bundles on the geometry like force fields or
other constraints which can then be passed into the simulation on another
object.

### Constraint Types

The following constraint types are currently supported in the XPBD Solver node:
* Mesh colliders: Handles general collisions with closed(!) meshes.
* Infinite plane colliders: Can handle e.g. an infinite ground plane
  efficiently.
* Damping: General damping of linear and angular velocities to increase
  stability.
* Pin Position: Explicitly pin the position of individual points. Used for hair
  root points.
* Pin Rotation: Explicitly pin the rotation of individual points/segments. Used
  for hair root points.
* Rod Stretch/Shear: Attempts to maintain a specific rest length of a curve
  segment (stretch) and ensures that the rotation of the segment aligns with
  point positions (shear).
* Rod Bend/Twist: Attempts to maintain a specific rotation between neighboring
  segments.
* Edge Length: Constrains the length of mesh edges to a given rest length.
* Cross Edge Length: A cheap bending constraint that works by adding a distance
  constraint of two vertices opposite an edge.

Most of these constraints also have a compliance value. It indicates how much
the constraint is allowed to be broken. A value of zero means that the contraint
should be perfectly maintained. Sometimes this cannot be achieved due to too few
substeps or constraint steps, or because the way the system is setup makes it
impossible. Since this is a very non-linear value, it is generally exposed as a
"softness" value between 0 and 1 (although technically there is no upper limit).
It's also named e.g. "Bendiness" or "Stretchiness" depending on the context.

### Other New Nodes

Besides the solver node, there are two additional new built-in nodes. These are
required to build the higher level assets.
* Transfer Attributes: Allows copying all or a subset of attributes from one
  geometry to another using custom ids on each domain for the mapping.
  Importantly, this is even capable of transferring anonymous attributes.
* Tag Filter: A simple node that takes a list of tags and a filter string and
  checks if the filter matches the tag list. Currently, only a comma separated
  list is allowed as filter but a slightly more complex syntax may be supported
  in the future. The goal is to be able to reuse the same syntax across
  different tagging systems in Blender.

### Field Pre-evaluation

The XPBD Solver node does not evaluate any fields itself currently. Instead it
relies on other nodes to pre-evaluate these fields and to write them in specific
named attributes for easy consumption.

Besides simplifying the solver, this appears to be necessary to cleanly support
constraints which are interpolated across the substeps like pinning constraints.
For those, the solver not only needs the current pin position, but also the pin
position from the previous time step. Doing this attribute handling entirely
outside of the solver node allows it to be used more ways.

Two different kinds of pre-evaluations are necessary:
* Hard-coded attribute names: The solver reads from (and sometimes writes to)
  these hard-coded attribute names directly. This includes `position`,
  `velocity`, `rotation`, `angular_velocity`, `external_force`,
  `external_torque`, `mass`, `moment_of_inertia`, `static_friction`,
  `dynamic_friction`, `radius`.
* Effector specific attributes: Some effectors (like the Pin Position
  constraint) needs additional attributes on the geometries it affects. In this
  specific case, it's necessary to know for the current and previous frame which
  points are pinned and where (and that per constraint when there are multiple).
  * The used naming convention for these attributes is:
    `sim:prop:{effector_path}:{property_name}` (e.g. `sim:prop:Hair/Pin
    Position:selection`). The effector path is the bundle path starting at the
    root bundle.
  * The data from the previous frame is stored with a very similar naming
    convention: `sim::prop_prev:{effector_path}:{property_name}`.
  * Note that outside of building fully custom simulation systems, the user is
    never expected to deal with these attributes manually. This is entirely
    handled in existing node groups.

### Todos before release

Before this is released, a few things need to be done:
* New node group assets still need to be finalized, especially with respect to
  the surface geometry and forces.
* The already existing hair assets need to be updated too.
* The operator to set up hair needs to be updated.

contains a single set of push constants and can lead to many small
buffers.

This PR bundles the push constants into larger buffers. These buffers
are owned by the context. The buffers have a fixed size and reallocates
new buffers when needed. The buffers are discarded when the render
graph is flushed.

This change doesn't change any performance, but would reduce the amount
of buffers in play.

message:
Fix #157740: EXR images with a single Z or Depth channel open black

EXR images only containing a single "Z" or "Depth" channel are
displayed either fully black or sometimes noisy.

This is because this single channel does not match any of the
combinations of channels that Blender uses to load EXR images.
As a result no channel data is read at all, leaving the image buffer
uninitialized, resulting in black or noisy images from the garbage in
memory.

To fix this add a case detecting that the file contains an unknown
channel and loads this as grayscale if other combinations are no
better match.

subject: Vulkan: Fix compilation when VK_USE_64_BIT_PTR_DEFINES is not 1
message:
Vulkan: Fix compilation when VK_USE_64_BIT_PTR_DEFINES is not 1

When `VK_USE_64_BIT_PTR_DEFINES` is not 1 the (default) underlying type
of dispatchable vulkan object handles is `uint64_t`. This causes C++ to
complain about multiple to_string functions with the same type.

It may be possible for this to break when a custom
`VK_DEFINE_NON_DISPATCHABLE_HANDLE` is used but in such cases it should
always possible to fix that by setting `VK_USE_64_BIT_PTR_DEFINES`
explicitly as well.

An alternative could be to use something like
`VK_DEFINE_NON_DISPATCHABLE_HANDLE(object) typedef struct { uint64_t handle; } object;`
but it would prevent custom `VK_DEFINE_NON_DISPATCHABLE_HANDLE` entirely.

(A template hell using `std::enable_if` may be possible as well but I
wouldn't recommend it)

Ref https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_DEFINE_NON_DISPATCHABLE_HANDLE.html
