subject: Geometry Nodes: Add Merge by Distance building block nodes
message:
Geometry Nodes: Add Merge by Distance building block nodes

The main goal of this PR is to add the ability to replace the Merge by
Distance node with customizable node groups built on top of smaller and
more generic building blocks. The main part of that plan is the Merge
Points node which works with the Group ID of vertices so merging
geometry can be defined directly by the selection, indices and groups,
without the need for the current workaround of changing positions and
dealing with floating point precision issues at far coordinates in order
to avoid false positive merges.

In addition to just editing of the mesh and the point cloud, this PR
also adds a pair of nodes to reproduce "by Distance" part. The Cluster
by Distance node works similarly to Index of Nearest but instead of
knowing local most nearest elements, now each point knows the ID of the
cluster of some size it belongs to. Internally this is done in non-
trivial way which is hard to reproduce as user level currently. And both
optimizations and different algorithms for that problem can be add later.

The other new node, Cluster by Connected, is currently just designed to
replace the "Connected Only" feature of the Merge by Distance node.

From performance side this change does not have a large impact. The main
bottleneck is the mesh merge part (clusterization cost is smaller).

Refactor: RNA: Use parsed DNA structs instead of renamed SDNA

RNA used the SDNA blob which has renames baked in, and would then
imperfectly map it back to the original C++ names that we are actually
binding to. With recent DNA refactoring we can get the structs and
members without the renames, and make the implementation for mapping

can avoid substiting some C++ types to bind them directly with RNA.

subject: Fix: correctly handle HTTP download sizes when stream compression is used
message:
Fix: correctly handle HTTP download sizes when stream compression is used

When HTTP stream compression was used, it would break conditional HTTP
downloading, because the streamed (so compressed) number of bytes of the
request was compared with the on-disk (so decompressed) size of the
downloaded file.

This is now fixed, and some other size-related fields have been renamed
to make it explicit that they are about the on-disk size.

Since this changes how the HTTP request metadata is stored on disk,
exising entries never match the on-disk file, and so every conditional
download will just re-download the file. This can't be helped, because
it's unknown whether the original request used stream compression or
not.

subject: Assets: add Python function to cancel download
message:
Assets: add Python function to cancel download

Introduce download cancellation functions, for the HTTP downloader in
general, and for asset downloading.

Thumbnails and the downloading of asset library listings cannot be
cancelled. These are expected to be relatively small anyway.

The design:

- The HTTP downloader returns the exact URL that's being downloaded.
  This value is returned by the various abstraction layers in between.
  This ensures that the correct URL is known, regardless of the
  adjustments made by these abstraction layers (turning relative URLs
  into an absolute one, adding the expected file hash, etc.)
- The downloading URL is used to identify which download should be
  cancelled.
- When the same URL is queued for downloading multiple times, all of
  them are cancelled by a single call to the cancel function.
- Cancelling a URL that is not known to the downloader (because it was
  never requested, or because it's already fully downloaded) is a
  valid operation. It's simply a no-op.

Relevant for the calls from C++:

- `download_asset_file()` now returns the URL that was queued.
- `cancel_download()` takes the URL of the asset library (to identify
  the downloader instance) and the URL returned by the function above.
- Cancellation will be reported as 'download error' with
  `http_dl.DownloadCancelled` as exception type.

subject: Fix #157474: Blender crash when using undo while editing pose
message:
Fix #157474: Blender crash when using undo while editing pose

At runtime, keep track of the bones of an Armature in a flat array. The
pose object's `bPoseChannel::bone` pointers are replaced with the bone's
index in that array. This makes the lookup of those bones independent of
the memory location of the armature data.

Removes `BKE_pose_remap_bone_pointers()`, which is no longer needed
because the index-based lookup survives armature copies.

This fixes a crash that happened in quite a complex scenario:

- Packed-linked armature object.
- Library override on the object so it can be posed.
- Move a bone, then undo.
- The undo system would also rewrite the pack-linked Armature data,
  invalidating the `bPoseChannel::bone` pointers in both Armature object
  instances (the originally-linked one, and the library override).
- Only one of those object instances was flagged for rebuilding.
- Move a bone again, which triggers the diffing process for the library
  override.
- This would access the now-invalid bone pointers of the not-updated
  Armature object instance, and crash Blender.

`bPoseChannel::bone` was stored in DNA, but treated as runtime data
(written as `nullptr`, reconstructed on read). It has been removed
entirely from DNA.

Invariant: each `bPoseChannel::runtime::bone_index` index into its
armature's `runtime::bones` array. Two mechanisms to maintain this
invariant:

- `Array<Bone *> bArmature::runtime::bones` is accessed by
  `bArmature::bone_get_indexed()`. If the array is empty, it is
  automatically rebuilt. Code that invalidates the array (for example
  because bones have been created/removed or reallocated) can just clear
  the array.

  Whenever this array is generated, a 'generation counter' is
  incremented.

- `int64_t bPoseChannel::runtime::bone_index` is used to call that
  `bone_get_index()` function, whenever the armature bone is needed. The
  value of `bone_index` needs occasional rebuilding as well, whenever
  the above `bones` array changes. This is detected by keeping a copy of
  the generation counter that was last used. If the Armature has a
  different generation counter, it automatically triggers a re-indexing
  of the bones.

The Armature's generation counter is initialized by the Armature's
`session_uid`. This ensures that swapping out the `ob->data` pointer to
another Armature gets detected as a change, and thus will trigger the
re-indexing of the bones.

This newly introduced structure helps to fix the issue in two ways:

- Direct pointers to sub-data of another ID (so from Object to sub-data
  of the Armature) are removed.
- The data model itself contains the necessary information to determine
  whether the bones need re-indexing. This means it is no longer
  necessary for code that edits the Armature data to visit all Objects
  that use the Armature to set the right flags.

This is built on top of the `bPoseChannel::bone_get()` functions
introduced in 092af9d7c04759e82e3142678da899f0cc447ca3.
Bugs latent in that commit may suface now that the stub `bone_get()`
function has been replaced. Unit tests have been added to cover the
main code paths.

subject: BLI_delaunay_2d: replace ray-cast with topology even-odd hole detection
message:
BLI_delaunay_2d: replace ray-cast with topology even-odd hole detection

Replace the multi-threaded per-region ray-cast detector with a more
efficient single-threaded flood-fill that visits each face & edge once.

Performance:

As the slowdown wasn't linear and depended on available threads,
the improvement depends on the system & polygon complexity.
From my tests on a complex polygon with many holes, ~99k edges:

Speedup, comparing the old/new methods:

- 1 thread: ~44x
- 4 threads: ~22x
- 16 threads: ~11x

... more threads after that didn't make a significant difference.

Implementation:

This matches the existing non-zero detector which also uses CGAL's
approach (`mark_domain_in_triangulation` in `Triangulation_2`).

The old detector grouped faces into regions and, for each region, cast
a ray from a face to a fixed far-off point and counted edge crossings.

The new one starts at the outer boundary and walks inward through
connected regions, flipping the fill state each time it crosses an
input polygon boundary.

Details:

- Fix for edge-case:
  each edge now stores how many input polygon boundaries share it,
  and the per-edge parity flip is `count & 1`.
  An edge shared by two boundaries contributes no flip,
  so overlapping shapes - stacked rectangles, coincident edges -
  now fill correctly under the SVG/PostScript even-odd rule.
  The old detector counted such edges once.

- Inputs without overlapping boundaries are unaffected by the
  boundary-count change, though some may still differ where the old
  ray-cast happened to intersect a vertex exactly or overlapping edge.

- Update `NonZeroWindingFan` and `NonZeroWindingCoincidentVerts` to match.

- See `detect_holes_with_fillrule_even_odd`
  and`polygon_boundary_count_map` code-comments for details.

USD: Implement incremental save for export

USD export currently only saves to disk at the very end of export. Due
to how USD de-duplicates data, all timeSamples remain in memory until
that time. This is problematic for cases such as #156402 that, due to
their size, quickly exhausts memory.

The solution is to call Stage Save() throughout the export process
instead of waiting until the end. However, it needs to be configurable.
Incremental saves have caused issues in the past for Google Drive
locations and it will be slower to export (slightly). Additionally, it's
not trivial or elegant to estimate the size of the exported data either.
We leave it up to the user to decide how frequently to save.

The new option will be displayed when the Animation option is selected.

Fixes #156402

subject: Fix: Memory leak when refreshing library while previews are pending
message:
Fix: Memory leak when refreshing library while previews are pending

Refreshing an asset library means the assets get destructed, which will
also "release" the preview image. "Releasing" means, removing it from
the global preview cache, and either deleting it directly, or tagging it
for deletion if loading/downloading in a thread is ongoing still. That
means when the asset library reloads and re-requests previews, entirely
new previews will be requested. But the still pending requests will have
pointers that are not owned by the global cache anymore, and need
freeing. The `BKE_previewimg_render_end()` function is designed to
handle this freeing correctly.

subject: Fix #154319: Undefined behavior when repeatedly refreshing asset library
message:
Fix #154319: Undefined behavior when repeatedly refreshing asset library

There was a data race when a preview was re-requested that was still
being downloaded or loaded from disk.

If the re-request happened before finished requests were handled through
an update-timer tick (i.e. before `PreviewLoadJob::update_fn()` was
called through the timer), the now finished request would be pushed to
the todo queue again. When the update-timer tick would happen now, it
would handle the request as finshed and free it, not realizing that it
was pushed to the todo queue again. So the todo queue would hold a
dangling request pointer.

The solution is to not push the request to the todo queue again. Also
don't change the state, simply let any existing request finish cleanly.
The additional request still is to the same resource, so we don't need
to restart the request and just re-use the existing one.

subject: Fix #117656: system error when setting ID property to numpy values
message:
Fix #117656: system error when setting ID property to numpy values

When setting an ID property to some value for some numpy data types,
the assignment (or property creation) may succeed but a delayed system
error is thrown later. The system error is thrown because an earlier
exception was not caught.

This happens for data types that do not match a built-in Python type
(i.e. `PyLong_Check`, `PyFloat_Check`, etc. fail), but do seem to
support the mapping protocol, so we try to convert them with
`idp_from_PyMapping`. The silenced exception is actually thrown from
`PyMapping_Length` as the numpy objects do no have a `len` method.

According to the Python documentation, `PyMapping_Check` also succeeds
if the object implements `__getitem__` although it might not be a
mapping.

This adds some guards in `idp_from_PyMapping` to return null if querying
mapping information (keys, values, and length) fails. Returning null
ensures that later on we check for the exception and report it
correctly.

subject: Refactor: abstract away direct `bPoseChannel::bone` pointer access
message:
Refactor: abstract away direct `bPoseChannel::bone` pointer access

Abstract away the direct access to `bPoseChannel::bone`, by changing
each user to call `bPoseChannel::bone_get(object)` or
`bone_get(armature)` instead.

No functional changes intended, as currently `pchan->bone_get()` just
returns `pchan->bone`.

This refactor allows future changes, where the Armature bone is
returned based on an array index instead of a direct pointer.
Furthermore, some extra bookkeeping will be used to ensure these array
indices are up to date (instead of having to 'manually' flag armature
objects with `POSE_REBUILD`). But, in order to do this bookkeeping,
both the Object and the bArmature pointers have to be known; this is
why most use sites have been changed to `bone_get(object)`.

In hot loops this can be simplified to `bone_get(armature)`, with the
up-to-date-check outside the loop. That's for a future PR, though.

`blender::bke::PChanBone` and `PChanBoneConst` are introduced to
simplify passing the pair `{pchan, bone}` to functions. This way,
lookups only have to happen once, and subsequent code simply has
access to the pair. A limitation is that the constness of both
pointers is linked, so either both are mutable or both are const. In
the vast majority of cases this is what we need.

When a function gets both a `PChanBone` and an armature/object
pointer, this means the function walks the hierarchy in some way, and
needs to perform more bone lookups.

This also introduces `PointerRNA CTX_data_active_pose_bone_ptr(C)`. It
is part of the broader pattern established here: pchans should travel
with their owning object, not be looked up independently.

subject: EEVEE: Improve AO far occluders
message:
EEVEE: Improve AO far occluders

This improves far occluders contribution to the ambient occlusion
and Fast GI.

The previous implementation was discarding potential occluders based
on the sample distance regardless of the thickness value.

This resulted in over occlusion if the thickness was high and the sample
in range, and in under occlusion if the sample was far but its thickness
should have made it contributed.

To fix this we ideally need to clip the sample segment to the AO / GI
distance sphere. This is not so cheap, so we assume the ray is aligned
with the view Z axis which simplify the 3D problem to a 2D problem.

It gives exact results in orthographic camera mode but not in
perspective.
But the difference is minimal under non-extreme FOV. In the worst case,
it skew the contribution of the samples a bit.

Fix: BLI_delaunay_2d hole-detection slow with need_ids=false

Performance regression (likely from [0]) which could cause an
exponential slowdown. In my tests it's it gives significant slowdown
for a high poly stress test (between 10-100x depending on complexity).

`add_face_constraints` tagged face-boundary edges with id 0 instead of

then never matched any edge, so the interior flood escaped the face
and walked the whole CDT per input face.

Always pass `face_edge_id` - it's used internally as a boundary marker.
This doesn't imply orig array use, as they are not needed,
and won't be created (as they depend on `need_ids`).

subject: Compositor: Use depsgraph updates for triggering execution
message:
Compositor: Use depsgraph updates for triggering execution

This patch utilizes the dependency graph editor update mechanism to
trigger the execution of the interactive compositor. Previously, WM
notifiers were used to trigger execution but they were often not
granular enough or were missed in some cases. While depsgraph updates
are more reliable. This has the following improvements:

- Adding/adjusting a node that is not yet connected to the output will
  now no longer trigger a redundant execution.
- Undo that is not related to the compositor node tree will now no
  longer trigger a redundant execution. This also means that operators
  will no longer block in the 3D viewport.
- The compositor will properly execute on changes to cameras and objects
  referenced by the compositor.
- Frame changes will no longer execute the compositor if it does not
  depend on time.
- The interactive compositor is now more responsive since we schedule
  the job immediately after updates, instead of sending a notifier,
  waiting for the editor listener, tagging an editor refresh and finally
  scheduling the job.

Fixes #65926.

subject: PyAPI: expose ImBuf.with_buffer as a shaped memoryview
message:
PyAPI: expose ImBuf.with_buffer as a shaped memoryview

Previously the context manager yielded a flat 1-D memoryview for the
full image and a 2-D `(rows, columns * channels)` view for a region,
which obscured the geometry of the underlying pixels.

Returning shaped `(height, width, channels)` memoryview in both cases:

- Matches the shape convention used by `numpy` and other image
  libraries, and the shape of `bpy.types.Window.screenshot` so
  values can flow between them without reshaping.
- Enables direct per-pixel/per-channel indexing as `buf[y, x, c]`
  instead of computing a flat offset.

Bulk slice-assignment still requires 1-D on both sides
(a CPython limitation, `NotImplementedError`).

subject: Fix #156857: FPS Exceeded during playback with viewport interaction
message:
Fix #156857: FPS Exceeded during playback with viewport interaction

Correct the FPS averaging logic to show a correct value which
was previously biased to show a higher FPS on uneven playback.

Details:

The rolling FPS average was computed as the mean of the per-frame FPS
(1/interval).

Viewport interaction on heavier scenes (or any heavy operation
during playback) could delay the animation stepping timer,
causing the next timer update to use a short time to "catch-up",
where the timer fired again almost immediately.

The short catch-up interval produced a very large FPS sample that
skewed the mean, pulling the displayed FPS above the real playback rate.

Resolve by dividing the number of recent frames
by the time between the oldest and newest. The ring buffer
now stores frame timestamps rather than per-sample rates.

This results in much simpler code.

Ref !157678

subject: Fix: time reversing on Unix breaks animation playback
message:
Fix: time reversing on Unix breaks animation playback

On Unix/POSIX systems BLI_time_now_seconds{_i} wasn't monotonic
as documented. `gettimeofday` uses the system time - which may go
backwards if the time is set, from leap seconds or NTP server
adjustments as the system runs.

In practice this meant any operation depending on time could stutter
or pause when the time changed, animation playback could freeze
although it was always possible to cancel it by pressing escape.

Resolve using CLOCK_MONOTONIC, which typically increases from the
time the system started.

Details:

- WIN32 already used a similar value - where the exact starting
  time is an implementation detail instead of the time since the epoch.

- In micro-benchmarks the difference between both implementations
  is close to noise, although the new code is very slightly faster ~2%.

Ref !157993

subject: Tests: add & improve tests for BLI_delaunay_2d
message:
Tests: add & improve tests for BLI_delaunay_2d

Various improvements to BLI_delaunay_2d tests.

- Improve NestedHoles

  The existing checks only counted output verts and faces, so a bug
  that swaps which regions fill would preserve the totals and pass.

  Improve this test with per-face checks. Look up the innermost
  square's four input verts to ensure their topology is as expected.

- Ensure correct topology in NonZeroWindingSelfIntersect

  Asserting only that Even-Odd and Non-Zero face counts match
  allows bugs that flip both rules simultaneously
  (e.g., both returning 0 or 4) to pass.
  Further, checking the face count can't distinguish between
  filling the correct lobes versus the wrong side-wedges,
  as both yield 2 faces, leaving topology errors undetected.

  Ensure the face count to exactly 2 for each rule and verify
  the vertex coordinates of each lobe to ensure the correct
  triangles are generated.

- Improve NonZeroWindingMultiFaceEdge{Mixed}

  The previous assertions checked only relative face counts
  (`even-odd < non-zero` for the all-CCW case, `even-odd == non-zero`
  for the mixed CW/CCW case), so a balanced-swap regression that
  fills the wrong band could match the count and pass.

  Assert the exact triangles by input vertex id so balanced-swap
  regressions which don't change the face-count are caught.

- Add DisjointPolysInLargeHull

  None of the hole-detection tests used a region that connects
  to `outer_face` only through unconstrained triangulation edges,
  so the propagation of the "outside" classification across implicit
  edges was unverified.

  Test two disjoint triangles inside one convex hull.
  The gap between them is itself a triangle with no constrained edges;
  it must still classify as outside.
  Both even-odd and non-zero rules must produce the same 2-triangle
  result, with each filled triangle carrying the expected input id -
  so propagation across implicit edges is exercised directly.

- Add EvenOddNestedHolesDeep

  NestedHoles only goes two levels deep and ties no input ids to
  output faces, so an off-by-one parity bug that mis-fills an
  alternate ring while preserving the total face count would still pass.

  Add a more comprehensive test with alternating-fill rings,
  asserting both the total face count and which input ids appear on
  which output faces, so a parity off-by-one that preserves the count
  but shifts the filled rings is caught.

- Add EvenOddBoundaryDisagreement

  The boundary-disagreement branch of
  `detect_holes_with_fillrule_even_odd` reached when a region has
  multiple boundary edges to `outer_face` with mixed parity flips - was
  only handled by tests with uniform parity along a region's outer
  boundary.

  Add a test where outer and inner rectangles share part of the
  convex hull so a region reaches `outer_face` through edges that
  disagree on parity, catching a flipped conflict-resolution direction.

- Add SharedSplitBoundary

  No existing test produced more than one CDT edge between the same
  pair of regions, so the even-odd region-adjacency build's
  table edge deduplication step was unverified.

  Add two adjacent rectangles sharing a boundary split by a midpoint
  vertex, producing two CDT edges between the same region pair so
  the duplicate adjacency entry forces deduplication.

Ref !157979

subject: Refactor: simplify object/editmode armature selection code-paths
message:
Refactor: simplify object/editmode armature selection code-paths

Refactor code which was which was filtering object drawing at
multiple levels making it difficult to reason about and maintain.
This code had been incrementally updated,
exceptions for armature pose mode and edit mode remained in
`DRW_draw_select_loop` which no longer make sense.

One practical advantage of this change is that it is possible
for the caller to define the behavior of selection drawing,
where previously this was supported in most cases via a filter
argument but overridden in the case of armature edit/pose modes.

There should be no functional changes from a user perspective,
since this refactor should only change where filtering occurs.

**Internal Changes:**

Changes worth noting:

- The grease pencil engine was previously disabled for edit-armatures
  (and sometimes pose-mode) The object filter prevents grease pencils
  from drawing so it shouldn't make a difference in practice.

  If we wanted to enforce this, it should probably be applied for all
  non-grease-pencil edit-modes, not just armature.

- Remove: `ED_view3d_give_base_under_cursor_skip_editmode`
  This was added to fix #139014,
  it was needed because the callers filter argument was ignored
  in armature-edit-mode. Meaning objects could not be "picked".
  That fix is reverted in this commit as it is no longer needed.

**Details:**

Simplify `DRW_draw_select_loop` by removing special case
logic for poses and edit-mode armatures.

This is now handled by the filter enum `eV3DSelectObjectFilter`,
in the case of object-locking & pose-bones the
filter was ignored for `DRW_draw_select_loop`.
Move these checks to ED_view3d_select_filter_from_mode.

Also remove `use_obedit_skip` was was
misleading as it didn't skip the edit objects,
it just skipped edit-mode isolation that was only used for armatures.

Ref !155459

subject: Fix #157915: Freeze when deleting a scene asset
message:
Fix #157915: Freeze when deleting a scene asset

**Problem**
Deleting a scene asset causes Blender to freeze completely.

**Cause**
A deadlock occurs in `AssetLibrary::remap_ids_and_remove_invalid`. The
thread acquires the `local_id_assets_mutex` to iterate over local ID
assets. While still holding this lock, it calls `remove_asset()`, which
subsequently attempts to acquire the exact same non-recursive
`local_id_assets_mutex`, causing an infinite wait.

**Solution**
1. **Scope reduction:** Reduced the scope of the `local_id_assets_mutex`
   lock in `remap_ids_and_remove_invalid()`. The lock is now correctly
   released before the loop iterates over `removed_assets` to call
   `remove_asset()`.
2. **Future-proofing:** In `remove_asset()`, combined the two sequential
   `std::scoped_lock` declarations into a single variadic lock
   (`std::scoped_lock lock{asset_storage_.external_assets_mutex,
   asset_storage_.local_id_assets_mutex};`). This guarantees both locks
   are acquired simultaneously, preventing any potential lock-order
   deadlocks from other threads.

Fixes #157915

subject: Cycles: Implement attribute access in Raycast node
message:
Cycles: Implement attribute access in Raycast node

On the user side it is implemented using extensible socket declaration:
user now can add sockets to access attributes. It is done in the node
settings panel: adding attribute creates input and output socket. The
input socket is a string that denotes attribute to sample, and output
socket provides access to the value of the attribute. A little caveat
is that Color attribute create 2 sockets: one for color, and another
for alpha. This is because color in shader nodes is RGB.

Cycles SVM implementation is based on the existing NODE_ATTR SVM node:
Raycast generates a set of these nodes and uses existing attribute
evaluation on the hit_sd.

Cycles OSL implementation required a bit of trickery to make it fit
the AOT type of shader compilation. The node_raycast() shader outputs
attributes as arrays, and there are extra converter shaders compiled
dynamically to convert those arrays to individual values that could be
addressed by the nodes that use those attribute sockets. There is a
limitation: there could be only up to 32 or each of the float, alpha,
or color/vector attributes.

There is also a mechanism now in Cycles for shaders to request global
attributes. Without this Cycles will optimize all attributes that are
not used by a specific geometry, making it quite tedious to setup in a
way that raycast could still access those attributes. Without such
mechanism user would have need to add attribute nodes to every shader
and mix it in with some low non-zero weight to the output so that it
does not get optimized out. The implementation is not really ideal as
it might lead to situation when attributes are requested by unused
shaders, but it is the best we can do without more global refactor.

EEVEE implementation returns 0 for the attributes. It is quite tricky
to implement attribute sampling, so for now it is Cycles-only feature.

Ref #155590

`BKE_appdir_folder_caches` now always sets a path
(returns void), falling back to a `.cache/` subdirectory
of the session tempdir when the OS cache root is unavailable.

subject: Nodes: Transfer compatible reroute links on Swap
message:
Nodes: Transfer compatible reroute links on Swap

**Problem**
The Swap operator transfers links from the swapped node to the new node
based on socket names. Hence, swapping a reroute node (whose socket
names are an implementation detail) to another node usually leads to the
links (the main purpose of the reroute) not being transferred.

Furthermore, the swapped node inherits the reroute's position, which
leads to it having its top left corner anchored where the reroute was
before. This is an inconsistency with how swapping most nodes usually
allows the nodes to remain visually in the same position as the
previous node.

**Solution**
The Swap operator now transfers reroute links to the first socket with
compatible type of the new node. This enables a new workflow combining
the *Add Reroutes* and *Swap* operators.

The position of the swapped node is now centered horizontally where the
reroute was before. Its vertical position is shifted upwards slightly:
- Its label is centered at the same position as the reroute was before.
- If the node is collapsed, it appears vertically centered where the
  reroute was before. In particular, if the node has a single input or
  output socket, it will be displayed vertically at the same position
  where the reroute was before.

subject: BLI: optimize CPPType::get and simplify registration
message:
BLI: optimize CPPType::get and simplify registration

This uses the fact that we require `BLI_CPP_TYPE_REGISTER` to be called before
the corresponding `CPPType` is used. This allows the `CPPType::get` method to
just return the pointer without having to optionally lazily initialize the type.
This results in significantly less code and can potentially also improve
performance.

Due to the way this is implemented now with a global static variable, it is not
necessary to have `BLI_CPP_TYPE_MAKE` now. So only a single line is necessary to
create a `CPPType` now instead of two.

Since the types are not lazily initialized anymore, it is important to call the
register functions before tests start now. This was kind of a soft requirement
before but often worked without. Now there is an assert that checks when the
register call is missing.

This results in a 472kb smaller stripped binary size.

subject: Fix #157854: Fluid domain mesh missing in F12 render
message:
Fix #157854: Fluid domain mesh missing in F12 render

Fix #157854: Fluid domain mesh missing in F12 render

## Problem

Baked Mantaflow meshes are visible in the viewport but missing during F12 render.

## Cause

During render evaluation (`DAG_EVAL_RENDER`), the depsgraph builds a fresh context. In `fluid_modifier_processDomain`, cache reading (`manta_read_mesh`, etc.) was attempted before the fluid object was reallocated to match the cached configuration.

When `manta_needs_realloc` returned true, cache reading was skipped, causing a fallback to the domain bounding box instead of the baked mesh.

## Solution

Move `BKE_fluid_reallocate_fluid` to the start of the `if (read_cache)` block so the fluid object is always correctly allocated before reading cache data.

This ensures cache loading works correctly during render evaluation.

subject: Fix #120892: GHOXT/Wayland keyboard input for non English layouts
message:
Fix #120892: GHOXT/Wayland keyboard input for non English layouts

For keyboard layouts that don't map A-Z (Cyrillic for example)
there is a logical problem, as users want to be able to:

- Type text using their current layout.
- Activate Blender's key shortcuts.

For some layouts in Wayland, most keys were mapped to "Unknown Key"
making them useless for activating shortcuts.

Since X11 already worked around this [0], users migrating
from X11 to Wayland experienced it as a regression.

Resolve using a fallback layout which is used
when the active layout doesn't recognize a key.

The fix works by:

- When the keymap or active layout changes, search for a fallback layout.
- Calculate a "score" for each layout (number of known GHOST keys).
- Pick the layout with the highest score; if it beats the active
  layout's score, use it as the fallback.
- When a key lookup in the active layout returns an "Unknown Key",
  retry the lookup using the fallback layout.

Details:

- This doesn't impact characters entered for text insertion.
- When two layouts have a matching score, the first layout wins.
- Similar functionality was supported on X11 (see #47228), but it
  relied on `XLookupKeysym` which always used the first layout.
  This Wayland implementation is an improvement: it doesn't rely
  on layout order, instead selecting the layout with the most
  matching keys.

subject: Geometry Nodes: Deduplicate internal fields before evaluation
message:
Geometry Nodes: Deduplicate internal fields before evaluation

Currently some expensive nodes often occur multiple times in a field
network. For example, with the hair system it is common to use UV
sampling to propagate multiple attributes from the surface mesh to the
curves. Currently the fields are evaluated once for every occurrence of
the node.

This PR introduces a de-duplication step for internal fields in the
network. The hashing of field operations and input nodes is "upgraded"
to use more robust 128 bit hashing so that we can skip the equality step
after hashing. This is particularly sensitive because a naive
implementation would have exponential cost. For that reason we use a
cache to avoid a second deep hash computation when revisiting a field
node in the network.

The de-duplication has to run as a post-construction, pre-evaluation
step because fields are build in a decentralized way. Each field has no
idea about other fields that might be potential duplicates from
elsewhere in a node group evaluation.

Fun fact, the first steps for this were committed two years ago: 7ff752b7891a4c96c128b69eeff50f2b7e29986b

subject: Fix #155866: Geometry nodes transform gizmo rotates on scale
message:
Fix #155866: Geometry nodes transform gizmo rotates on scale

**Description of the problem addressed:**

Resolves #155866. When adjusting the scale of a rotated object using the
Geometry Nodes transform gizmo, the object inadvertently rotates. This occurs
because the gizmo applied the non-uniform scale via a direct matrix
multiplication on the 3x3 transformation matrix, which introduced shear. When
the modifier stack subsequently decomposed this matrix, the shear was
misinterpreted as a change in rotation.

**Description of the solution:**

Updated `TransformGizmos::update_scale_transform_and_target_property` to prevent
the introduction of shear. Instead of overwriting the original matrix with the
sheared result, the patch calculates the newly scaled matrix, extracts the
magnitude (length) of the new column vectors, and applies these new lengths
strictly to the original, orthogonal column directions. This ensures the scale
is applied correctly while perfectly preserving the original rotation, matching
the behavior of the standard Object Mode gizmo.

**Testing Performed:**
* **Non-uniform scaling:** Verified that scaling a rotated object on a single
  axis using the Geometry Nodes gizmo no longer causes rotation drift.
* **Uniform scaling:** Confirmed that scaling on all axes simultaneously still
  functions correctly.
* **Object mode parity:** Confirmed the behavior now identically matches the
  standard object mode transform gizmo.
* Tested thoroughly using the provided `gizmo_behavior.blend` file.

subject: Nodes: Preserve grid-alignment on Make Group
message:
Nodes: Preserve grid-alignment on Make Group

**Problem**

The Make Group operator can break grid-alignment of grouped nodes.
This is because when the nodes are copied into the new group, they are offset so
that their bounding box is centered around the canvas origin.

**Solution**

The offset applied to grouped nodes is now snapped to a multiple of
the node editor grid step. Nodes that were grid-aligned remain grid-aligned
after being grouped, and the relative positions of all nodes are kept intact.
Nodes that were not grid-aligned remain not aligned.

The Group Node which replaces the selected nodes is now also grid aligned, so
its offset relative to the bounding box of the grouped nodes is the same as was
applied to them. Besides making the node grid-aligned, this ensures that the
*Ungroup* operator commutes with *Make Group* without introducing drift.

In favor of making the nodes grid-aligned when possible, the positions of the
Group Input and Group Output nodes in the newly created group have been slightly
modified so that:
- The horizontal gap between them and the grouped nodes is now equal, 3 grid
  units (previously it was 3 and 2.5).
- If the leftmost and rightmost nodes were grid-aligned, they are horizontally
  grid-aligned.
- They are always vertically grid-aligned.

Fix: hidden instancers cause invalid visibility for selection drawing

In `DRW_draw_select_loop`, an instancer that wasn't drawn
(invisible self, not selectable, for example) never had the instancing
object filter applied. Its duplis then inherited a stale filter result,

that supports "SkipRecursive".

A new `has_duplis` argument lets the predicate avoid
work whose result the iterator would discard
(e.g. filtering an instancer whose instances are already hidden).

and iterate over dupli-instances - only to have them filtered out.

subject: Fix: Nodes: Crash when creating new panel toggle
message:
Fix: Nodes: Crash when creating new panel toggle

**Problem**
Attempting to create a new panel toggle from the Group Sockets
interface, after selecting a panel leads to a crash.

The `NODE_OT_interface_item_new_panel_toggle` operator attempts to set
the `is_panel_toggle` property before moving the socket to its panel.
The `is_panel_toggle` setter assumes that the socket is under a panel.
Attempting to set `is_panel_toggle` for a root socket causes the crash.

**Solution**
The setter has been updated to gracefully handle root sockets.

The `NODE_OT_interface_item_new_panel_toggle` operator now moves the new
socket into its panel before attempting to set `is_panel_toggle`, since
the setter now ignores root sockets. The setter was recently added to
ensure position invariants after (un)marking a socket as panel toggle in

enforced. The shader/geometry _Mix_ node in particular allows arbitrary
mix factors, which results in extrapolation and scaling instead of
rotation.

arbitrary angles.

subject: Fix #149284: Sculpt Expand Mask leaves visual artifacts
message:
Fix #149284: Sculpt Expand Mask leaves visual artifacts

## Problem
When using Mask Expand (Shift+A) in Sculpt Mode, glitchy face corners
appear to be masked but are not. They persist even after clearing the
mask. Inverting the mask will wipe them.

## Cause
BVH nodes for (Mesh and BMesh) have both unique and shared vertices.
The update function is only applied to unique vertices, and the dirty
check compares a node's unique vertex mask values before and after the
update. If only shared vertices of a node are changed, that node is
never tagged as dirty.

For vertices shared between multiple BVH nodes, this means that a vertex
may be both masked and unmasked at the same time, leading to the
behavior described above.

## Solution
To maintain full concurrency, the fix reads all vertices per node but
only writes to the unique vertices per node. However, this introduces a
race condition: reads of shared vertex mask values may occur before or
after writes by the node that owns them. To address this, an initial
mask snapshot is created to compare against.

subject: Refactor: Paint: Break apart `paint_row_float` & `paint_row_byte`
message:
Refactor: Paint: Break apart `paint_row_float` & `paint_row_byte`

This commit makes a number of changes to prepare for further
parallelization.

Instead of reading, blending, and writing pixels in a row one by one,
we now batch each operation together.

* The `paint_row_float` and `paint_row_byte` functions no longer exist
* The `ImBuf` float and byte data is no longer accessed on a per-pixel
  basis. Instead, they are cast to and used as `float4` & `uchar4`
  `MutableSpan`s
* A row is skipped for further processing if all the `factors` are 0,
  this replaces the existing `pixels_painted` check
* A `Vector<float4>` for holding the scene-linear pixel data is added.
* A `Vector<float4>` for holding the factorized per-pixel blend value
  is added.

Notably, this PR results in a return to roughly the same order of
magnitude of performance prior to recent changes that enforced always
blending in scene linear color space.

At the beginning of 5.2's Alpha, the related performance test for a
cube with a 4096x4096 byte texture took 0.778s. This increased to
4.535s with the previously mentioned changes, and is now back to 0.071s
with the current patch. This performance improvement is primarily due
to the new `pixels_painted` check, which avoids the reading, conversion
blending, conversion, and writing of new color data if a row of pixels
would be unaffected.

See PR for the full performance breakdown.

Part of #155365

subject: Cycles: Texture cache eviction for final renders
message:
Cycles: Texture cache eviction for final renders

Evict unused texture cache tiles between render tiles and multiviews, to
reduce memory usage. Tiles that were loaded but not accessed during the
previous render tile are freed before the next tile begins rendering.

A per-tile access state byte tracks three values (NONE, REQUESTED, USED)
and is used both to drive tile loading from cache misses and to decide
which loaded tiles can be evicted at tile boundaries.

Cache eviction is automatically enabled, but there is a debug option to
disable it. There is also an debug option to preserve a specified amount
of unused image texture memory to aoid avoid trashing unnecessarily in
simple cases. It increases peak memory usage to render faster, however
in tests on a Macbook M3 it did not seem worth it. But left in to
experiment on other devices and scenes.

subject: Fix #157310: Geometry Nodes format string assert with {s:01} string input
message:
Fix #157310: Geometry Nodes format string assert with {s:01} string input

Resolves #157310.

**Root Cause:** When using the Python-compatible format syntax in the Format
String node, the regex validation for the `width` parameter used `\d+`. This
allowed it to match numbers starting with `0` (e.g., `01`). However, the
underlying `fmt` library strictly parses a leading `0` as the zero-padding flag.
Because zero-padding is an invalid formatting operation for string types, `fmt`
throws a `fmt::format_error`. This exception bypassed the expected validation,
hitting the `BLI_assert_unreachable()` in the catch block and crashing Blender.

**Solution:** This PR updates `get_pattern_by_type_impl` to split the regex for
width and precision:
- The `width` regex is changed to `[1-9]\d*`, ensuring it strictly requires a
  non-zero starting digit.
- The `precision` regex remains capable of handling `0` (e.g., for `{:.0f}`).

**Result:** Entering an invalid format string like `{s:01}` now correctly fails
the node's pre-validation. Instead of a hard crash, the node safely halts
execution and displays a error warning in the UI, which is the expected
behavior for invalid format syntax.

subject: Fix #157280: Shader Weight sockets available with dynamic declarations
message:
Fix #157280: Shader Weight sockets available with dynamic declarations

Shader nodes with dynamic declarations receive incorrect values for
their "Weight" input socket. This causes wrong shader weighting in the
final material output.

The reason is that the "Weight" sockets commonly used in shader nodes
are by default declared _unavailable_, so that they don't show up in the
editor. These sockets are only used internally in the "localized" node
tree copy that is created before shader evaluation. After the localized
tree copy is created the Weight sockets are explicitly made available by
clearing the `SOCK_UNAVAIL` flag (`ntree_shader_weight_tree_invert`).

This is necessary because the subsequent `stack_index` allocation for
shader sockets is based on the topological order of nodes
(`get_node_code_gen_order`). The topological sorting ignores links
between unavailable sockets.

Shader nodes use a `ShaderValueNode` linked to the `Weight` socket.
To ensure correct `stack_index` the order should be, for example:
  [`ShaderValueNode`, `ShaderNodeSubsurfaceScattering`]
When the Weight socket is unavailable the `ShaderValueNode` gets placed
at the end of the list:
  [`ShaderNodeSubsurfaceScattering`, `ShaderValueNode`]

Now the shader node copies the uninitialized `stack_index` for the
Weight socket before the value node allocates a `stack_index`, and so
the shader reads a different stack value from the one the value node
actually contains.

When a node has a dynamic declaration the approach to making Weight
sockets available does not work any more.
The`BKE_ntree_update_without_main` call at the end of
`ntree_shader_weight_tree_invert` includes checks for outdated node
declarations. Since the `SOCK_UNAVAIL` flag has been manually toggled
for Weight sockets it does not match the dynamic node declaration any
more and an update of the shader node is triggered, which resets the
flag and makes the socket unavailable again.

Solution is to make all shader nodes context-dependent and make the
"Weight" sockets available for internal GPU shader trees. The gpu
"localized" tree gets a dedicated flag `NTREE_IS_GPU_SHADER_INTERNAL` to
identify this case in the node declaration build functions. Making
Weight sockets available explicitly is no longer necessary.

Compositor modifier/effect inputs always need to be linear colorspace,
floating point. When the inputs are not that, they were converted on
the CPU previously. Now, when compositor is set to use the GPU,

suitable for plotting waveform/parade/vectorscope scopes.

The raason to use a custom scope space rather than plotting in the display
space is that HDR PQ and HLG display space allocate a lot of space to HDR
values, wasting space in the plots. Instead we allocate 75% to SDR and
25% to HDR values.

Additionally it means we avoid having to insert arbitrary OCIO transforms
into scope plotting shaders, which is tricky.

For SDR displays the mapping is sRGB and the gamut of the display, which is
equal to the display space for sRGB and Display P3. For HDR display it's the
same for SDR values and for HDR values it's a log function that goes up to
10K nits, with C1 contuinity to the sRGB curve.

subject: Deps: Fix rubberband failing to compile due missing cstdlib include
message:
Deps: Fix rubberband failing to compile due missing cstdlib include

Currently, trying to build rubberband on macOS using the latest Xcode
toolchain (26.4) leads to the following error:

```
In file included from ../external_rubberband/src/common/mathmisc.cpp:24:
../external_rubberband/src/common/mathmisc.h:58:1: error: unknown type name 'size_t'; did you mean 'std::size_t'?
   58 | size_t roundUp(size_t value); // to nearest power of two
      | ^~~~~~
      | std::size_t
/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include/c++/v1/__cstddef/size_t.h:20:7: note: 'std::size_t' declared here
   20 | using size_t = decltype(sizeof(int));
      |       ^
<more size_t related errors...>
```

The issue seems to be caused by changes in implicit include behavior in
the latest version of the LLVM standard library, with this PR[^1] opened
on the rubberbang Github mirror referring to libcxx 21, which also
matches the version Xcode was upgraded to in its latest 26.4 release[^2]

Fixed by explicitely including the `<cstdlib>` include in the affected
mathmisc.h file. While this issue was encountered on macOS, it most
probably affects all platforms buildling with LLVM 21+, and thus no
guards were applied for it to affect all platforms.

As this is just a simple standard include fix, this should induce nor
require any library rebuilds.

[^1]: https://github.com/breakfastquay/rubberband/pull/126
[^2]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcode#Toolchain_versions

subject: EEVEE: HandleRange support
message:
EEVEE: HandleRange support

Instancing optimizations support for EEVEE.
Part of #130291.

Instancing-heavy scenes (CPU bottlenecked) are twice as fast:
````
100k GN instances

5.0:
OpenGL ~11 FPS
Vulkan ~8 FPS

PR:
OpenGL ~22 FPS
Vulkan ~16 FPS
````

Unlike Workbench and Overlay, some EEVEE modules require per-instance
logic/tracking (Velocity, Shadows), and some render pipelines require
per-instance subpasses (Forward Transparency, Volumes).
This means EEVEE cannot always treat instances purely as batched draws.

Solving this requires changing some of the current assumptions in the
EEVEE sync logic.

### Per-Instance Data

Previously, sync functions parameters used a mix of:
* `Object`
* `ObjectRef`
* `ObjectKey`
* `ObjectHandle`

However, with HandleRanges, the sync code needs to retrieve:
  * instance count
  * per-instance `object_to_world`
  * per-instance `ObjectKey`
  * per-instance `ResourceHandle`
  * per-instance `recalc_flags` (Ideally, not yet implemented)

Since all of these require the `ObjectRef` data to be computed, and we
should reduce the use of raw `Object*` as much as possible (#144811),
this PR refactors function signatures to always use
`const ObjectRef&`/`const ObjectHandle&`.

`ObjectRef` has new functions to retrieve per-instance data, and a new
`sub_key_` property to signal when it's meant to reference the particle
systems of an `Object`.
`ObjectKey`s now takes the sub_key value directly from the `ObjectRef`
and takes an `instance_index` parameter.
`ObjectHandle` is an `ObjectRef` subclass that also includes the recalc
flags (which are computed inside `EEVEE`), and a single
`ResourceHandleRange`, so downstream code can always retrieve the
correct handle regardless of its type (regular, sculpt, or partsys).

`ObjectHandle` is only used for objects with `ResourceHandleRange`s,
objects that don't need it.
(for example, `Light`s still use `ObjectRef`)

`ResourceHandleRange` now allows retrieving the subhandle from a single
instance.

### Per-Instance Subpasses

EEVEE uses the result of `material_get` / `material_array_get` to
retrieve the subpasses it has to draw into.
However, with `ResourceHandleRange`s, a single subpass per
`MaterialPass` may not be enough, since some pipelines require one
subpass per instance.

So the `MaterialPass` types that need a single draw call per instance
now always have a null subpass.
Creating the subpasses by calling the appropriate pipelines is now
handled by the `SyncModule`.
The `SyncModule` has been refactored to take this into account, and
cleaned up to avoid code duplication.

subject: VSE: Expose compositor node group inputs to strip modifier UI
message:
VSE: Expose compositor node group inputs to strip modifier UI

This PR allows the VSE compositor modifier to expose the compositor node
group inputs in its modifier panel. Effectively, this allows users to
control the inputs of a node tree setup without having to open the node
group.

Here's a high level rundown for how this works:
* In `NodeTreeMainUpdater` we create a runtime RNA interface
  (Struct RNA) based on the node group interface (inputs, outputs,
  panels). This happens anytime the node tree interface changes.
* This generated SRNA (`GeneratedTreeSrnaData`) is owned by the node
  group runtime data.
* In `seq::compositor_nodes_update_interface` we create and sync the
  RNA data with the
  `system_properties` ID properties that are stored per strip modifier.
  Note that `IDProperty` is just legacy term for a system that allows
  storing more or less arbitrary data to DNA.
* When executing the compositor modifier, we read the input values from
  the RNA properties on the strip modifier and pass the values on to the
  compositor.

Note: `SOCK_MATRIX` is supported in the compositor, but there isn't a UI
widget for this types yet, so its sockets are hidden for now.

The first color socket (`Image`) is always hidden from the UI and
populated with the strips image data.
The second color socket (`Mask`) is hidden from the UI if the mask
property on the modifier is in use.
Otherwise it is treated as a regular color input.

The test `mod_comp_chain_nested` was using an unpopulated mask input so
the reference image for this test got updated.

Fix #157183: Crash if Group Output has unused output connected

The compositor crashes if the Group Output node has something connected
to an input that is not actually used. This is because node group
operations skip scheduling nodes connected to unneeded inputs, but code
in the operation still assumes all connected inputs will have an
operation that provides its result.

unneeded and connect a dummy input to them, taking care to update
reference counts as needed.

subject: Build: Set ARMV8.2-A as minimum architecture for Linux ARM64
message:
Build: Set ARMV8.2-A as minimum architecture for Linux ARM64

Both for precompiled libraries and Blender itself if nothing else
overrides it. This should cover consumer devices that can realistically
run Blender on the GPU. Dot product and half float are also included as
these are useful and should be widely supported too.

The -march=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16+lse flag is set in the same way as we set
-march=x86-64-v2, with some refactoring to make that function generic.

Previously Linux ARM64 precompiled libraries for OpenImageDenoise used
SVE instructions because they were compiled on DGX Spark and ISPC uses
something akin to -march=native by default. But SVE is not available on
Apple Silicon.

For everything else it was using the GCC default which is ARMv8.0-A. The
choice of ARMV8.2-A and extensions is still conservative, and includes:

subject: Refactor: Adjust paint stroke cleanup methods
message:
Refactor: Adjust paint stroke cleanup methods

Prior to this patch, we had three methods related to cleanup at the end
of a stroke:

* `stroke_done`: A private method called during modal invocation when
  the stroke would finish.
* `done`: A virtual method, called by `stroke_done` to perform
  mode-specific cleanup.
* `free`: A remnant of the old code that performed generic paint cleanup
  as part of `stroke_done`, also public.

This situation is overly complicated in the case of needing to cancel a
stroke outside of the normal modal invocation, i.e. if certain
prerequisites are not maintained and the stroke needs to be cancelled
prior to starting.

To simplify this situation, this patch makes the following changes:
* `stroke_done` renamed to `done`
* `cancel` & `finish` methods exposed, this simply calls `done` with
  necessary arguments
* `free` call removed entirely, existing code put into `done`
* virtual, mode-specific `done` function is no longer only called if the
  stroke has started.

The end state is that users of the `PaintStroke` class only now have to
call either `finish` or `cancel` if necessary inside an operator
`invoke`.

Fix: Node Editor: memory leak when creating inputs via socket drag/drop

Input nodes can be created by dragging the group sockets and droping
them in the node editor. During the drag a tooltip is created using

This is needed to get accurate compositor updates when frame changes.
This includes the following changes:

- Node evaluation dependencies code now sets the time_dependent member
  based on the existence of nodes that depends on time.

subject: Fix #156810: Restore local scissor clipping for curve and scope widgets
message:
Fix #156810: Restore local scissor clipping for curve and scope widgets

## Root Cause
Commit a28eb4dcea (fixing #139646) removed the global scissor test call
from node_draw.cc. Several UI drawing functions in interface_draw.cc
were implicitly relying on this global state to clip their content to
their widget boundaries.

## Fix
Add local `GPU_scissor_test(true/false)` calls around the draw routines
in each affected widget, consistent with per-widget scissoring. The
scissor region was already being calculated and set correctly in each
function, only the enable/disable calls were missing.

## Affected Functions
- `draw_but_CURVE`
- `draw_but_CURVEPROFILE`

subject: Fix: crash when loading file from within asset library
message:
Fix: crash when loading file from within asset library

Fix a crash that could occur when the asset browser was showing an
asset library, and then you open a blend file inside that asset
library.

The fix is two-fold:

- `get_asset_library_on_disk(path)` first checks whether this
  not-normalized path is already associated with a loaded library. If
  not, it allocates the library object and stores it in a mapping.
  However, the key to that map is the normalized path, and not the
  not-normalized path passed to the function. This inconsistency is
  fixed by normalizing first, and then using the normalized path in
  both places.
- `lib->load_or_reload_catalogs()` was called before the library
  object was registered as 'loaded'. This caused the library to be
  loaded again, after which the map insertion fails (because it was
  done in a way that ensures uniqueness). This is solved by inserting
  into the map first, and then calling
  `lib->load_or_reload_catalogs()`.

subject: Fix #127707: wrong parameters passed to NodeTreeInterfaceSocket.from_socket & init_socket
message:
Fix #127707: wrong parameters passed to NodeTreeInterfaceSocket.from_socket & init_socket

NodeTreeInterfaceSocket.from_socket and init_socket receive wrong values
for the node and socket arguments. When inspecting their values on the
Python side, they are either null or the next node or socket.

This is because RNA_parameter_set_lookup, which is used to set
parameters to call the function via Python, needs to receive arguments
by address, except in a few select cases for PointerRNA and strings, but
we are actually passing those pointers by value.

Later when setting up the Python objects for the call, those pointers
are reinterpreted as void** and dereferenced, which would end up reading
either `Node.next` or `Socket.next`, thus passing null or the next
element if it is not null.

To fix this, pass the pointers by address.

Combining marks (e.g. accents) have a zero advance width and were
previously stacked at the current pen position, which placed them at

- An `r_bounds` output parameter to `BLF_character_to_curves`
  populated from the FreeType glyph metrics scaled to VFont units.
- A `bounds` field on `VChar` to cache the per-glyph box.
- Layout logic in `vfont_to_curve` to center zero-width glyphs over
  the previous base character using these bounds.

message:
Refactor: ImBuf: Clarify cropping ownership, don't change buffers in-place

With implicit sharing, it works much better for such operations to
result in a newly allocated buffer, because ImBuf doesn't know how to
reallocate the buffer data without adding additional complexity. In
practice this can reduce the amount of copying when the input data is
const, which wouldn't be worth optimizing for before this.

This also handles ownership properly, unlike the existing code which
could cause ImBuf to reallocate a buffer it did not own.

The goal is to simplify the future addition of implicit sharing.

subject: Fix #155155: Vertex paint fails when no active color attribute exists
message:
Fix #155155: Vertex paint fails when no active color attribute exists

This PR fix vertex paint not starting when no color attribute exists.

Vertex paint could not start if the mesh had no active color attribute.
If the user deleted the color layer, the operator would fail to start
and the brush cursor would not appear.

This happens because the operator poll required an existing color
attribute, so the code that ensures the attribute (ED_mesh_color_ensure)
was never reached.

The poll was relaxed so vertex paint can start even if the mesh has no
color attribute. During stroke initialization the attribute is ensured
and its metadata is retrieved before initializing the paint stroke.

Now vertex paint starts normally, the brush cursor appears (not the
default cursor), and the first stroke creates the color attribute
automatically.

subject: Grease Pencil: Articulated Dots render (i.e. GPU dot placement)
message:
Grease Pencil: Articulated Dots render (i.e. GPU dot placement)

This is a implementation of [Shen's and Li-Yi's paper](https://github.com/ShenCiao/CialloResearch/tree/main/paper).
An outdated implement can be found at #111652 and
https://devtalk.blender.org/t/add-stamp-brush-and-fix-airbrush/30884
discusses the method.

This algorithm works by drawing the texture of extra dots on each
segment, making the illusion that more dots have been created.
The dots are rendered in reverse order so that when a pixel has full
opacity it will stop calculating.
Because the extra dots only exist on the fragment shader, and each pixel
will only have a few pass of dots, this method can handle what *appears*
to be a **unlimited** number of points without severely slowing down and
with **no extra memory use**.

This implementation has multiple new feature not present in the paper:
- Point are place in `3D` world space instead of `2D` view space.
  This makes it so that points will not change position when the
  camera moves.
- Three different placement modes: `Count`, `Radius` and `Density`.

* `Count`: Place a set number of dots per segment. A value of 1 means
  a single dot is placed per evaluated control point.
* `Density`: Place a set number of points per length unit of stroke.
* `Radius`: Place dots along a segment based on a percentage of the
  radius of the stroke.

The main goal of this work is to allow apparent of strokes to not
depend on point density.

subject: Fix #111039: Texture Paint Backface Culling does not work with symmetry
message:
Fix #111039: Texture Paint Backface Culling does not work with symmetry

Symmetry painting was implemented in e2d60d180ed8

Generally speaking, the whole "pipeline" of projection painting gets
done per symmetry pass (per "view") from a loop that goes over all
`ProjPaintState` in `paint_proj_new_stroke`, so all relevant data for
"clipping" should be updated per pass:
- `project_state_init`
- `project_paint_begin`
- `proj_paint_state_viewport_init`
- `proj_paint_state_screen_coords_init`
- `proj_paint_state_vert_flags_init` (for tagging `PROJ_VERT_CULL` for
Normal Falloff)

So then, there does not seem to be a reason for
`project_paint_prepare_all_faces` to skip the culling/clipping  that is
done there (project_paint_winclip, project_paint_flt_max_cull and the
backface culling) when we have multiple views since these all only
depend on already updated screen coords/data.

Quite a lot of test have been done and they all seem to behave properly
with this PR.

subject: Fix (studio-reported) GeoNode Modifier: Crash when missing linked geonode ID.
message:
Fix (studio-reported) GeoNode Modifier: Crash when missing linked geonode ID.

When the linked geonode ID was missing, runtimeRNA versioning code would
do nothing and keep the existing 'old' GeoNode modifier idproperties
around.

While the initial idea to do this was likely to preserve old data until
conditions where met to version properly later, this is moot: if the
file is not saved, and linked geonode ID become available later again,
versioning will happen without problems. But if file is saved in this
state, it will never get versionned again (since its fileversion would
then be above threashold).

Further more, having these deprecated `settings.properties` in the
geonode modifier was causing some serious issues (e.g. somehow some ID
pointers from these were pointing to evaluated IDs during depsgraph node
building phase...), leading to crashes.

So instead, also nuke these deprecated idproperties without attempting
to version them into the new system, when geononde ID is missing.

Also added warning reports about this data loss:
```
00:16.497  blend.readfile   | WARNING Modifier 'SHD-Normal Transfer' from Object 'GEO-raccoon-tufts' is using a missing linked Geometry Node Group, its settings will be lost (reset to default) if the file is saved in this state.
00:16.497  blend.readfile   | WARNING Modifier 'SHD-Material' from Object 'GEO-raccoon-tufts' is using a missing linked Geometry Node Group, its settings will be lost (reset to default) if the file is saved in this state.
```

subject: Geometry Nodes: Optimize Distribute Points on Faces
message:
Geometry Nodes: Optimize Distribute Points on Faces

This commit splits the initial point generation into multiple phases.
First comes a parallel calculation of the number of points generated
for each triangle. Then those counts are accumulated as `OffsetIndices`
and the output data is allocated. Then the points are created for each
triangle in parallel. This is in contrast to the previous serial loop
that appended points to output vectors as it's created. The position
output vector now has the exact capacity necessary, so its allocation
is reused for the final position attribute.

Overall, on my Ryzen 7950X, this results in a 6.4x performance
improvement in a test case generating 14 million points on 2 million
triangles (797ms to 124ms), and roughly a 3x performance improvement
when generating 13k points - many fewer points per triangle.

The result is somewhat similar to #119002, but the change is more
focused and doesn't attempt to optimize the Poisson Disk mode.

Refactor: ImBuf: Access byte and float buffers with functions

Instead of accessing the float and byte buffer data directly, use
functions that either return mutable or const pointers to the buffer
data. Because we plan to use implicit sharing for these buffers, the
mutable version of the access function has "for_write()" in its name
to indicate that it may perform a copy to create mutable data. This
also clarifies the purpose of the code and uncovered many places that
should use const (most trivial ones I changed in this commit).

Any remaining direct access to the float and byte buffer data is low
level code dealing with ownership of the buffers, is doing something
that looks not const-correct to me, or is otherwise non-standard and
will have to be adjusted when these buffers become implicitly shared.

These access methods are on `ImBuf` instead of the buffers to allow
improvements to the semantics of when buffers are available and
potential caching in the future.

subject: Fix #151154: rotation floating point errors with 90-degree rotations
message:
Fix #151154: rotation floating point errors with 90-degree rotations

Detect exact 90-degree multiples from numeric input or snap increments
and use exact sin/cos values (0, 1, -1) instead of computing them from
imprecise radian angles.

The approach avoids epsilon-based angle snapping by detecting quadrants
at the input source:

- Numeric input: track the pre-unit-scale value (val_no_units) on
  NumInput and check if it's an integer multiple of 90 degrees.
- Snap increment: recover the integer step count and degree increment
  to determine the exact degree value via integer arithmetic.

Add a `NUM_INT_INPUT_VALUE` flag, and val_no_units field to NumInput.
Pass an optional quadrant through the rotation matrix computation chain.

Ref !155749

subject: WM: Add unique identifiers to reports, and expose them to Python API
message:
WM: Add unique identifiers to reports, and expose them to Python API

Add monotonically increasing UIDs to Report entries and expose the
reports collection to Python via RNA. This enables extensions to track
individual reports by `session_uid` for analytics and statistics tooling.

Changes:
  - Add `session_uid` (int, atomic session-wide counter) to Report struct.
  - Assign `session_uid` in `BKE_report()` and `BKE_reportf()`.
  - Expose `WindowManager::reports` collection with read-only RNA
    properties (`session_uid`, `type`, `message`).

Notes:
  - Reports are runtime only, they are not saved in blendfiles, so no
    versioning is needed.
  - UIDs count up from 1 and survive report clearing, within a session.
  - Counter is a function-local `static std::atomic<int>`, safe across
    threads.

Python call example:
```python
for r in bpy.context.window_manager.reports:
    print(f"session_uid={r.session_uid}, type={r.type}, message={r.message}")
```

subject: Refactor: Functions: update field storage and API
message:
Refactor: Functions: update field storage and API

This reimplements the entire field API. Large parts of the API surface is the
same, but how a field is stored has change significantly.

The main motivating goals for this refactor were:
* Support storing single value fields without doing an allocation.
* Support referencing common fields without doing reference counting (e.g. the
  position field).

On top of these goals, a few other improvements were done:
* Field types are not nullable anymore. So one needs to use `std::optional` in
  such cases. This also implies that `GField` can't be default-constructed
  anymore because then it wouldn't have a type.
* Field comparisons are shallow now. Previously one could easily do a deep
  comparison of nested field inputs.
* `GField` now stores a `std::variant` to support different internal storage
  types, making it more easily extensible.

In my test file that is adapted from #156308 I get a speedup from 60ms to 54ms
of the modifier evaluation time.

subject: Fix #156748: Geometry Nodes modifiers lose pointer property on save/reload
message:
Fix #156748: Geometry Nodes modifiers lose pointer property on save/reload

**Bug:**
Commit `1561c1ea4a` introduced a regression where object pointers in
Geometry Nodes modifiers are lost upon reloading a `.blend` file. This was
caused by a double-walk during the `lib_link` phase.

`system_properties` was correctly added to the base ID walk in
`BKE_modifiers_foreach_ID_link` (`modifier.cc`). However, an identical
`IDP_foreach_property` walk was concurrently added to the specific
`foreach_ID_link` callback in `MOD_nodes.cc`. Walking an ID pointer twice means
the second pass receives an already-resolved memory address instead of a file
address, which fails the lookup map and nullifies the pointer.

**Fix:**
Removed the redundant `IDP_foreach_property` walk for
`nmd->modifier.system_properties` in `MOD_nodes.cc`.

Tested with the provided file in the issue to confirm the pointer now correctly
survives a save and reload.

subject: Rework memfile undo & pointer stability interactions.
message:
Rework memfile undo & pointer stability interactions.

Generating stable addresses for all pointers when writing memfile undo
steps is not a practical option, as with certain user cases (many
IDProperties, many heavy actions, etc.), it implies generating millions
of stable addresses, which translates into seconds of lag.

See e.g. #150350 and #151827.

In practice, stable addresses are almost never necessary in undo case
anyway - in fact, they can even have an adverse effect, potentially
preventing to detect an ID as modified because different actual memory
addresses would be remapped to the same stable value between neighbor
undo steps.

So this commit effectively removes stable addresses on undo 'by
default', introducing a dedicated API to tag and generate stable values
for the few cases that actually need it (typically, data dynamically
generated at writefile time, see e.g. the `AttributeStorage` case).

In details:
* The work around for shared data (`BLO_write_shared_tag` and related
  code) is removed, as real address of shared data can be directly used
  now.
* `get_address_id` and related code will never _generate_ stable values
  anymore, but only do a default lookup in the `pointer_map`, and return
  the real address if no entry is found.
* A new API, `BLO_write_stable_for_undo_tag`, is introduced to allow
  tagging pointers that do need stable addresses on undo.
  It uses a very similar approach as the previous
  `BLO_write_shared_tag`, generating a stable address id and tagging it
  with a high-significant bit to ensure no collision is possible with a
  real memory address.
* Stable ids mapping is cleared after each ID writing, to allow for
  `BLO_write_stable_for_undo_tag` to assert that given pointer has not
  been handled before (since private ID data dynamically generated at
  write time can re-use same addresses as in a previous ID).

The only data currently using the new `BLO_write_stable_for_undo_tag`
system (and therefore getting stable addresses) are the 'DNA attributes'
generated on write in the `AttributeStorage` containers of Meshes,
GreasePencils, (modern) Curves and PointClouds. We may need to add more
in the future though.

Regarding performances:
| Report | Blender 4.5 | main | PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #151827 | 0.85s | 1.15s | 0.95s |
| #150350 | 0.025s | 0.6s | 0.11s |

-------------

Note that while doing the 'default lookup' for every pointer is already
way more efficient than actually generating stable address ids for them,
it is still a significant overhead (extra memcopy of the written data +
iteration over all pointers + default lookup).

Depending on how much slower this PR remains compared to 4.5, we may
have to also add a dedicated API to write data without any remapping
(with some debug asserts in it to ensure no written pointers are in the
stable address map then).

This should be handled in a separate PR in any case, and would be best
if it was not necessary, as it would add additional complexity to the
code, and probably some uncertainty regarding which data is effectively
safe to fully skip stable address remapping.

subject: Assets: Rework how asset libraries access their Preferences definition
message:
Assets: Rework how asset libraries access their Preferences definition

Each asset library instance somehow has to be mapped to its custom asset
library definition in the Preferences, so it can query
Preferences-dependent info via the library, and changes in the
Preferences are reflected immediately. So far the mapping was kept
loose, by looking up the Preferences library definition on relevant
queries. This can break when changing names or paths.

Another issue is that the import method and relative path options in the
Preferences would only have an impact after reloading the asset library.

Now, simply store a pointer to the Preferences library definition in the
asset library, and get properties from there directly. The reason we
didn't do that so far is that these pointers could dangle when an asset
library is removed. However, we can avoid that, by ensuring the pointer
is still valid on every access. This should be a lot more reliable.

others, which are also not consistent with CPU since it does the correct
conversion. This is because GPUMaterial code generator is only aware
about raw data types, not what they represent. For instance, it assumes
all float4 types are colors, while they could be a generic 4D vector.

socket types. This means that we have to introduce GPU node variants for
each of the conversions, but once GPUMaterial support all necessary data
types, those will be deduplicated.

subject: Cycles: Use implicit sharing to avoid copying some attributes
message:
Cycles: Use implicit sharing to avoid copying some attributes

This commit extends Cycles to allow using Attribute array implicit
sharing info from Blender. This is used to avoid a copy of the evaluated
attribute arrays before they're added to the final buffer for their type.
We can only do this when the attribute type layout match between Blender
and Cycles, which means float and float2 attributes can skip the copy on
the point or curve domain, and also the face corner and face domains in
the adaptive subdivision case.

The buffer stored in attributes is now a raw pointer rather than a
std::vector. As a side effect, resizing the attribute no longer
zero-initializes new values. That was wasted work in practice anyway.

Unfortunately float color and float4 attributes are not covered here
because Blender does not allocate these types with the necessary
alignment. That can be addressed later; I've started it here: !156035.

Besides that, there are some other next steps:
- Use implicit sharing to avoid copying data that Cycles doesn't process
  as attributes, like topology arrays for adaptive subdivision (and
  maybe investigate removing padding so that float3 can be shared too).
- Add some sort of global cache to avoid creating multiple Cycles arrays
  for attributes that aren't layout compatible or are on non-matching
  domains.
- Add some way to delay the attribute type conversion and flattening
  until constructing the final arrays, to benefit non-layout-compatible
  types.
- Looking much further into the future, completely avoid the "large
  buffer per data type" system that Cycles uses to hold geometry data
  (just mentioning this because "completely avoid all copies of Blender
  data" is an interesting prospect).

subject: Geometry Nodes: Runtime RNA for node tree interface
message:
Geometry Nodes: Runtime RNA for node tree interface

This PR implements the changes described in #132129. The main goal is to
use actual RNA types to store node group inputs on the Geometry Nodes
modifier and node tools, rather than using custom properties. This makes
the API much friendlier, as well as resolving long-standing technical
debt.

The API change looks like this:
```python
# Before
modifier["identifier"] = 5.0
modifier["identifier_use_attribute"] = True
modifier["identifier_attribute_name"] = "some_input_attribute"
modifier["identifier_attribute_name"] = "some_output_attribute"
# After
modifier.inputs.identifier.value = 5.0
modifier.inputs.identifier.type = "ATTRIBUTE"
modifier.inputs.identifier.attribute_name = "some_input_attribute"
modifier.outputs.identifier.attribute_name = "some_output_attribute"
```

The `identifier` is the identifier of the interface socket (e.g.
`Socket_2` currently). This PR does not allow changing this property
name, that can be done as separately later.

Another benefit of this change is that combined with the work from
#148763, now the node tool inputs are remembered between invocations
like properties from any other operator. To get node tool registration
working, we have to include all the information necessary for the RNA
property registration in the asset meta-data.

Backward and forward compatibility are supported (though animation paths
are only backward compatible), but this does break the current Python API
for accessing Geometry Nodes modifier properties.

Assets: Make remote library listing work with custom properties

The remote library listing already included custom properties. However,
the format they used didn't match what the C++ indexer expected at all.
This means the custom properties would essentially get lost. Sometimes
they contain important information though, for example, the type of node
tree so the compositor asset shelf can display only compositing assets.

The C++ indexer expected the same format as for the local asset index.
This avoids duplicating the reading code. This commit makes the listing
match that.

Another issue is, that a top level custom property should always be a
group property (this is the one iterated within when doing
`bpy.types.AssetData.items(), like the listing generator does).
Otherwise adding more properties isn't supported, and property lookups
assumed this. We can handle that by letting the indexer create the top
level group if needed, that way it can be implicit in the remote library
listing.

subject: Cycles: Add fundamental support for upscaling denoisers
message:
Cycles: Add fundamental support for upscaling denoisers

Adds basic infrastructure for denoisers that can also upscale for
viewport rendering, by taking advantage of the existing resolution
divider functionality.

The implementation basically tracks two resolution dividers, the normal
one and an additional one that also has a denoiser upscale factor
applied. It then uses the latter one for rendering and processing on
noisy render buffers, and the former one for any processing happening
after denoising. This has the advantage of allowing an additional
resolution divider on top of denoiser upscaling (so can also set the
pixel size to something other than 1x and that is still being
respected). The resolution divider was made into a floating point value
to allow fractional scale factors.
